clue.co-licenseplate-desc: In South America, yellow license plates are almost unique to Colombia.
clue.br-language: Brazil is the only South American country that uses the Portuguese language. It uses letter “Ç”, something Spanish does not.
clue.br-soil: The color of the soil can help you guess! This iron rich, red soil is primarily found in Brazil.
clue.br-states: Finding state abbreviations is common in Brazil. PR stands for Paraná. The abbreviations can be seen on the map when zoomed out.
clue.ca-bilingual: Some countries like Canada are bi-lingual, meaning they have multiple official languages. In Canada you can find both English and French.
clue.ca-maximum: Speed signs in Canada say ‘Maximum’. This word works in both English and French.
clue.co-language: Colombia uses Spanish, as does most other countries in South America.
clue.co-licenseplates: Looking at license plates can help you find your way in the world. Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow plates.
clue.co-taxi: Taxi cars will often feature useful information such as the name of the city they are driving in.
clue.es-language: Most languages have unique words for ‘street’ or ‘road’. In Spanish you will see Calle (street) a lot!
clue.es-roadsign: The Spanish crosswalk signs have a lot of stripes on it, making it stand out from most of the other European ones.
clue.es-vegetation: Look at the vegetation! You will find more tropical trees such as palm trees as you move closer to the equator.
clue.greece-capital: Learning the capitals of countries is a great tool when trying to make a good guess. You can often find signs pointing towards them.
clue.greece-flags: Flags are usually found in the country they represent. Learning them can be very beneficial to figure out where you are.
clue.greece-language: Most European countries use the latin alphabet. Greece is one of the outliers that uses their own unique set of letters, the Greek alphabet!
clue.jp-drivingside: Check for driving direction. In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.
clue.jp-machine: Some countries have very specific, unique niches. For example does Japan have millions of vending machines, making them a common sight here.
clue.jp-vehicles: Vehicles style differs vastly between countries. In Japan small, boxy cars is very common.
clue.kr-drivingside: Check for driving direction. In South Korea they drive on the right side of the road.
clue.kr-internetdomains: Keep an eye out for internet domains. In South Korea they use .KR at the end of an internet adress.
clue.kr-language: In written Korean you will find a lot of big circles.
clue.mt-achitecture: Take notice of the surrounding architecture and building materials. You will see a lot of walls and building made from limestone in Malta for example.
clue.mt-drivingside: Don’t lose track of which side the cars are driving on. Malta is one of the few European countries that drive on the left.
clue.mt-language: Learning the words for street and road in different languages can be really helpful. Triq is the Maltese word and it will only show up in Malta.
clue.mx-drivingside: In Mexico they drive on the right side of the road. As do all other non-island countries in North America.
clue.mx-infrastructure: Utility poles will be different country to country. They come in many different colors, shapes and materials. Mexico usually have octagonal poles made of concrete.
clue.mx-taxi: Taxi cars can often feature useful information, such as the name of the city they are driving in. CDMX is an abbreviation of the Mexican capital Ciudad De Mexico.
clue.nl-landscape: Landscape can be a great clue to figure out where you are. The Netherlands is very flat for example.
clue.nl-licenseplate: License plates on vehicles differ from country to country. In the Netherlands they are yellow, a quite rare sight!
clue.nl-sun: You can tell what hemisphere you are in by looking at the sun. A sun to the South usually means you are on the Northern half of the globe.
clue.rs-language-duo: Serbian can be written in both Cyrillic or Latin letters. You can often find both written on signs here.
clue.rs-language-letters: There are many different languages using the Cyrillic alphabet. Most of them have a few unique letters. The Serbian language is the only to feature the'Ђ' letter.
clue.rs-poles: Utility poles will be different country to country. They come in many different colors, shapes and materials. Serbia will usually have round poles made of concrete.
clue.swe-bollards: Bollards (small road side poles) usually differs between countries. Learning details like this can make you a great guesser.
clue.swe-language: Use language to your strength. Most languages have unique or prominent letters. The Swedish language uses the letters “Å, Ä and Ö” for example.
clue.swe-licenseplate: Most countries in Europe use similar license plates with a blue strip to the left. Sweden included.
clue.th-drivingside: In Thailand they drive on the left side of the road.
clue.th-language: In the written Thai language there is a lot of small circles on the letters.
clue.th-stopsign: Stop signs differ between countries. In Thailand the stop signs are written in Thai.
clue.se-language-title: Swedish uses Å, Ä and Ö
clue.dc-au-ausbollard: Australian bollards are white with a vertical red stripe towards the top.
clue.dc-au-drivingside: In Australia they drive on the left side of the road.
clue.dc-au-yellowpoles: In the state of Western Australia you can find yellow sign posts.
clue.dc-br-language: Brazil is the only South American country that uses the Portuguese language. It has the letter “Ç”, something Spanish does not.
clue.dc-br-redsoil: This iron rich, red soil is primarily found in Brazil.
clue.dc-br-states: Finding state abbreviations is common in Brazil. The abbreviations can be seen on the map on certain zoom levels.
clue.dc-ca-speedsign: Speed signs in Canada say ‘Maximum’. This word works in both English and French, the official languages of Canada.
clue.dc-ch-lowcam: In Switzerland the images were captured with a lower mounted camera. This brings us closer to the ground and makes the country feel different from most other.
clue.dc-ch-plates: License plates in Switzerland do not feature the blue european strip on the left. Instead the red country emblem can be seen.
clue.dc-co-taxiinfo: Taxi cars will often feature useful information such as the name of the city they are driving in.
clue.dc-co-yellowplate: Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow license plates for personal vehicles.
clue.dc-fr-bollard: The bollards in France are round with a pointy top. They have red or gray reflector that wraps all way around. They are reminiscent of small lighthouses.
clue.dc-gh-ghanatape: One of the most (in)famous hints in Geoguessr is the tape on the top-right bar that can be seen when looking down. It can only be found in Ghana.
clue.dc-gh-taxiplates: On taxi cars in Ghana you can see the panels around the tires being painted orange.
clue.dc-id-kabupaten: Indonesia is divided into hundreds of regencies know as Kabupaten (Kab. for short). This term is unique to Indonesia.
clue.dc-id-rupiah: The currency in Indonesia is Rupiah. It is displayed as RP.
clue.dc-it-doublestrip: The Italian license plates will have a blue strip on both sides. The front plates are also shorter than usual.
clue.dc-it-signs: Directional signs in Italy tend to be bright blue with a white capitalised text.
clue.dc-jo-taxi: In Amman, the capital of Jordan, you will find taxis in a distinct yellow-and-green palette.
clue.dc-jp-drivingside: In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.
clue.dc-jp-smallcars: In Japan small, boxy cars are very common. They are called Kei cars.
clue.dc-jp-vendingmachine: Japan has millions of vending machines, making them a common sight here.
clue.dc-kr-circles: In written Korean you will find a lot of big circles.
clue.dc-kr-drivingside: In South Korea they drive on the right side of the road.
clue.dc-lk-amongus: The written Sri Lankan language Sinhala have letters that are very round. Some letter makes it look like there are small doodle characters among us.
clue.dc-lk-drivingside: In Sri Lanka they drive on the left side of the road.
clue.dc-mn-barren: The Mongolian landscape is often barren, featuring large open areas without much vegetation.
clue.dc-mn-bollard: The Mongolian bollard is reminiscent of a bowling pin.
clue.dc-mt-drivingside: Malta is one of the few European countries that drive on the left.
clue.dc-mt-limestone: You will see a lot of walls and buildings made from limestone in Malta.
clue.dc-mt-triq: Triq is the Maltese word for street and it will only show up in Malta.
clue.dc-mx-pinktaxi: Taxi cars in the Mexican capital are white and pink. They also feature the text CDMX, an abbreviation of Ciudad De Mexico.
clue.dc-mx-poles: Mexico usually has octagonal utility poles made of concrete.
clue.dc-nl-flat: The Netherlands is a very flat country. You won't find many hills here.
clue.dc-nl-yellowplate: In the Netherlands license plates are yellow, quite a rare sight in Europe.
clue.dc-pe-blackwhite: Many signposts in Peru are square-shaped and painted in alternating black and white.
clue.dc-pe-conkcreet: Metal signs in Peru are standing on visible concrete plinths.
clue.dc-pe-tuktuk: Tuk Tuks are a common sight in Peru. They are usually referred to as mototaxi.
clue.dc-ph-boxes: In the Philippines city abbreviations can often be found on boxes mounted on utility poles.
clue.dc-ph-conkcreet: Roads in the Philippines are often made of big concrete blocks.
clue.dc-ph-drivingside: They drive on the right side of the road in the Philippines.
clue.dc-pl-crossing: Pedestrian crossing signs in Poland only features a horizontal line. No "zebra stripes" here.
clue.dc-pl-greensign: Polish road signs often come in a distinct green color with a white text.
clue.dc-pl-holypole: The utility poles in Poland are often thin and features a lot of holes. These holes usually don't go all the way down.
clue.dc-rs-duo: Serbian can be written in both Cyrillic or Latin letters. You can often find both written on signs here.
clue.dc-sn-blueplates: Senegal uses blue license plates, the only country in Africa to do so.
clue.dc-sn-drivingside: In Senegal they drive on the right side of the road.
clue.dc-th-circles: In the written Thai language there is a lot of small circles on the letters.
clue.dc-th-drivingside: In Thailand they drive on the left side of the road.
clue.dc-th-stop: In Thailand the stop signs are written in Thai.
clue.no_plates_01: In Norway, commercial license plates are green, and are often seen on vans.
clue.tn-djerba-palms: The island of Djerba is known for its many palm trees, which can be seen all across the island.
clue.ca-checkered-signs: In Canada, T-intersection signs are diamond-shaped and have a distinctive checkered pattern.
clue.pt-chimneys: In southern Portugal, you will often see small chimneys that are either square or round in shape.
clue.br-ladder-poles: The poles you often see in Brazil have a ladder-like design at the base. They have horizontal sections near the bottom.
clue.kh-poles: In Cambodia, you will typically see either concrete ladder poles with rectangular sections or round poles with small holes.
clue.ar-red-soil: In Argentina, red soil is mainly found in the northeastern region, particularly in the panhandle.
clue.us-heb: H-E-B is a supermarket chain that operates exclusively in Texas.
clue.ru-kaliningrad-trees: In Russia, roads lined with trees are common in the Kaliningrad region.
clue.es-chevrons: In Spain, you can find both black and white chevrons and blue and white chevrons.
clue.mk-road-signs: In North Macedonia, road signs are yellow and black, and town names appear in both Latin and Cyrillic alphabets.
clue.mk-bollard-1: One type of bollard in North Macedonia has a trapezoid shape, colored white and black, with a red reflective strip.
clue.jo-google-car: In Jordan, the Street View coverage was captured by a black Google car.
clue.jp-yamaguchi-guardrails: Yamaguchi Prefecture in Japan is recognized for its distinctive bright yellow roadside guardrails.
clue.ng-northern-clothing: You are more likely to see women wearing hijabs and men dressed in traditional Islamic outfits in the northern regions of Nigeria.
clue.be-orange-signs: In Belgium, you will often find orange signposts and sign backs.
clue.tr-grainy-roads: Many roads in Turkey have a grainy look from the mix of light and dark local stones used in the asphalt.
clue.ch-framed-signs: In Switzerland, many road signs have a thin metal border that gives them a clean, framed look.
clue.ae-road-lines: In the UAE, outer road lines are yellow, while the center lines can be white or yellow.
clue.kg-license-plates: Licence plates in Kyrgyzstan feature a red strip on the left side.
clue.mo-license-plates: In Macau, cars have black licence plates.
clue.mo-portuguese-signs: Portuguese often appears alongside Chinese on signs in Macau, reflecting its history as a Portuguese colony.
clue.ec-bollards: In Ecuador, bollards are typically either thin and round with two red stripes or flat with two red reflectors.
clue.lu-license-plates: In Luxembourg, cars have yellow license plates with a blue strip on the left side.
clue.id-bali-crowns: In Bali, you can often spot murdha, decorative crown like ornaments placed along the tops of traditional roofs.
clue.in-dry-landscape: Some parts of the northern Himalayan region administered by India are known for dry, high altitude landscapes with very little vegetation.
clue.sn-license-plates: In Senegal, older plates are fully blue, while newer ones have just a blue strip on the left side.
clue.sn-dashed-lines: In Senegal, roads often have long white dashed lines along the sides.
clue.cy-water-tanks: In Cyprus, buildings often have a white, horizontal water tank with a round lid.
clue.pe-poles: In Peru, you can often see concrete utility poles with three horizontal crossarms.
clue.bd-bengali: Bengali is an official language of Bangladesh, and its script has a horizontal line across the top of each word.
clue.lt-poles: In Lithuania, utility poles are usually square concrete posts with a diagonal support beam.
clue.mx-electricity-counters: Mexico, along with several Central American countries, uses circular electricity meters.
clue.pl-warning-signs: Poland's warning signs are triangular with a yellow background and a thin red border.
clue.za-chevrons: South Africa uses red and white chevron signs, and small, thin chevrons with a single arrow are common across Southern African countries.
clue.kr-jeju-walls: Jeju Island in South Korea is known for its many rock walls made from dark volcanic stone.
clue.de-green-sticker: In Germany, most cars have a green circular sticker on the bottom right of the windshield.
clue.se-short-lines: In Sweden, the outer road lines often have short, white dashed markings.
clue.ug-google-car: Street View in Kampala has a white Google car with rectangular side mirrors.
clue.nl-brick-roads: Brick roads are common throughout the Netherlands.
clue.bo-curvy-poles: In eastern Bolivia, many wooden utility poles are noticeably curvy.
clue.gr-faded-lines: You will often see worn double white center lines in Greece.
clue.co-colombian-cross: In Colombia, signposts have white backs that form a cross shape, known as the Colombian Cross.
clue.uy-signposts: You will often find thick and white wooden signposts in Uruguay.
clue.uy-triple-road-lines: In Uruguay, you can find triple road markings, double yellow lines with a white dashed line running between them.
clue.nz-give-way: In New Zealand, Give Way signs feature red text and a small white outline.
clue.at-vienna-signs: In Vienna, street signs appear as dark blue plaques, with the first number indicating the district.
clue.at-red-white-tape: In Vienna and some smaller Austrian cities, signposts have red and white tape, resembling the Austrian flag.
clue.fi-license-plates: In Finland, license plates are slightly shorter than in most other European countries, and they include the standard EU blue strip on the left.
clue.vn-language: The Vietnamese language is written in a modified Latin script that features an extensive system of diacritical marks.
clue.ro-holey-poles: In Romania, you will frequently come across so called holey poles, with holes running all the way down to the ground.
clue.rw-license-plates: Rwanda has long license plates, with white plates on the front and yellow plates on the back.
clue.uk-lines-reflectors: Dashed center lines with reflectors set between them are a good road marking clue for the UK.
clue.ad-stone-buildings: Stone buildings are common all across Andorra.
clue.ar-license-plates-black: Argentina uses two styles of license plates. One type has what appears to be a black dot in the middle.
clue.ar-license-plates-blue: Argentina uses two styles of license plates. One type has got a blue strip across the top.
clue.pt-azores-rock: Across the Azores, you will often see dry stone walls crafted from dark volcanic rock.
clue.tr-stop: In Turkey, stop signs say "DUR", which is unique to the country.
clue.my-black-sticker: In mainland Malaysia, electricity poles often have black stickers on them.
clue.ru-black-socks: In Russia, signposts often have their lower sections painted black.
clue.mn-tent-car: In Mongolia the google car is often visible. It takes many shapes but usually a tent can be seen packed on the car.
clue.lk-holey-poles: Sri Lanka commonly uses concrete utility poles with large see through holes in the lower half, often called holey poles
clue.is-pedestrian-signs: In Iceland, you will see pedestrian crossing signs with four stripes at the bottom and a subtle yellow hue.
clue.ke-safaricom: The mobile network Safaricom is exclusive to Kenya, and its branded signage appears in almost every town.
clue.kz-tree-trunks: The bottom of tree trunks in Kazakhstan are often painted white.
clue.pa-taxis: Yellow taxis marked with a horizontal checkered stripe are a common sight in Panama.
clue.hu-utca: Street names in Hungary usually end with the word "utca".
clue.na-road-lines: Like many countries in Southern Africa, Namibia uses roads with single yellow outer lines and white center lines.
clue.lb-bad-quality: Lebanon is currently the only Middle Eastern country with official low-quality camera coverage.
clue.cl-white-lines: In Chile, you will usually see all white road lines.
clue.ua-red-car: In Ukraine, you will most often see the back of a red Google car.
clue.bw-signposts: If you're in southern Africa and come across this, you know you're in Botswana.
clue.ng-police-car: A police vehicle, usually white or black, trails the Nigerian Street View car in nearly every coverage. The exact model may differ from images shown.
clue.fr-blue-strips: Small blue rectangular "stickers" on utility poles are a distinctive clue for France.
clue.in-camera-quality: The majority of Indian coverage comes from a notoriously poor camera, recognized by low sharpness and washed-out colors.
clue.gl-tasiilaq: In Tasiilaq, you can usually recognize the coverage by the quad bike with large grey handguards.
clue.ie-yellow-lines: Irish roads often have dashed yellow outlines.
clue.cz-arrow-signs: Directional signs in Czechia taper to a solid filled arrow tip.
clue.cr-stop-signs: In Costa Rica, stop signs show the word "ALTO" instead of "STOP".
clue.ph-jeepneys: In the Philippines it is common to find jeepneys in urban environments. They are often heavily decorated.
clue.bw-license-plates-description: Botswana and Namibia are the only countries in southern Africa where yellow rear plates are the norm.
clue.bw-nature-description: The terrain in Botswana is predominantly flat and arid with scattered small trees. Soil is generally sandy and pale white.
clue.bw-roadnumbers-description: Wayfinding signs use a green background, consistent with the wider southern African convention. Only in Botswana do major roads start with an A.
clue.sz-roadnumbers-description: Roads prefixed with the letters "MR" are found exclusively in Eswatini.
clue.sz-busshelter-description: Distinctive concrete bus shelters appear frequently along Eswatini's roads.
clue.sz-roadline-description: Just like most southern African countries, Eswatini's roads feature yellow outer lines.
clue.gh-license-plates-description: In Ghana private vehicles carry white plates, while commercial vehicles use yellow ones. Both colours are frequently visible.
clue.gh-nature-description: The terrain in Ghana is predominantly flat and lush, with characteristic red laterite soil.
clue.ke-snorkel-description: Kenyan coverage features distinctive vehicles very often equipped with a snorkel.
clue.ke-followcar-description: A grey Toyota SUV can frequently be seen trailing the Street View car in Kenyan coverage.
clue.ke-license-plates-description: Kenyan vehicles carry long white front plates and square yellow rear plates.
clue.ls-mountains-description: Bare, treeless mountains with flat tabletop profiles and prominent horizontal rock ridgelines are Lesotho's signature feature.
clue.ls-architecture-description: Round thatched-roof huts appear frequently in rural Lesotho.
clue.ls-vehicles-description: Lesotho drives on the left, in common with its southern African neighbours.
clue.ls-grass-description: Lesotho's grasslands consist predominantly of short grass, unlike Eswatini which in general has tall grass.
clue.mg-vehicles-description: Much of the Madagascar coverage was captured using different types of transportation, including boats and cow carts.
clue.mg-people-description: The people capturing the Madagascar images can often be seen in them.
clue.mg-baobabs-description: The famous Avenue of the Baobabs is unmistakable thanks to the enormously thick-trunked baobab trees flanking the road.
clue.mg-nature-description: Madagascar's southern and central regions tend to be very arid, while the north is tropical and lush.
clue.na-license-plates-description: Vehicles in Namibia typically carry yellow plates on both front and rear.
clue.na-truck-description: Namibian Street View coverage was captured using a white pickup truck equipped with a short front-mounted antenna that consistently tilts slightly to the left.
clue.na-germanvibes-description: Due to its history as a German colony, Namibia retains visible Germanic influence, particularly in place names and the architectural style of some older buildings.
clue.na-nature-description: Desert-like landscape dominates most of Namibia, although there are a few exceptions to this.
clue.ng-googletruck-description: Most Nigerian coverage shows the Google car, a pickup truck with the cab and bed visible. The cab colour and other features vary.
clue.ng-badcam-description: Nigeria is currently the only mainland African country with official low-quality street view coverage.
clue.rw-brakelight-description: The Google car, a large pickup truck, is fully visible in most Rwandan imagery and distinctively has a visible brake light.
clue.rw-nature-description: Most soil across Rwanda has a noticeable reddish tint.
clue.rw-bikers-description: In Rwanda, all motorcyclists are required to wear red vests and helmets.
clue.st-badcam-description: The entire São Tomé and Príncipe street view coverage was done using official low-quality camera, with a blur completely covering the car.
clue.st-language-description: Portuguese is the primary language of São Tomé and Príncipe and can hence be seen on most signs.
clue.st-yellowtaxi-description: All cabs in São Tomé and Príncipe are yellow.
clue.st-nature-description: São Tomé and Príncipe is located on the equator so you'll find rainforest all over the country.
clue.sn-googletruck-description: In most of the Senegal coverage a silver, white or black truck is visible.
clue.sn-language-description: In Senegal, French is the official language and dominates all visible signage.
clue.za-language-description: South Africa has eleven official languages. While English dominates signage, the Dutch-like language Afrikaans has had a big influence on for example city names.
clue.za-direction-signs-description: South African directional signs are green with yellow road numbers. Road-numbers starting with N or R are exclusive to South Africa.
clue.za-security-description: In South Africa, suburban homes in and around major cities are commonly enclosed behind tall walls, fences, and gates.
clue.ug-capital-description: Almost all Ugandan coverage is in or near the capital Kampala.
clue.ug-license-plates-description: Ugandan vehicles have white front plates and yellow rear plates.
clue.ug-nature-red-description: Soil in Uganda is distinctly red, even paved roads have a redlike tint.
clue.tn-license-plates-description: Tunisian license plates are black with white text. They are the only African country to have that.
clue.tn-language-description: Tunisia is the only street view country combining French and Arabic. Bilingual signage appears frequently, with Arabic identifiable by its lines and dots.
clue.tn-nature-description: Bordering the Mediterranean, the Tunisian landscape is in general dry.
clue.bd-language-description: Bengali, the language in Bangladesh has got a lot of triangular shapes, something similar scripts do not feature.
clue.bd-rickshaw-description: Rickshaws appear constantly throughout Bangladesh, with green motorized auto rickshaws being especially common.
clue.bd-road-description: Ponds, canals, and agricultural plots running alongside the road are a common sight across Bangladesh.
clue.bt-license-plates-description: Bhutanese vehicles carry distinctive red license plates that are easy to spot even from a distance.
clue.bt-road-description: Rows of stone blocks serve as barriers along rural roads, one of the most reliable visual cues for recognising Bhutan.
clue.bt-flags-description: Colorful prayer flags strung alongside roads are a common sight throughout Bhutan.
clue.bt-architecture-description: Traditional Bhutanese buildings have ornately painted wooden window and door frames.
clue.kh-license-plates-description: Cambodian plates are white with blue lettering, though the blue is often hard to see through the blur, making them look white.
clue.kh-language-description: The Khmer writing system has a highly recognisable script, with intricate, curvy letterforms in most fonts.
clue.cx-license-plates-description: Vehicles on the Christmas Island carry yellow license plates.
clue.cx-bollards-description: Bollards on Christmas Island are identical to the Australian ones. White with a red vertical stripe on the front.
clue.cx-crab-description: There are areas on Christmas island with large amounts of crabs. You can also find crab-related traffic signs throughout the island.
clue.cy-license-plates-description: License plates in Cyprus can come in many colors. White and yellow for regular cars and red for rentals.
clue.cy-bollards-description: Cyprus has white, triangular bollards with slanted tops. A small reflector on the front is red and white on the back.
clue.hk-ac-description: Wall-mounted air-conditioning units are a common sight in Hong Kong.
clue.hk-language-description: Signage in Hong Kong routinely pairs English text with traditional Chinese characters.
clue.hk-taxis-description: Taxis in distinct colors are often seen in Hong Kong. There are red, blue and green ones. They have green stickers on the bumpers.
clue.hk-architecture-description: Residential tower blocks in Hong Kong are exceptionally tall, visibly taller than their counterparts in nearby countries.
clue.in-language-description: India has many different languages. If you see written text with a continuous line running along the top of each word, you are in the central or northern parts of the country.
clue.in-english-description: As one of India's official languages, English is widely present on signs and boards across the country.
clue.id-road-signs-description: In Indonesia you can find yellow distance markers tilted towards the road, with a notch cut near the top. They list shorthand names for three destinations.
clue.il-license-plates-description: License plates in Israel are yellow and have a blue strip on the left.
clue.il-stop-signs-description: Israeli stop signs have no text. Instead they depict a raised hand, a common sign for stopping.
clue.il-language-description: The most common text seen in Israel is Hebrew. It looks a bit blocky and has letters with mostly uniform height.
clue.il-small-road-signs-description: In Israel you can find these small sings alongside roads. They come in red, green and blue.
clue.jo-language-description: In Jordan Arabic is the official language, recognisable by its connected script of lines and dots. Commercial signage rarely includes English.
clue.jo-chevron-description: The chevrons in Jordan are white with red arrows.
clue.kz-license-plates-description: Standard Kazakh plates appear mostly white when blurred, with a small blue patch visible on the left side.
clue.kz-truck-description: All Kazakh Street View imagery was captured using a white pickup truck, which may be fully visible or partially blurred out.
clue.kz-crossing-description: Kazakh pedestrian crossings use yellow and white stripes and have white dashes running along either side. Sometimes only the dashes appear without the stripes.
clue.kg-googlecar-description: A silver Google car with four visible bars is used for all coverage in Kyrgyzstan.
clue.kg-winter-description: All Kyrgyz Street View coverage was captured in winter, so expect bare trees, dull-looking terrain, and snow in many places.
clue.kg-bollards-description: Kyrgyzstan uses white bollards featuring a diagonal black stripe near the top.
clue.kg-religion-description: Kyrgyzstan has a majority Muslim population, so mosques are a common sight across the country.
clue.la-language-description: Lao writing is compact and rounded, with diacritical marks above and below characters.
clue.la-goolgecar-description: In Laos the google car is visible with a bars sticking out. In the capital Vientiane the car is however not visible.
clue.la-architecture-description: As a predominantly Buddhist country, Laos is filled with ornately decorated temples, often featuring gold leaf detailing.
clue.la-stop-signs-description: Laotian stop signs display Lao script, sometimes with 'STOP' in Latin underneath. The Lao text uses only two characters.
clue.lb-language-description: Lebanon's official language is Arabic, but French and English signage is widespread.
clue.lb-license-plates-description: Lebanese plates come in long and short formats, each with a blue strip on the left resembling European plates. Taxi plates are deep red.
clue.my-stop-signs-description: Stop signs saying "BERHENTI" are unique to Malaysia.
clue.my-road-lines-description: Two-lane roads often feature double white center lines, Malaysia is the only Southeast Asian country that does this.
clue.my-license-plates-description: Malaysian plates are black with two white sections, easily visible even through blurring.
clue.mn-stop-signs-description: The Mongolian stop signs are written in Mongolian Cyrillic. They are unique to say "ЗОГС".
clue.np-license-plates-description: Nepal uses long plates. The standard versions are white, while private vehicles carry red plates and public transport uses black ones.
clue.np-badcam-description: All imagery in Nepal comes from a notoriously poor camera, recognized by low sharpness and washed-out colors.
clue.np-road-description: Nepali roads frequently have yellow edge markings, either dashed or solid, paired with white dashed center lines on wider routes.
clue.np-bollards-description: Roadside bollards in Nepal are concrete with alternating black and white stripes (between 3 and 5 bands) and typically have a red mark on the cap.
clue.om-license-plates-description: Omani private vehicles carry yellow licence plates, whereas commercial vehicles have red ones.
clue.om-nature-description: Oman is dominated by arid, sparsely vegetated terrain. The central and southern interior is largely flat, while the northern coastline has dry, rugged mountains
clue.om-road-signs-description: Chevrons in Oman are yellow with black arrows and stand out for having an unusually high number of arrow markings.
clue.om-googlgecar-description: All Omani Street View imagery was captured using a white pickup truck. As a result, a large portion of the vehicle or a prominent front blur is typically visible.
clue.ph-language-description: English is one of the official languages in the Philippines and appears on signs frequently.
clue.qa-license-plates-description: Qatari private vehicles carry long white plates with a maroon strip on the left. Trucks have square black plates, and police vehicles use blue plates.
clue.qa-nature-description: Qatar is an almost entirely flat, arid desert with vast sand expanses and very little greenery.
clue.hr-stickers: Oval stickers bearing the letters 'HR' can be sometimes be spotted on Croatian vehicles.
clue.qa-crossing-signs-description: Qatari pedestrian crossing signs depict a man wearing a traditional thobe.
clue.qa-football-description: Coverage taken before the 2022 FIFA World Cup frequently shows promotional banners for the event.
clue.lv-bus-signs: Latvian bus stop signs feature a bus icon with five windows, distinguishing it from the four-window design used in Lithuania and Estonia.
clue.ar-chevrons: Argentina is the only South American country that has white chevrons with red arrows.
clue.ru-license-plates-description: Russian plates are entirely white with black text and lack the blue EU-style strip found on most European plates.
clue.ru-bollardspam-description: Intersections in Russia frequently feature unusually large clusters of bollards, far more densely packed than in most other countries.
clue.ru-asian-vehicles-description: Japanese-made vehicles with the steering wheel on the right become increasingly common the further east you go in Russia.
clue.ru-language-description: Russian uses the Cyrillic alphabet. It is the only script showing up on most signs.
clue.sg-street-signs-description: Singaporean street signs are green with round edges. They have a very distinctive white font.
clue.sg-vehicles-bus-description: In Singapore, most buses are lime-green.
clue.sg-littering-description: Singapore is exceptionally clean and have orderly streets as there are heavy fines for littering.
clue.sg-language-description: English is the common language in Singapore, with exclusive use in numerous public services.
clue.kr-polestripes-description: South Korean utility poles often carry black-and-yellow diagonal stripes near the base. The stripes do not reach the ground.
clue.lk-license-plates-description: Sri Lankan license plates are white in the front and yellow in the rear.
clue.lk-tapered-bollards-description: In Sri Lanka you can find short, tapered stone bollards. They are white with a black base.
clue.tw-language-description: Taiwanese signage uses Traditional Chinese, a complex script with intricate multi-stroke characters.
clue.tw-polestripes-description: In Taiwan, nearly all utility poles carry diagonal black-and-yellow striped markings that most often run all the way down to the ground.
clue.tw-bollards-description: Taiwanese bollards feature two or three circular reflectors on a black rectangle.
clue.tw-noparking-description: Red-painted edge lines indicating no parking appear frequently, especially in urban areas, essentially unique to Taiwan.
clue.th-flags-description: In Thailand, flags are commonly hung along streets. Besides the national flag, yellow royal banners appear frequently.
clue.th-road-signposts-description: Thai sign-mounting posts are thick and square-shaped, typically white, with the lower portion painted black.
clue.th-license-plates-description: In Thailand, passenger vehicles carry large white plates. Commercial vehicles have yellow plates instead.
clue.ae-desert-description: The natural terrain in UAE is predominantly flat and arid, with open desert stretching in every direction.
clue.ae-unpaved-road-description: Despite the country's wealth, it is not unusual to encounter unpaved roads in residential areas.
clue.vn-bollards-description: Small concrete bollards are the most common ones in Vietnam. They have a red top.
clue.vn-pole-box-description: Grey electricity boxes can be seen mounted to utility poles in Vietnam. They are tapered towards the bottom and have a few windows.
clue.uy-bollards-description: Bollards in Uruguay are fully white on the front, and fully yellow on the back,
clue.uy-tridentpole-description: A common variation of the many Uruguayan poles are the so-called trident poles with three insulators all pointing upwards.
clue.co-paintedpole-description: Colombian poles can be found painted with black-yellow-black stripes.
clue.co-fences-description: It is common to find wooden fences in Colombia, often made from various pieces of wood.
clue.bo-license-plates-description: Bolivia uses short plates. They will look white or slightly blue.
clue.bo-bricksonbricks-description: Buildings featuring big exposed red bricks is a common sight in Bolivia.
clue.bo-clothes-description: Bowler hats and large skirts are outfits commonly seen in Bolivia.
clue.cl-yellow-lines-description: Chile can have either fully yellow or fully white lines. The two colors are almost never combined.
clue.cl-bollards-description: Chilean bollards are white with a white reflector on the front, and a yellow on the back. They are overall quite a rare sight.
clue.cl-concrete-pole-description: You will find rectangular, indented concrete poles in Chile. The upper part typically has small pinholes.
clue.ec-ladderpole-description: In Ecuador you can find these poles with a large amount of indents, referred to as ladder poles.
clue.ec-concrete-road-description: It is fairly common to find concrete roads in Ecuador.
clue.nz-bollards-description: Bollards in New Zealand feature a red strip that wraps around the back, extending partially across the front.
clue.nz-triangles-description: Triangles can be found painted on the road at intersections in New Zealand.
clue.au-give-way-description: "Give way" signs in Australia have black text and a white outer border.
clue.ca-metric-description: Canada uses the metric system and thus displays speed in kilometers per hours (km/h).
clue.ca-french-east-description: In Canada, written French will mainly be found in the provinces of Québec and New Brunswick.
clue.cw-road-signs-description: In Curaçao road signs borders can be seen wrapping over to the back. These borders are usually blue or red.
clue.cw-googlecar-description: The Curaçao images were taken by a black car with visible bars, a combination unique to this island.
clue.cw-language-description: Curaçao is part of the Netherlands and uses the Dutch language.
clue.do-stop-signs-description: The Dominican Republic stop signs say 'PARE'. This is unlike most other North American countries.
clue.do-license-plates-description: License plates in the Dominican Republic fade from yellow at the top to white at the bottom.
clue.do-googlecar-description: If you see bars with thick rubber strips when looking down then you are guaranteed to be in the Dominican Republic.
clue.gl-architecture-description: Most residential buildings on Greenland are painted in bright colors, often red, green or blue.
clue.gl-barren-description: The terrain on Greenland is entirely devoid of trees and tall plants. The ground is frequently blanketed in snow.
clue.gl-shore-description: You are bound to spot water in Greenland as almost all settlements are set on the shore.
clue.gt-painted-pole-description: Seeing utility poles painted pink is a common occurrence in Guatemala. Other colors such as green appears as well.
clue.gt-googlecar-description: All vehicle-based coverage in Guatemala uses a grey car whose roof rack and side mirrors are visible through the blur.
clue.gt-license-plates-description: Guatemalan plates are compact. When blurred, they typically show either a blue or green tint.
clue.pa-stop-sign-description: Like most other Spanish speaking countries in North America, stop signs in Panama say ALTO.
clue.br-black-signs: Most road signs in Brazil have black backsides.
clue.sz-tall-grass: Eswatini features stretches of tall grass.
clue.es-road-markers: Distance markers along Spanish roads are recognisable by their colourful borders and the road number printed at the top.
clue.us-mail-boxes: Mailboxes with a small flag are a common sight in North America.
clue.jp-overhead-arrows: This arrow above the road marks the road during heavy snow and is mainly seen in Hokkaido.
clue.bg-bilingual-signs: Road direction signs in Bulgaria are blue, arrow-shaped, and printed in both Cyrillic and Latin script.
clue.pa-license-plates-description: Front plates are not mandatory in Panama so look for the rear ones, which are short, white plates with a turquoise band across the top.
clue.pa-googlecar-description: Panama's Street View car is a large white pickup truck. It is either fully visible or totally hidden, leaving a large blur.
clue.pr-language-description: Signage throughout Puerto Rico is predominantly in Spanish despite being part of the USA.
clue.pr-walmart-description: US retail chains like Walmart are common in Puerto Rico. A useful differentiator from other Latin American territories where such stores are absent.
clue.pr-speed-signs-description: Puerto Rican speed limit signs have the same design as in the US but are written entirely in Spanish.
clue.ca-mailbox-description: Shared mailbox units are a regular sight in Canada.
clue.us-imperial-description: The US uses the imperial system, meaning speed and distances will be displayed in miles.
clue.us-triangular-signs-description: Triangular yellow signs reading 'No Passing Zone' are found only in the US.
clue.us-road-lines-description: US roads have yellow center lines (usually double) and white outer lines.
clue.vi-lhd-description: The Virgin Islands is the only US territory that drives on the left side of the road.
clue.vi-googlecar-description: A white or red truck street view car will be visible while exploring the US Virgin Islands.
clue.vi-license-plates-description: The Virgin Islands uses two types of blue plates. Dark blue and turquoise.
clue.al-bollards-description: Bollards in Albania are white with a black, slanted top. The top features a red reflector on the front and a gray on the back.
clue.al-license-plates-description: License plates in Albania come in two forms. One with a red strip to the left, and one featuring blue strips on each end.
clue.al-rruga-description: The Albanian word for street is rruga.
clue.ad-license-plates-description: License plates in Andorra lacks the blue eu-strip. Instead an orange dot can be found on the left side.
clue.ad-mountains-description: Andorra is located in a mountain range between France and Spain, this leads to mountains being visible at all times.
clue.at-einbahn-description: Signs for one way streets in Austria say 'EINBAHN'.
clue.at-bollards-description: Austrian roadside bollards are white with a black cap, often with a small rounded knob at the very top.
clue.be-bollards-description: The standard Belgian bollard is white and has a yellow rectangular reflector on the front and a white one on the back.
clue.be-license-plates-description: Belgian number plates stand out for their red-colored characters, a tint that remains visible even through blurring.
clue.be-crossing-signs-description: Belgian crossing signs show a figure with a square-shaped head walking over two horizontal dotted lines.
clue.bg-language-description: Bulgaria writes primarily in Cyrillic, though Latin transliterations appear on many signs.
clue.bg-bins-description: It is common to spot these metal waste bins in Bulgaria.
clue.hr-domain-description: The top domain in Croatia is .HR, originating from the local name for the country, Hrvatska.
clue.hr-bollards-description: Croatian bollards feature either red or white reflectors that sit on top of a black section.
clue.hr-license-plates-description: Older license plates in Croatia are fully white. Newer ones feature a blue strip on the left.
clue.cz-bollards-description: The Czech bollards feature two orange reflectors stacked on top of each other on traffic side
clue.cz-doublepole-description: Round concrete utility poles are common in Czechia. They are frequently installed in joined pairs.
clue.cz-number-signs-description: Building numbers in Czechia are displayed on small blue or red signs lined with a thin white border.
clue.mk-license-plates-description: North Macedonian plates are white and can have the blue EU strip. A noticeable red block sits near the left side.
clue.no-fjord-description: Fjords are a common sight along the Norwegian coast.
clue.no-yellow-signs-description: In Norway directional signs are yellow with a thin black outline.
clue.no-white-signs-description: Regulatory traffic signs in Norway feature a red border on a white background.
clue.dk-road-lines-description: All road markings in Denmark are white. Double center lines appear frequently on Danish roads.
clue.dk-bollards-description: The standard Danish bollard is white with a yellow reflector and a prominent dark orange band, a combination exclusive to Denmark.
clue.dk-streetname-description: The suffix 'vej', Danish for 'road', appears at the end of most street names.
clue.dk-framed-signs-description: Danish wayfinding signs are mounted low to the ground inside a distinctive tubular metal frame. They appear in red or blue.
clue.dk-flat-nature-description: The terrain across Denmark is predominantly flat.
clue.ee-license-plates-description: Estonia uses standard EU-plates. White plates with a blue strip on the left.
clue.ee-small-signs-description: Small blue signs with numbers on them can be found in Estonia. They are placed perpendicular to the road.
clue.ee-crossing-signs-description: Estonian pedestrian crossing signs feature three black stripes.
clue.ee-bollards-description: Estonian bollards have a rounded profile. The front carries a rectangular reflector while the back has two circular ones, in either white or orange.
clue.fo-notree-description: The Faroe Islands are virtually devoid of natural tree growth, the vegetation consists almost entirely of grass and low shrubs.
clue.fo-rugged-nature-description: The terrain on Faroe Islands is defined by sweeping fjords bordered by steep, green mountains.
clue.fo-bollards-description: The bollards on Faroe Islands are yellow and quite small.
clue.fi-outer-road-description: Outer road lines on Finnish roads are always continuous solid white lines, never dashed.
clue.fi-snowpole-description: Finland has orange snow poles with a single narrow white band positioned close to the top.
clue.fi-street-names-description: Finnish road names typically end in 'tie' (road) or 'katu' (street).
clue.fi-crossing-signs-description: Finnish pedestrian crossing signs feature five black stripes.
clue.fr-streetname-description: 'Rue' is the standard French word for street and appears on countless signs throughout the country.
clue.fr-ladderpole-description: France have concrete utility poles with a series of step-like indentations. This design is referred to as a 'ladder pole'.
clue.de-bollards-description: German bollards are black-and-white posts fitted with white or pale grey reflectors, switching to orange at intersections.
clue.de-mailbox-description: German mailboxes are yellow and carry the black 'Deutsche Post' horn logo.
clue.de-one-way-signs-description: One-way street signs carrying the full word 'Einbahnstraße' are exclusive to Germany.
clue.de-windturbine-description: Wind turbines are encountered across Germany with considerably greater frequency than in any other European nation.
clue.gi-bigrock-description: A massive limestone mountain towers Gibraltar and is visible from virtually everywhere.
clue.gi-vehicles-description: Despite being a British territory, Gibraltar drives on the right, the opposite of the UK mainland.
clue.gr-license-plates-description: Greek license plates are either fully white or follow the standard EU layout with a blue strip on the left side.
clue.gr-woodpole-description: Most Greek utility poles are made of timber, often seen in a dark brown tone.
clue.gr-bollards-description: Bollards in Greece are white and have a red, square reflector on the front, and a white on the back.
clue.gr-directional-signs-description: Arrow-shaped blue signs carry place names in two scripts: Greek lettering in yellow and a Latin transliteration in white underneath.
clue.hu-holy-pole-description: Hungary has concrete utility poles with narrow rectangular holes that continue all the way to the ground.
clue.hu-language-description: Hungarian is characterized by heavy use of acute accents and notably long words. Keep an eye out for the unique letters Ű and Ő.
clue.hu-bollards-description: Bollards in Hungary are black and white. They have a wedge-like profile and a red reflector on the front, and a white on the back.
clue.is-license-plates-description: Icelandic license plates do not feature the blue EU strip on the left. A yellow dot can sometimes be seen in the middle.
clue.is-bollards-description: Icelandic bollards are yellow and have a single white reflector. They appear on virtually every stretch of rural road across the country.
clue.is-barren-nature-description: Much of the Icelandic countryside is devoid of trees, covered instead by dark grey soil composed largely of volcanic rock.
clue.is-language-description: Written Icelandic can be recognized by a frequent use of accents and unique letters such as ð and þ.
clue.ie-license-plates-description: Irish license plates are white and have the standard EU blue strip on the left.
clue.ie-yield-signs-description: In Ireland the triangular give way signs say 'YIELD'.
clue.ie-language-description: Irish road signs usually carry text in both English and Irish.
clue.it-bollards-description: Bollards in Italy are white with a black top. They have a red reflector on the front and a white on the back.
clue.it-street-name-description: The Italian word for street is 'Via'.
clue.it-road-lines-description: Solid white outer lines without any center lines is a common sight in Italy.
clue.lv-license-plates-description: Latvia have standard white EU plates with a blue strip on the left.
clue.lv-small-signs-description: Small blue signs with numbers on them can be found in Latvia. They are placed parallel to the road.
clue.lv-bollards-description: Latvian bollards are white and feature a vertical reflector on the front and two round ones on the back. The reflectors can be white or orange.
clue.li-valley-description: As Liechtenstein is located in a valley, mountains are always visible, especially to the east.
clue.li-bollards-description: Bollards in Liechtenstein are rounded with a round top. They are black and white and feature a vertical reflector on the front.
clue.li-license-plates-description: Liechtenstein license plates are black with white text with an emblem slightly to the left. It will appear as black or red.
clue.li-lowcam-description: All Liechtenstein imagery is captured with a low-mounted camera.
clue.lt-license-plates-description: Lithuania has standard white EU plates with a blue strip on the left.
clue.lt-small-signs-description: Small blue signs with numbers on them can be found in Lithuania. They are placed in pairs, with a 45 degree angle to the road.
clue.lt-bollards-description: Lithuanian bollards are whites and have a rectangular orange reflector on the front and a white on the back.
clue.lu-architecture-description: Luxembourg houses typically have dark slate roofs and plain, undecorated walls painted white, grey, or in pastel tones.
clue.lu-directional-signs-description: Luxembourg's directional signs are yellow with a thin black outline. They are arrow shaped and often feature a number in a red box .
clue.lu-white-signpost-description: In Luxembourg, nearly all road signs are mounted on white signposts.
clue.xx-general-description: English is one of Malta's official languages and is widely used on signage and storefronts.
clue.mt-small-description: Roads on Malta tend to be only one or two lanes wide due to the island's small size and low population.
clue.mc-rich-description: Monaco is a tiny, but rich country. Buildings look fancy and streets are clean.
clue.mc-urban-description: There are no rural areas in Monaco, everything is urban.
clue.mc-boats-description: Monaco has multiple marinas filled with fancy boats. There is even street view out on the water.
clue.me-nature-description: The landscape in Montenegro is very mountainous. The mountains tend to be lush and covered in green vegetation.
clue.me-license-plates-description: Montenegrin license plates are white and feature a blue strip on the left. They also have red coat of arms close to the center.
clue.me-bollards-description: Montenegrin bollards are white with a red reflector on the front, a white reflector on the back, and a black top.
clue.me-rifts-description: Image artifacts in the sky are common to see in Montenegro. These are referred to as 'Rifts' by the community.
clue.pt-license-plates-description: Portugal have white plates with a blue EU strip on the left and, on most vehicles, a yellow strip on the right, which is unique to Portugal.
clue.pt-streetname-description: The Portuguese word for street is "Rua", visible on nearly every street sign.
clue.pt-hunt-description: Portuguese hunting signs are diamond or rectangular in a red-and-white color scheme.
clue.ro-trees-description: In Romania, trees and utility poles frequently have their lower sections painted white.
clue.ro-waystone-description: Romanian road waystones are very common. They are white and can have red or blue accents. They have the road number on the side.
clue.sm-crosswalk-description: San Marino has crosswalks with big areas painted in blue.
clue.sm-towers-description: San Marino is situated around a mountain with three peaks each with a medieval tower. They are visible from many locations in the country.
clue.sm-license-plates-description: San Marino license plates are compact and white with blue lettering, noticeably shorter than the standard European format.
clue.sm-italian-description: San Marino uses the Italian language and much of its infrastructure is identical to Italy.
clue.rs-bollards-description: Serbian bollards come in several designs, but most share an off-centered reflector.
clue.rs-web-description: The top domain in Serbia is .RS, originating from its full name Republic of Serbia.
clue.sk-bollards-description: Slovak bollards have two orange reflectors on the front and a white reflector on the back.
clue.sk-arrow-signs-description: Slovak direction signs have a blue background and small white arrows.
clue.sk-streetsigns-description: In Slovakia, street name signs are commonly white with blue lettering and a thin red border.
clue.si-nature-description: Slovenia's terrain is generally very hilly and heavily forested, with occasional patches of agriculture.
clue.si-bollards-description: Slovenian bollards are white with a black top. The front reflector is bright red and the back reflector is white.
clue.si-house-signs-description: Slovenian house number plates are typically red with white text.
clue.si-architecture-description: Slovenian buildings are alpine-inspired with light-colored walls and dark wooden details.
clue.es-hunting-description: In Catalonia you can find black and white signs indicating hunting grounds.
clue.es-crossing-signs-description: On the Spanish crossing signs there are eight stripes, the most in all of Europe.
clue.se-overwalkplace-description: Swedish pedestrian signs feature four stripes on the crossing. A variant with a female silhouette also exists.
clue.se-bollards-description: Swedish bollards are black-and-white, usually fitted with a grey reflector. Near intersections, the reflectors are often orange.
clue.se-snowpole-description: Swedish snow poles are typically orange with a tall white reflector positioned slightly above the midpoint.
clue.tr-bollards-description: Turkish bollards are flat, white, and rectangular with a red reflector on the front. A way to remember is to think of their flag which is also red and white.
clue.tr-minaret-description: It is common in Turkey to see minarets.
clue.tr-speciali-description: The written Turkish language has a special 'i', which will have a dot even when capitalized.
clue.ua-license-plates-description: License plates in Ukraine have a strip on the left that is blue and yellow, a representation of their flag.
clue.ua-paintedstuff-description: In Ukraine you may come across various pieces of infrastructure painted blue and yellow, matching the color of their flag.
clue.uk-license-plates-description: In the UK, license plates are yellow in the rear and white on the front.
clue.uk-crossing-signs-description: Pedestrian crossings in the UK do not feature signs, instead there are striped poles with a light at the top.
clue.uk-terraced-description: Two-story, terraced buildings are extremely common in the UK.
clue.qa-bubble-antenna: In Qatar, the Google car usually features an antenna with a small bubble on top.
clue.no-chevrons: In Norway, you can see black and yellow chevrons.
clue.im-oldcam-description: The images on Isle of Man were captured by an older camera, identifiable by lower resolution and a big bottom blur.
clue.im-license-plates-description: License plates on Isle of Man are yellow on the rear and white in the front. They have a red strip to the left.
clue.im-shrubs-description: Gorse shrubs, bushes with vivid yellow flowers, are commonly found on Isle of Man.
clue.je-oldcamera-description: The images on Jersey were captured by an older camera, identifiable by lower resolution and a big bottom blur.
clue.je-license-plates-description: License plates on Jersey are yellow on the rear and white in the front, with a small red emblem to the left. This can be hard to see.
clue.je-language-description: Even though Jersey is part of the UK, French can be seen written on signs and many locations have French names.
clue.je-booths-description: Phone booths on Jersey are painted yellow.
clue.as-nature-description: The vegetation on American Samoa is tropical. All land not used by humans is covered in dense jungle.
clue.as-vehicles-description: On the main American Samoa island, Tutuila, the rear of a rusted black pickup truck is visible.
clue.gu-green-signs-description: Street signs in Guam are green.
clue.gu-reflector-description: Roads on Guam are often studded with an unusually high amount of road reflectors.
clue.gu-pole-description: Utility poles on Guam are almost always made of concrete and tend to be noticeably thick.
clue.mp-pole-description: The Northern Mariana Islands uses wooden utility poles.
clue.mp-road-signs-description: On Northern Mariana Islands street signs are blue.
clue.mp-nature-description: Flame Trees appear on the Northern Mariana Islands. Its wide crown covered in bright red flowers is easy to spot.
clue.pe-red-bricks-description: Red brick buildings are common near Lake Titicaca in Peru and resemble architecture frequently seen in western Bolivia.
clue.dk-general-description: Red brick houses are very common in Denmark. Roofs often have orange, black or brown tiles.
clue.id-west-sumatra: West Sumatra has these unique boat-shaped roofs.
clue.ae-general-description: Houses in residential areas are usually made out of this light-colored stone.
clue.fi-red-houses: Along Sweden and Norway, Finland has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.
clue.se-red-houses-description: In the countryside Sweden, along with Norway and Finland, has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.
clue.tr-snow-poles-description: Turkish snow marker poles are alternating black, orange, and white and fitted with red reflectors.
clue.pl-zabka-description: The convenience store Żabka can be found pretty much everywhere in Poland.
clue.br-phone-numbers: Phone numbers in Brazil often include an area code as a separate two-digit prefix.
clue.id-white-sections: Most Indonesian license plates are black with white letters, often appearing as three white segments through blur.
clue.us-speed-signs: Speed signs in the US say ‘Speed Limit’.
clue.pl-bollards: Polish bollards have a red band around them, with a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back.
clue.ar-double-poles: Double poles with horizontal bars are commonly found in Argentina.
clue.fr-road-numbers: Yellow road signs beginning with “D” are specific to France and are often placed above direction signs or on town entry signs.
clue.us-yield-signs: US yield signs are triangles with a red border and the word “YIELD” on a white background.
clue.jp-pole-marking-description: Japanese poles often have thin, vertical yellow lines on a black section towards the bottom.
clue.jp-bollards-description: Japanese bollards are white and have a circular reflector on the top.
clue.ru-crosswalk-description: Crosswalks in Russia use alternating white and yellow stripes instead of the solid white stripes seen in most other countries.
clue.py-chevron-signs-description: Chevrons in Paraguay are yellow with black arrows.
clue.py-googlecar-description: Coverage in Paraguay has a visible Google car. It appears to be black or silver.
clue.py-road-lines-description: Paraguay tends to have white solid outer lines and a single dashed yellow center line.
clue.py-dark-signs-description: The backs of road signs in Paraguay are usually quite dark.
clue.py-cross-signs-description: In Paraguay some smaller road signs have a design that resembles a cross on their backside.
clue.no-kiwi-description: Kiwi is a store chain that only exists in Norway.
clue.ch-bollards-description: Bollards in Switzerland can either be cylindrical with a round top or have a rounded rectangular shape with a slanted top. Both are black and white with a rectangular reflector on the front.
clue.my-jalan-description: In Malaysia it is common to see the abbreviation JLN for Jalan, the local word for street.
clue.id-jalan-description: In Indonesia, it is common to see the abbreviation JL for Jalan, the local word for street.
clue.mx-bollards: Mexico uses round, white bollards with a black base.
clue.au-road-lines: Australia generally uses all white road lines.
clue.lt-sign-borders: Lithuanian signs have a red border with a thin white outline.
clue.al-highway-shield-description: Alaskan highway shields feature the Big Dipper constellation in the lower-left corner.
clue.al-tree-appearance-description: Alaskan trees tend to be slimmer with narrower foliage.
clue.al-snow-capped-mountain-description: Tall, snowy mountain peaks are visible in much of Alaska.
clue.al-subarctic-tundra-interior-descri: Interior and northern Alaska have sparse undergrowth and short trees.
clue.al-alexander-archipelago-descriptio: Towns in the panhandle's island chain sit among steep, densely forested mountains with mostly wooden buildings.
clue.al-anchorage-suburb-description: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, shopping districts, and visible mountain ranges.
clue.al-aspen-tree-description: Quaking aspens with white bark and round leaves grow at lower elevations in interior and south-central Alaska.
clue.al-agricultural-field-description: Farming in Alaska occurs mainly in the Matanuska Valley and Kenai Peninsula.
clue.al-trans-alaska-pipeline-descriptio: The pipeline is often visible from main roads and is a strong identifier.
clue.as-country-flag-description: The national flag of American Samoa is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ad-autumn-foliage-description: Much of the Andorran coverage was captured in October, so autumn colours on deciduous trees are common.
clue.ad-snow-pole-description: Wooden snow poles in various colours line roads throughout Andorra.
clue.ad-catalan-language-description: Andorra's official language is Catalan, recognisable by 'i' meaning 'and' and words that often end in consonants.
clue.ad-street-name-carrer-description: Street signs in Andorra use the Catalan word 'carrer' for street.
clue.ad-kilometre-marker-cg-cs-descripti: Andorran roads have distance markers labelled with CG or CS route numbers.
clue.ad-yellow-guardrail-reflector-descr: In Andorra, guardrails have yellow reflectors.
clue.ad-bollard-description: Andorran bollards are white with square orange reflectors and appear along main highways.
clue.ad-traffic-cone-description: Traffic cones in Andorra are yellow and turquoise-green.
clue.ad-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Andorran pedestrian crossing signs show a crosswalk with 8 stripes.
clue.ad-country-flag-description: A vertical tricolour of blue, yellow, and red, sometimes with the coat of arms in the centre.
clue.aq-snow-ice-description: The vast majority of Antarctica is blanketed in snow and ice.
clue.aq-dark-soil-description: Wherever bare ground is exposed in Antarctica, it is consistently dark in colour.
clue.aq-penguin-description: Penguins appear in parts of the Antarctic coverage and confirm the southern hemisphere.
clue.aq-ross-island-western-tip-descript: The western tip features very dark, barren rocky ground with almost no snow cover.
clue.aq-ross-island-cabin-description: A small wooden cabin with a grey metal roof south of the island's eastern tip.
clue.aq-mcmurdo-interior-tripod-descript: Tripod footage inside several of McMurdo Station's buildings.
clue.aq-mcmurdo-wooden-hut-description: A small wooden hut on the station's eastern side with interior tripod footage.
clue.aq-mcmurdo-ice-trekker-description: A trekker walks across a frozen surface surrounded by machinery southeast of the station.
clue.aq-mainland-dry-valley-description: A surreal, barren landscape of empty valleys on the mainland west of Ross Island.
clue.aq-south-mcmurdo-black-island-area-: A wide, snowy expanse with scattered low hills south of McMurdo Station.
clue.aq-country-flag-description: The national flag of Antarctica is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ar-wooden-utility-pole-description: Timber poles appear frequently, including unique A-frame variants.
clue.ar-road-line-description: Roads have broken white centre lines, solid double yellow dividers, or both.
clue.ar-kilometre-marker-description: Distance markers have a white body with a dark band showing the route number.
clue.ar-guardrail-reflector-description: Guardrails have rectangular yellow and red reflectors.
clue.ar-wide-open-landscape-description: Vast, open terrain with sparse vegetation and few people.
clue.ar-city-taxi-map-description: Distinctive taxi colour schemes help pinpoint locations in multiple cities.
clue.ar-western-mountain-description: The far west is dominated by mountainous terrain along the Andes.
clue.ar-chaco-formosa-description: Sandy ground covered with dense low shrubs and trees.
clue.ar-grassland-plantation-description: Open grasslands dotted with scattered clusters of planted trees.
clue.ar-buenos-aires-lake-description: Roadside ponds and small bodies of water appear in Buenos Aires province.
clue.ar-san-luis-red-pavement-descriptio: San Luis roads have a reddish surface bordered by tall Argentine needle-grass.
clue.ar-central-south-barren-flat-descri: Central-south Argentina features empty, level plains with almost no vegetation.
clue.ar-tierra-del-fuego-grass-descripti: Low, windswept grass with few shrubs signals Tierra del Fuego or SE Santa Cruz.
clue.ar-entre-rios-tree-plantation-descr: Argentina's densest commercial tree plantations are in Entre Ríos.
clue.ar-tierra-del-fuego-beech-forest-de: Dense beech forests are a hallmark of Tierra del Fuego.
clue.ar-caranday-wax-palm-description: Caranday Wax Palm has short fan-shaped fronds and grows in sparse stands, mainly in Formosa.
clue.ar-caranday-palm-trithrinax-descrip: Trithrinax campestris has compact fan leaves and a trunk with dried leaf matter, native to Córdoba highlands.
clue.ar-macaw-palm-description: Macaw Palm has narrow, slender fronds with a pointed crown, wild in Formosa, Chaco, and Misiones.
clue.ar-cardon-cactus-description: Cardón cactus grows at high altitudes in Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta, and Jujuy with branching candelabra shape.
clue.ar-toothpick-cactus-description: Stetsonia coryne is a tall, branched cactus with long slender spines, found between Catamarca and Córdoba.
clue.ar-wild-sunflower-description: Wild sunflowers grow commonly along roadsides in Salta, Jujuy, and Tucumán.
clue.ar-calden-tree-description: Caldén is a medium-large deciduous tree with fine foliage and twisting branches, found mainly in La Pampa.
clue.ar-pampas-grass-description: Pampas grass has tall clustered stems topped by soft white plumes, defining the Pampas region.
clue.ar-sugarcane-field-description: Sugarcane cultivation is concentrated in Tucumán, with smaller pockets in Salta and Jujuy.
clue.ar-sorghum-field-description: Sorghum crops have deep red seed heads, common in Santa Fe, Córdoba, and Buenos Aires.
clue.ar-corn-field-description: Maize cultivation is widespread in northern Argentina, especially Córdoba, Buenos Aires, and Santiago del Estero.
clue.ar-sunflower-field-description: Commercial sunflower fields are most common in southern Chaco, with some in Buenos Aires and southern Córdoba.
clue.ar-hook-pole-la-rioja-mendoza-descr: Wooden utility poles with curved hook shapes appear only in La Rioja and Mendoza.
clue.ar-mendoza-single-insulator-pole-de: Mendoza utility poles have one insulator mounted on the side.
clue.ar-tucuman-pole-sticker-description: Tucumán utility poles often have tall white stickers with multi-digit numbers.
clue.ar-cordoba-road-marker-description: Córdoba provincial roads have distinctive kilometre markers unique to the province.
clue.ar-la-pampa-t-junction-sign-descrip: La Pampa T-junctions have rectangular yellow signs with route numbers, arrows, and a chevron base.
clue.ar-jujuy-red-brick-description: Bolivia-style red brick construction appears in western Jujuy province.
clue.ar-pink-trumpet-tree-description: Pink-flowering lapacho trees line streets in northern Salta towns like Orán and Tartagal.
clue.ar-jujuy-salt-pan-description: Expansive salt flats are concentrated in Jujuy province.
clue.ar-cordoba-western-mountain-descrip: Moderate-elevation mountains lie west of Córdoba city, lower than the Andes.
clue.ar-horse-trekker-san-juan-descripti: Horseback Trekker coverage exists in southwest San Juan province.
clue.ar-mendoza-vineyard-description: Vineyards backed by mountains and plains indicate Mendoza wine region near the city.
clue.ar-bahia-blanca-grass-hill-descript: Rolling grassy hills near the coast northeast of Bahía Blanca in southern Buenos Aires.
clue.ar-monkey-puzzle-tree-description: Monkey puzzle trees grow in western Neuquén, especially along provincial road 23.
clue.ar-rp25-snow-coverage-description: The eastern section of the RP25 in Santa Cruz province has coverage captured under heavy snowfall.
clue.ar-country-flag-description: The national flag of Argentina is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.au-gum-tree-eucalyptus-description: Eucalyptus trees have pale bark and rounded clumps of foliage.
clue.au-white-road-line-description: Australian roads use white markings almost everywhere.
clue.au-rumble-strip-description: Edge lines sometimes have short white bars across them as rumble strips.
clue.au-chevron-description: Curve warning chevrons appear as white arrows on black or black arrows on yellow.
clue.au-green-directional-sign-descripti: Green signs with white arrows indicate nearby towns and distances.
clue.au-speed-limit-sign-description: Speed limits show a black number in a red ring on a white rectangular plate.
clue.au-state-licence-plate-description: Every Australian state has its own plate design, often visible even through blur.
clue.au-phone-area-code-description: Australian phone numbers have an eight-digit number preceded by a two-digit state area code.
clue.au-state-bus-stop-description: Bus stop designs differ by state and appear frequently in urban areas.
clue.au-stobie-pole-south-australia-desc: The distinctive steel-and-concrete Stobie pole with a trident or rotated-E top is a hallmark of South Australia.
clue.au-rusty-metal-pole-northern-territ: Northern Territory has rusted metal utility poles peppered with holes along their length.
clue.au-concrete-pole-victoria-descripti: Concrete utility poles are heavily concentrated in Victoria.
clue.au-trident-pole-top-wa-vic-descript: Pole tops shaped like a three-pronged fork appear in Western Australia and Victoria.
clue.au-upward-angled-coil-pole-top-quee: Queensland electricity poles often have side-mounted coils that tilt upwards.
clue.au-three-coil-pole-top-victoria-des: Victoria pole tops typically carry three round coils: one vertical at the peak and one on each side.
clue.au-l-shaped-metal-crossbar-tasmania: Tasmanian utility poles often feature a slim metal arm bent at a right angle forming an L-shape at the top.
clue.au-blue-pole-sticker-queensland-des: Round blue stickers appear on power poles throughout Queensland.
clue.au-black-pole-marking-description: Queensland power poles bear distinctive black printed marks, often with angled numbers.
clue.au-olive-green-possum-guard-descrip: Tasmania's electricity poles have olive-green possum guards.
clue.au-green-pole-base-description: Western Australian timber utility poles often have green-painted lower sections.
clue.au-short-bollard-reflector-descript: Bollards with reflectors shorter than standard are concentrated in Queensland and South Australia.
clue.au-brown-bottom-bollard-description: Western Australian road bollards often have a brown-painted lower portion.
clue.au-black-white-striped-bollard-desc: Bollards with alternating black and white horizontal stripes are found only in Western Australia.
clue.au-black-yellow-bollard-description: Black and yellow bollards are a Queensland-only design.
clue.au-flat-signpost-description: South Australia and Western Australia occasionally use flat-profile sign poles instead of cylindrical ones.
clue.au-yellow-signpost-sticker-descript: Northern Territory signposts sometimes have small yellow adhesive labels.
clue.au-fluorescent-sign-border-descript: Queensland road signs often have bright fluorescent borders.
clue.au-red-no-stopping-sign-description: New South Wales uses red 'No Stopping' signs; other states use white.
clue.au-text-based-parking-sign-descript: ACT 'No Stopping' and 'No Parking' signs include the restriction spelled out in words.
clue.au-white-directional-sign-descripti: Tasmania is the only state with white-background directional road signs.
clue.au-c-road-description: Route numbers prefixed with 'C' appear in Victoria and Tasmania.
clue.au-25kmh-school-zone-description: South Australia enforces a 25 km/h school zone speed limit.
clue.au-130kmh-speed-limit-description: Northern Territory has a 130 km/h speed limit.
clue.au-thin-keep-left-sign-description: A slimmer 'Keep Left' sign without an arrow appears in NSW, Queensland, and Northern Territory.
clue.au-dark-green-property-marker-descr: Roadside property markers in dark green are a Western Australian feature.
clue.au-white-property-marker-descriptio: South Australia uses white property markers along its roads.
clue.au-guardrail-ending-description: Guardrails in NSW and the ACT end with a black stripe on a yellow field.
clue.au-blue-circle-hydrant-pole-descrip: Victoria has white hydrant indicator poles topped with a red segment and a blue circle.
clue.au-red-top-fire-hydrant-description: Fire hydrants in Victoria have red-painted caps.
clue.au-reddish-orange-soil-description: Western Australian ground, especially near Perth, has a reddish-orange colour.
clue.au-brush-plant-description: Brush-type shrubs with dense, bushy growth are common in Western Australia.
clue.au-termite-mound-description: Tall brown rough, spiky structures rising from the earth are termite mounds, mainly in the Northern Territory.
clue.au-dry-shrubland-description: From Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA, arid scrub, broad-canopied gum trees, and sandy orange earth define the landscape.
clue.au-green-golden-field-description: A belt of verdant or golden farmland runs from southern Yorke Peninsula to Echuca with broad gum canopies.
clue.au-tropical-north-queensland-descri: Far north Queensland's coastal strip is lushly tropical with palms and dense dark green foliage.
clue.au-sugarcane-field-description: Sugarcane fields dominate northern Queensland's tropical agricultural landscape.
clue.au-inland-nsw-landscape-description: Interior NSW is flat with red soil and dry pale-green scrub, becoming more temperate and hilly near borders.
clue.au-tasmania-landscape-description: Tasmania has green rolling hills, roadside eucalyptus, and densely forested hilly interiors.
clue.au-rare-google-car-snorkel-descript: Cars with snorkels, protecting engines during water crossings, are concentrated in NSW and the ACT.
clue.au-mount-gambier-sa-description: Mount Gambier in SA features chalky white soil and large pine plantations.
clue.au-kangaroo-island-sa-description: Kangaroo Island has scrubby low eucalyptus, bushy undergrowth, and orange-tinted soil.
clue.au-brisbane-street-sign-description: Brisbane City Council street signs have a distinctive design.
clue.au-sydney-street-sign-description: City of Sydney street signs have a unique design.
clue.au-country-flag-description: The national flag of Australia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ro-licence-plates-description: Romanian plates are long, white European style with a single blue strip on the left.
clue.ro-romanian-language-description: A Romance language with unique diacritics Ă/ă, Ș/ș, and Ț/ț.
clue.ro-round-concrete-poles-description: Round concrete utility poles are widespread in Romania.
clue.ro-large-yellow-pole-stickers-descr: Extremely large yellow stickers wrapped around poles, usually with the town or city name.
clue.ro-inverted-triangle-pole-tops-desc: Some pole tops have two support bars forming an upside-down triangle shape.
clue.ro-short-dash-edge-lines-descriptio: Outer road lines made of short dashes with narrow gaps are a clue for Romania.
clue.ro-thick-centre-lines-description: Centre road lines are often noticeably thicker than average.
clue.ro-directional-signs-description: Blue arrow-shaped signs with white borders, often showing road numbers in red or blue.
clue.ro-town-entry-signs-description: Yellow speed limit signs with city skylines, often with a white sign below showing the town name.
clue.ro-black-sign-backs-description: The back sides of road signs in Romania are often painted black.
clue.ro-chevrons-description: Red-on-white chevron boards frequently have a yellow frame.
clue.ro-bollards-description: Thin white bollards with a red vertical strip near the top.
clue.ro-thick-border-yield-sign-descript: Romanian yield signs have an extremely thick red border and thin white outline.
clue.ro-architecture-description: Single-family stone houses painted in pastels with orange tile or grey metal roofs; some have painted square tile walls.
clue.ro-carpathian-mountains-description: Tall forested mountains and hills dominate the centre and north of Romania.
clue.ro-agricultural-lowlands-descriptio: Flat or rolling agricultural land dominates southern and eastern Romania.
