clue.br-parana-street-name-pole-descript: Street names sometimes painted directly on utility poles at intersections in Paraná.
clue.br-sao-paulo-asymmetric-pole-top-de: Off-centre crossarm with diagonal support common in São Paulo and some other states.
clue.br-ceara-rondonia-unsupported-cross: Asymmetric crossarm with no bracing exclusive to Ceará and Rondônia.
clue.br-ceara-roraima-zigzag-pole-top-ti: Ceará and Roraima Zigzag Pole Top
clue.br-ceara-roraima-zigzag-pole-top-de: Zigzag-shaped top bar on a tall pole seen only in Ceará and Roraima.
clue.br-pencil-pole-description: Poles capped with smooth conical tips typical of Rio de Janeiro.
clue.br-alternating-horizontal-insulator: One central insulator above with horizontally alternating ones below in Mato Grosso and southern Acre.
clue.br-brown-mushroom-insulator-descrip: Brown mushroom-shaped insulators exclusive to Pernambuco.
clue.br-white-mushroom-insulator-descrip: White mushroom-shaped insulators in Bahia and around Brasília.
clue.br-transparent-insulator-descriptio: Clear glass or plastic insulators in Alagoas and Santa Catarina.
clue.br-spool-shaped-insulator-descripti: Thread spool-shaped insulators in Rio de Janeiro, Espírito Santo, and Ceará.
clue.br-elongated-thin-insulator-descrip: Long, slender insulators mainly in Ceará.
clue.br-horizontal-insulator-description: Sideways-mounted insulators common in Pará and Mato Grosso.
clue.br-long-grey-insulator-description: Tall grey insulators common in Pará, Mato Grosso, Tocantins, Bahia, and other states.
clue.br-maranhao-trident-insulator-descr: Black double-disc insulators arranged in a trident pattern characteristic of Maranhão.
clue.br-lollipop-insulator-description: Round or conical insulators on vertical rods above crossbars common in Rio Grande do Norte, Paraíba, and Pernambuco.
clue.br-dark-brown-insulator-grey-base-t: Dark Brown Insulators with Grey Bases
clue.br-dark-brown-insulator-grey-base-d: Found almost exclusively in Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.
clue.br-concrete-waste-bin-description: In Acre and Rondônia, Brazilian homes use concrete curbside waste baskets instead of metal.
clue.br-two-part-lamp-fixture-descriptio: Dual-head street lights are common in Minas Gerais and Goiás, and also appear in several other states.
clue.br-parana-armless-lamp-description: Northern Paraná street lights sometimes lack horizontal arms and are mounted directly on poles.
clue.br-direct-mounted-lamp-arm-descript: In several states, lamp arms are bent and run along the pole, attached directly to it rather than through a plate.
clue.br-roraima-city-coloured-lamp-descr: Roraima's lamp fixtures share a shape but are painted different colours by city.
clue.br-ceara-ornamental-lamp-arm-descri: Ceará street lights often have decorative, brightly painted arms, sometimes with town names.
clue.br-sao-paulo-divided-highway-descri: São Paulo has significantly more multi-lane divided highways than other parts of Brazil.
clue.br-sao-paulo-km-marker-phone-title: São Paulo Km Marker Phone Numbers
clue.br-sao-paulo-km-marker-phone-descri: Telephone numbers sometimes appear below kilometre marker posts in São Paulo.
clue.br-cobblestone-street-description: Cobblestone roads are most frequent in the northeast and Rio Grande do Sul.
clue.br-hexagonal-concrete-tile-descript: Hexagonal concrete paving blocks are common in Santa Catarina and Minas Gerais.
clue.br-acre-red-brick-road-description: Some roads in Acre are paved with red bricks.
clue.br-irregular-cobblestone-road-descr: Streets paved with uneven stones are common in southeastern Rio Grande do Sul and Minas Gerais.
clue.br-rough-square-stone-road-descript: Bumpy roads of roughly square-cut stones appear in western Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina.
clue.br-brown-tile-pavement-description: Brown tile footpaths, jagged or square, are typical of Rio Grande do Sul and sometimes Santa Catarina.
clue.br-european-influenced-architecture: Southern states, especially Santa Catarina, feature buildings with Germanic architectural style.
clue.br-stilt-house-description: Timber houses on stilts are common in Acre and flood-prone areas of Amazonas and Pará.
clue.br-piaui-red-gravel-shoulder-descri: Roads in Piauí have red gravel verges, often persisting alongside tarmac and kerbs.
clue.br-joao-de-barro-nest-description: Rufous Hornero bird builds round clay nests atop utility poles across southern Brazil.
clue.br-coastal-rio-grande-do-sul-wetlan: Coastal Rio Grande do Sul Wetland
Rio Grande do Sul's coast is an unusually flat wetland for Brazil.
clue.br-sao-paulo-pole-id-paint-descript: Poles in São Paulo have a yellow rectangle with letters and digits indicating municipality and ID.
clue.br-rio-de-janeiro-curved-lamp-arm-t: Rio de Janeiro Curved Lamp Arms
clue.br-rio-de-janeiro-curved-lamp-arm-d: Street light arms in Rio de Janeiro are continuously curved along their entire length.
clue.br-country-flag-description: The national flag of Brazil is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.io-palm-lined-sand-beach-descriptio: Sandy shorelines fringed with palm trees.
clue.io-coconut-palm-forest-description: Dense coconut palm stands along the coast.
clue.io-interior-grassy-clearing-descrip: Open grassy fields ringed by low bushes and palms on larger islands.
clue.io-offshore-trekker-footage-descrip: Imagery taken from shallow water offshore.
clue.io-country-flag-description: The national flag of the British Indian Ocean Territory is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.bg-licence-plate-description: Bulgarian plates have a blue EU band on the left side.
clue.bg-street-ulitsa-description: Streets are labelled улица (ulitsa), often shortened to ул.
clue.bg-concrete-utility-pole-descriptio: Dominant poles are round concrete cylinders.
clue.bg-alternating-hook-insulator-descr: Pole tops have small insulators arranged in alternating hooks along a crossarm.
clue.bg-three-large-hook-insulator-descr: Poles have three oversized hook-shaped insulators pointing upward, staggered side to side.
clue.bg-chevron-description: Curve warning boards show red arrows on a white background.
clue.xx-general-01-62-bilingual-signs-de: Road direction signs in Bulgaria are blue, arrow-shaped, and printed in both Cyrillic and Latin script.
clue.bg-town-entry-sign-description: Settlement names appear on plain white boards with Cyrillic and Latin text in two lines.
clue.bg-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Bulgarian pedestrian crossing signs show a pedestrian wearing a hat walking across four horizontal stripes.
clue.bg-bollard-description: Roadside bollards have red reflectors facing traffic and white on the rear.
clue.bg-thin-road-marking-description: Road line markings are noticeably narrow.
clue.bg-road-surface-quality-description: Road surfaces often have fine cracks and occasional potholes.
clue.bg-orange-roof-tile-description: Houses have orange clay tile roofs with visible mortar patches and uneven tilework.
clue.bg-suburban-area-description: Suburbs have tightly packed small houses with a run-down appearance.
clue.bg-topography-overview-description: The Balkan range bisects the country; broad plains lie north, Rhodope Mountains in the south, and small valleys in the west.
clue.bg-area-code-description: Telephone area codes start with a digit that narrows down the region.
clue.bg-pirin-rila-peak-description: Sharp, pyramid-like summits of Pirin and Rila parks are visible in certain provinces.
clue.bg-wind-turbine-description: Wind farms concentrate in Dobrich Province near the Black Sea coast.
clue.bg-nessebar-sozopol-old-town-descri: Historic cores feature buildings with raw stone, whitewashed walls, dark timber framing, and cobblestone lanes.
clue.bg-sofia-street-sign-description: Street plaques are white with two red bands—one along the bottom edge and one across part of the top.
clue.bg-stara-zagora-street-sign-descrip: Street plaques are brown with vivid yellow lettering.
clue.bg-country-flag-description: The national flag of Bulgaria is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-pole-01-01-cambodian-poles-descr: In Cambodia, you will typically see either concrete ladder poles with rectangular sections or round poles with small holes.
clue.kh-bollard-description: Common bollards are stone posts with red-and-white stripes or red tops with embedded reflectors.
clue.kh-road-marker-description: Kilometre posts are stone with white bases and rounded red tops showing road numbers and town distances.
clue.kh-chevron-description: Cambodian curve boards are black with yellow arrows but appear infrequently.
clue.kh-road-line-description: Cambodian roads have yellow centre lines; white edge lines are uncommon but always solid.
clue.kh-unpaved-road-description: Many Cambodian roads are unpaved; asphalt is mostly on main roads and in urban areas.
clue.kh-stilt-house-description: Wooden stilt houses with vertical plank walls and layered roofs are widespread in Cambodia.
clue.kh-house-colour-scheme-description: Traditional Cambodian stilt houses have walls in dark red-brown, light blue, or ochre orange, with doors and windows often bright blue.
clue.kh-roof-style-description: Many Cambodian homes have tiled orange or red roofs, sometimes with ornamental ridge and corner details; corrugated metal roofing is also common.
clue.kh-buddhist-temple-description: Ornately decorated temples with multi-tiered roofs and Buddhist flags are found throughout Cambodia.
clue.kh-beer-advertisement-description: Billboards and signs advertising Angkor, Anchor, and Cambodia Beer are ubiquitous.
clue.kh-cpp-party-sign-description: Distinctive blue signs from the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) often feature portraits of three party leaders.
clue.kh-central-agricultural-plain-descr: A flat, low-lying central plain with cultivated fields and villages.
clue.kh-northeast-landscape-description: Less cultivated northeast with wild vegetation and gently rolling hills.
clue.kh-southwest-highland-description: Highest elevations with hills, low mountains, dense forest inland, and more populated coastal areas.
clue.kh-white-sandy-soil-southeast-descr: Bright white to beige sandy soil common southeast of Phnom Penh and around the capital.
clue.kh-northern-thai-border-mountain-de: Mountainous ridgeline near the Thai border with characteristic red soil; roads lie in flat lowlands south of the ridgeline.
clue.kh-rubber-tree-plantation-descripti: Neatly rowed thin-trunked rubber trees with dark green canopies, found northeast of Phnom Penh, around Ban Lung, and near Pech Sreada.
clue.kh-road-48-black-white-bollard-desc: Black-and-white bollards appear only on Road 48 between Tatai and the Road 4 intersection.
clue.kh-kiri-sakor-road-construction-des: Road from Road 48 to Kiri Sakor is under construction with one paved lane and exposed red soil on the other side.
clue.kh-southwest-jungle-off-road-descri: Unpaved tracks northeast of Road 48 with red soil, dense jungle, and hilly terrain.
clue.kh-phnum-samkos-area-description: Overcast weather, large distant mountains, unpaved brown roads, and lush wild vegetation near Phnum Samkos.
clue.kh-road-4-red-shoulder-description: Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk has wide red-brown shoulders that darken closer to the coast.
clue.kh-oil-palm-plantation-description: Oil palm plantations along Road 4 and its rural offshoots just north of Preah Nob.
clue.kh-road-41-description: Wide gravelly grey road southwest of Phnom Penh running north-northeast through flat agricultural terrain with distant hills.
clue.kh-unique-pole-road-5-6-description: Utility poles on Roads 5 and 6 have three horizontal beams with hanging insulators on one side and distinctive base indents.
clue.kh-pech-sreada-rubber-plantation-de: Rubber trees near Pech Sreada with bright orange soil and a barren dry-season look.
clue.kh-angkor-wat-description: Massive Khmer temple complex north of Siem Reap with dark weathered stone and tourist crowds.
clue.kh-country-flag-description: The national flag of Cambodia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-road-signs-01-checkered-signs-de: In Canada, T-intersection signs are diamond-shaped and have a distinctive checkered pattern.
clue.ca-centre-line-marking-description: Canadian roads commonly use a single yellow centre line; double yellow lines also appear.
clue.ca-missing-front-plate-description: Seven provinces issue only a rear plate; vehicles without front plates exclude BC, Manitoba, and Ontario.
clue.ca-alberta-licence-plate-descriptio: White plate with bold red characters, visible through the blur as a red tint
clue.ca-british-columbia-licence-plate-d: British Columbia plates appear pale white with a slight bluish tint.
clue.ca-manitoba-licence-plate-descripti: Manitoba plates are white with dark blue character shapes, a faint pale-blue area near the top, and blurred green-turquoise landscape shapes along the lower edges.
clue.ca-new-brunswick-licence-plate-desc: New Brunswick plates appear pale white with a reddish tint.
clue.ca-newfoundland-labrador-licence-pl: Newfoundland and Labrador plates are pale white with a red blob in the lower-left area.
clue.ca-nova-scotia-licence-plate-descri: White plate with dark blue characters, visible only as blue blurred shapes.
clue.ca-ontario-licence-plate-descriptio: Dark blue plate with white characters, white trillium logo, and "A PLACE TO GROW" slogan at the bottom.
clue.ca-prince-edward-island-licence-pla: Prince Edward Island plates are pale white with a green tint and a faint red-orange blob in the centre.
clue.ca-quebec-licence-plate-description: Québec plates appear white with a dark bluish tint.
clue.ca-saskatchewan-licence-plate-descr: Saskatchewan plates are white with green character shapes, a faint green text-like area, and a golden wheat-sheaf graphic between the character groups.
clue.ca-10-alberta-description: Highway shields in Alberta have 'ALBERTA' written on the banner at the bottom.
clue.ca-10-british-columbia-description: Highway shields in British Columbia have the BC coat of arms at the top and 'B.C.' written below the route number.
clue.ca-10-manitoba-description: Highway shields in Manitoba have 'MANITOBA' written on the banner at the bottom.
clue.ca-10-new-brunswick-description: New Brunswick highway shields show the white silhouette of the province with 'NB' inside.
clue.ca-10-newfoundland-and-labrador-des: Highway shields in Newfoundland have 'NEWFOUNDLAND' written on the banner at the bottom.
clue.ca-10-nova-scotia-description: Highway shields in Nova Scotia show the provincial flag at the top.
clue.ca-10-ontario-description: Highway shields in Ontario have a black crown on top and 'ONTARIO' written at the bottom.
clue.ca-10-prince-edward-island-descript: Highway shields in Prince Edward Island have 'PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND' written on the banner at the bottom.
clue.ca-10-quebec-description: Route shields in Quebec are red on top and blue on the bottom, with a small fleur-de-lis below the route number.
clue.ca-10-saskatchewan-description: Highway shields in Saskatchewan have 'SASKATCHEWAN' written on the banner at the bottom.
clue.ca-11-alberta-description: Tall, narrow green rectangle with white numbers centered vertically, no additional symbols.
clue.ca-11-british-columbia-description: Green rectangular marker with white numbers, often with small white 'km' label below number.
clue.ca-11-manitoba-description: Green rectangle with bold white numbers, sometimes with small provincial highway shield above or below number.
clue.ca-11-new-brunswick-description: Green rectangle with white numbers, sometimes including small white 'km' at bottom right corner.
clue.ca-11-newfoundland-and-labrador-des: Green rectangle with white numbers, typically without additional text or symbols, mounted on metal posts.
clue.ca-11-nova-scotia-description: Green rectangle with white numbers, sometimes with small white 'km' at bottom.
clue.ca-11-ontario-description: Ontario's kilometre marker is a tall green rectangle with white numbers above a white square at the post's bottom.
clue.ca-11-prince-edward-island-descript: Prince Edward Island uses green rectangular markers with white numbers, sometimes with a small 'km' label, often on wooden posts.
clue.ca-11-quebec-description: Quebec's kilometre markers are green rectangles with white numbers, often with a small white 'km' below.
clue.ca-11-saskatchewan-description: Saskatchewan's markers are green rectangles with white numbers, sometimes with a small 'km' label, usually on metal posts.
clue.ca-provincial-speed-sign-variant-de: Ontario speed signs may include a black strip reading 'km/h' or 'begins'. British Columbia shows 'km/h' without the black section. Québec signs sometimes include French text.
clue.ca-alberta-bollard-description: Cylindrical white bollards with two black bands wrapped all the way around are common at Alberta intersections.
clue.ca-manitoba-bollard-description: Manitoba bollards are black over grey, usually with an orange stripe below the grey section; further north, rectangular wooden bollards appear.
clue.ca-quebec-guardrail-bollard-descrip: Slender white poles tipped with a red or green reflector, always mounted directly on guardrails, unique to Québec.
clue.ca-quebec-fire-hydrant-marker-descr: Yellow markers on top of signposts indicate underground fire hydrants throughout Québec.
clue.ca-quebec-rectangular-road-marker-d: Small rectangular reflective markers line Québec roadsides; their colour varies.
clue.ca-ontario-diamond-road-marker-desc: Diamond-shaped reflective markers are placed along roadsides in Ontario; their colour varies.
clue.ca-ontario-wire-guardrail-descripti: Ontario guardrails have round wooden posts linked by exactly three metal wires; some posts have a reflective white band.
clue.ca-northwest-territories-bollard-de: Cylindrical black-and-white bollards with two notably thick black bands, broader than Alberta's.
clue.ca-transformer-orientation-bc-nb-de: Pole-mounted transformers in British Columbia and New Brunswick face the road; elsewhere they align with the wires.
clue.ca-45-degree-transformer-pei-ns-des: Transformers on Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia are mounted at a 45° angle to the road; PEI ones usually have red numbers on the side.
clue.ca-ontario-pole-top-description: Ontario poles often have two insulators on the sides and one on top, attached with a distinctive bracket; multiple units can stack vertically.
clue.ca-quebec-pole-top-description: Some Québec utility poles carry insulator rods that tilt slightly upward, a recognisable silhouette.
clue.ca-quebec-pole-label-description: Québec utility poles sometimes display a vertical sticker split black and yellow, with a small 'Q' in the black half.
clue.ca-pei-pole-sticker-description: Prince Edward Island utility poles typically bear a small white sticker.
clue.ca-saskatchewan-alternating-pole-to: Insulators on consecutive Saskatchewan poles alternate sides: one pole has one insulator left and two right, the next reverses this.
clue.ca-quebec-t-intersection-sign-descr: Québec's T-intersection signs omit the chequerboard pattern entirely.
clue.ca-newfoundland-t-intersection-sign: Newfoundland's diamond-shaped T-intersection sign sits inside a rectangular yellow border, unique to the province.
clue.ca-bc-green-sign-back-description: The reverse side of road signs in British Columbia is often painted green.
clue.ca-bc-hanging-sign-description: In British Columbia, road signs are sometimes suspended from distinctive overhead brackets instead of posts.
clue.ca-bc-concrete-barrier-description: British Columbia favours solid concrete barriers over metal guardrails on highways.
clue.ca-manitoba-signpost-sticker-descri: Manitoba signposts sometimes carry a small green-and-white striped sticker.
clue.ca-saskatchewan-signpost-triangle-d: White triangular markers are attached to Saskatchewan signposts; the number varies.
clue.ca-saskatchewan-centre-line-dash-de: White dashed lines sometimes appear between yellow centre lines on Saskatchewan roads.
clue.ca-arret-stop-sign-description: Stop signs displaying only the French word 'Arrêt' are found exclusively in Québec.
clue.ca-bilingual-stop-arret-sign-descri: Stop signs bearing both 'Stop' and 'Arrêt' are predominantly a New Brunswick feature.
clue.ca-alberta-grid-road-system-descrip: Alberta's rural roads follow a numbered grid with Township roads running east–west and Range roads running north–south.
clue.ca-alberta-cable-guardrail-descript: Some Alberta highways have guardrails made of short posts connected by steel cables.
clue.ca-newfoundland-pyramid-post-top-de: Wooden guardrail posts in Newfoundland and Labrador are capped with a distinctive pyramid shape.
clue.ca-newfoundland-hydrant-marker-desc: Fire hydrants in Newfoundland often have a diamond-shaped marker beside them.
clue.ca-newfoundland-wooden-sign-base-de: Signs in Newfoundland and Labrador are sometimes supported by wooden box bases.
clue.ca-traffic-cone-colour-description: Ontario uses orange-and-black striped cones; Québec uses orange-and-white striped cones.
clue.ca-quebec-red-white-chevron-descrip: Québec curve warning boards are red and white, unlike the yellow-and-black used elsewhere.
clue.ca-rectangular-street-lamp-nb-ns-de: New Brunswick and Nova Scotia often use rectangular-shaped lamp heads on street lights.
clue.ca-western-mountain-description: Major mountain ranges are concentrated in British Columbia, western Alberta, and parts of Yukon.
clue.ca-yukon-boreal-landscape-descripti: Yukon features boreal terrain with hilly land, distant mountains, and coniferous trees lining roads.
clue.ca-bc-interior-kamloops-kelowna-des: Southern British Columbia's interior is drier and hillier with brown grasslands and pine forests.
clue.ca-great-plain-description: A vast, flat agricultural area with few trees, growing drier toward the southwest near Montana.
clue.ca-canola-field-description: Bright yellow canola flower fields are found in the central southern prairies.
clue.ca-southern-saskatchewan-hill-descr: Southern Saskatchewan has hilly, barren terrain with numerous river valleys.
clue.ca-manitoba-aspen-tree-description: Aspens with white trunks are common in Manitoba's forests, turning yellow in autumn.
clue.ca-canadian-shield-exposed-rock-des: The Canadian Shield features bare rock outcrops visible along highways in eastern Canada.
clue.ca-quebec-city-windsor-corridor-des: Canada's most populated zone, a flat green belt mixing farmland and woodland between Québec City and Windsor.
clue.ca-pei-red-soil-description: Prince Edward Island is known for its red-tinted earth and potato farming.
clue.ca-newfoundland-balsam-fir-descript: The balsam fir, a cone-shaped evergreen, is very common in Newfoundland.
clue.ca-area-code-description: Canadian phone numbers start with a three-digit area code in the format XXX XXX XXXX.
clue.ca-provincial-flag-description: Provincial flag, Québec's Fleurdelisé, is commonly displayed on buildings and roads.
clue.ca-newfoundland-wooden-bin-descript: Octagonal wooden bins are common in Newfoundland driveways.
clue.ca-acadia-description: Acadia is a French-speaking region in northern and eastern New Brunswick, flying a French tricolour with a yellow star.
clue.ca-gaspe-peninsula-description: Inland roads wind through heavily forested mountainous terrain with frequent overcast weather.
clue.ca-cape-breton-highland-description: Northeastern Nova Scotia's Cape Breton Highlands have high elevation and dense mixed forests.
clue.ca-country-flag-description: The Canadian flag is red and white with a red maple leaf in the middle.
clue.cl-licence-plate-description: Private vehicles have white plates; taxis and commercial vehicles have orange ones.
clue.cl-slotted-signpost-description: Sign poles often have open slots cut into the upper section.
clue.cl-orange-temporary-bollard-descrip: Bright orange temporary road markers with white stripes sometimes replace permanent bollards.
clue.cl-red-bridge-post-description: Bridge railings and fence posts are commonly painted red.
clue.cl-climate-zone-description: Chile spans arid desert in the north, Mediterranean near Santiago, and cold oceanic in the south.
clue.cl-regional-road-letter-system-desc: Regional road numbers use letters from A in the north to Y in the south, indicating latitude.
clue.cl-phone-area-code-description: Landline numbers show two-digit area codes following a geographic pattern.
clue.cl-atacama-desert-description: The northern third is the Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth, with barren sand and rock.
clue.cl-arica-parinacota-landscape-descr: Rounded, sandy-looking mountains with carved valleys are typical of the northernmost province.
clue.cl-atacama-coquimbo-mountains-descr: Jagged, uneven rock formations dominate Atacama and northern Coquimbo.
clue.cl-brownish-red-soil-description: Reddish-brown earth patches indicate Atacama province.
clue.cl-eucalyptus-plantation-descriptio: Rows of eucalyptus trees in semi-arid settings point to southwestern Valparaíso.
clue.cl-santiago-region-landscape-descri: Semi-arid hillsides with sparse scrub surround the capital.
clue.cl-maule-province-description: Greener than Santiago, with vineyards common across the province.
clue.cl-concepcion-pine-description: Pinus radiata with fluffy needle clusters grow mainly in Bío Bío.
clue.cl-tree-lined-narrow-road-descripti: Narrow roads flanked by dense trees are common in Bío Bío and Araucanía.
clue.cl-monkey-puzzle-tree-description: Araucaria araucana with stiff, scaly branches grow in eastern Araucanía highlands.
clue.cl-chilean-rhubarb-description: Nalca with oversized cabbage-like leaves grows on Isla Grande de Chiloé and nearby mainland.
clue.cl-southern-green-valley-descriptio: Deep green valleys with rocky peaks and overcast skies span southern Los Lagos to northern Aysén.
clue.cl-autumn-coverage-southern-aysen-d: Southern Aysén shows vivid orange and red autumn foliage.
clue.cl-alto-bio-bio-national-reserve-de: A treeless highland plateau with triple yellow centre lines and monkey puzzle trees near the east.
clue.cl-orange-street-lamp-description: Warm orange street lights are common in Calama and Chañaral.
clue.cl-santiago-photocell-lamp-descript: Light-sensitive photocells on street lamps are common in Santiago.
clue.cl-arica-pole-marking-description: Utility poles in Arica have white number markings; elsewhere in Atacama Desert they are yellow.
clue.cl-country-flag-description: The national flag of Chile is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.cn-simplified-chinese-script-descri: Mainland China uses simplified Chinese characters with fewer brush strokes.
clue.cn-blue-licence-plate-description: Vehicles display blue-backed number plates with white characters.
clue.cn-museum-interior-description: Much coverage consists of indoor museum photography, concentrated around Beijing and Shanghai.
clue.cn-country-flag-description: The national flag of China is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.cx-silver-pickup-truck-description: Coverage uses a silver pickup truck with an open flatbed behind the camera.
clue.cx-tropical-forest-landscape-descri: Thick tropical rainforest with unpaved tracks, white sandy soil, settlements, and palm groves.
clue.cx-rural-trail-coverage-description: Beyond paved roads, narrow overgrown bush tracks lead deep into the forest.
clue.cx-built-up-area-description: All settlements are in the northeastern corner; elsewhere is dense jungle.
clue.cx-trail-trekker-description: Short walking trails are scattered across the island, often opening to beaches or viewpoints.
clue.cx-country-flag-description: The national flag of Christmas Island is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.cc-landscape-description: Flat, low-lying terrain of white sand with coconut palms and mowed grass, less forested than Christmas Island.
clue.cc-coastal-trekkers-description: Walking routes along shorelines with white sand, ocean on one side and palm trees on the other.
clue.cc-horsburgh-island-description: Pulau Luar's inland trekker passes through dry, yellow grassland with thin vegetation.
clue.cc-country-flag-description: The national flag of the Cocos Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.co-vehicles-01-01-yellow-plates-des: Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow license plates for personal vehicles.
clue.xx-general-01-25-colombian-cross-de: In Colombia, signposts have white backs that form a cross shape, known as the Colombian Cross.
clue.co-kilometre-marker-description: Two designs exist: a tall green post labelled 'Pr' and a stone marker with black lettering, both exclusive to Colombia.
clue.co-concrete-dark-pole-description: Most poles are concrete, with dark-coloured poles more common here than nearby countries.
clue.co-northern-arid-landscape-descript: The far north features pale, sandy ground and a dry, barren environment.
clue.co-llanos-lowland-description: A broad flat plain east of the Andes with tropical grassland, savanna, and isolated trees.
clue.co-antioquia-pole-marking-descripti: Poles with narrow black bands top and bottom and a broad yellow middle are characteristic of Antioquia.
clue.co-afro-colombian-pacific-coast-des: The Pacific coastline has a predominantly Afro-Colombian population.
clue.co-leticia-vehicle-description: A distinctive non-standard vehicle is used around Leticia, Colombia's southernmost Amazon settlement.
clue.co-la-guajira-desert-description: Arid scrubland with scattered cacti; a highway from Uribia to Puerto Bolívar runs parallel to a railway line.
clue.co-country-flag-description: The national flag of Colombia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.cr-spanish-language-description: Costa Rica's official language is Spanish.
clue.cr-licence-plate-description: Plates are compact white with blue characters, appearing faint light-blue due to blurring.
clue.cr-round-concrete-pole-description: Utility poles have cylindrical concrete shafts.
clue.cr-beach-trekker-description: Shoreline trekker paths are mainly along the northern Pacific coast and Cocos Island.
clue.cr-forest-trekker-description: Trekker routes through woodland are mostly in the central highlands and Cocos Island.
clue.cr-urban-coverage-location-descript: City-level trekker imagery focuses on San José and Cartago, with smaller amounts in Liberia and Filadelfia.
clue.cr-country-flag-description: The national flag of Costa Rica is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.hr-croatian-language-description: South Slavic language in Latin script; frequent 'IJE' digraph.
clue.hr-chevron-sign-description: Curve warning boards with red arrow on yellow or white background.
clue.hr-b-type-square-guardrail-descript: Square-profile (B-type) highway guardrails, rare in Europe.
clue.hr-gen-3-autumn-foliage-description: Landscapes often show golden and orange leaf colors in autumn.
clue.hr-vehicles-01-country-stickers-des: Oval stickers bearing the letters 'HR' can be sometimes be spotted on Croatian vehicles.
clue.hr-yellow-directional-sign-descript: Road signs have a yellow background with a black border, often tapering to a point.
clue.hr-utility-pole-alternating-hooks-d: Cylindrical concrete or timber poles; wooden ones have alternating step-pegs up each side.
clue.hr-exposed-red-brick-building-descr: Bare red brick walls on houses and outbuildings are common, especially inland.
clue.hr-blue-fire-hydrant-description: Hydrants are blue with two diagonally angled outlets on each side.
clue.hr-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Sign shows a walking figure with a visible belt crossing a zebra with five stripes.
clue.hr-local-brand-description: Ads for Karlovačko and Ožujsko beer; Konzum and Plodine supermarkets appear in cities.
clue.hr-phone-area-code-description: Croatian landline numbers start with zero plus regional area code.
clue.hr-flat-slavonian-northeast-descrip: Northeast Croatia is a broad agricultural plain.
clue.hr-hilly-zagorje-northwest-descript: Countryside north and west of Zagreb is rolling, hilly farmland.
clue.hr-rocky-adriatic-coast-description: Coast features bare limestone mountains, scrubby Mediterranean vegetation, and many islands.
clue.hr-coastal-beige-stone-house-descri: Adriatic buildings are beige stone or brick, often with green shutters.
clue.hr-istria-red-soil-description: Istria peninsula has earth with a reddish hue.
clue.hr-istrian-bilingual-sign-descripti: Street name plates in western Istria show Croatian and Italian text.
clue.hr-town-name-ending-ec-description: Settlement names ending in '-ec' cluster in northern inland Croatia.
clue.hr-zagreb-description: Capital city with metropolitan feel, apartment blocks, hilly north, and blue electric trams.
clue.hr-tram-city-description: Only Zagreb and Osijek have tram networks.
clue.hr-plain-northeast-zadar-descriptio: Flat lowland northeast of Zadar with a mountain ridge on the northern horizon.
clue.hr-southern-cypress-tree-descriptio: Tall, narrow cypress trees near Dubrovnik.
clue.hr-country-flag-description: The national flag of Croatia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.cz-wide-type-b-guardrail-descriptio: Czechia and Slovakia use a broad variant of guardrail unique in Europe.
clue.cz-short-metal-bar-pole-top-descrip: Czech pole tops commonly have compact horizontal metal bars carrying line insulators.
clue.cz-inverted-triangle-pole-support-d: Angled braces supporting the crossarm create an inverted-triangle silhouette at the pole top.
clue.cz-trident-pole-top-description: A distinctive pole-top design with three prongs forming a trident-like profile.
clue.cz-bolt-mounted-lamp-base-descripti: Street lamp posts often have chunky base plates secured by pairs of protruding bolts.
clue.cz-red-white-striped-temporary-sign: Square temporary sign poles wrapped in alternating red and white bands are common.
clue.cz-chevron-description: Curve warning boards are white with a red arrow; a less common variant uses red arrows on yellow.
clue.cz-striped-gas-water-poles-title: Striped Gas and Water Marker Poles
clue.cz-striped-gas-water-poles-descript: Slender roadside poles painted in coloured stripes mark underground gas or water lines.
clue.cz-hiking-trail-markers-description: Painted blazes with a coloured band between two white bands mark walking trails and directions.
clue.cz-colourful-panel-apartments-descr: Soviet-era prefabricated housing blocks are well maintained and decorated with bold colours and patterns.
clue.cz-diamond-roof-tiles-description: Roofing tiles cut into a diamond pattern are common on residential buildings.
clue.cz-bridge-end-markers-description: Dark plaques at bridge ends display the road number on the left side.
clue.cz-czech-slovak-script-description: Czech uses Ř, Ě, and Ů; Slovak uses Ľ, Ô, Ä, Ŕ, and Ĺ to distinguish their similar scripts.
clue.cz-rolling-landscape-description: The Czech terrain is gently undulating with hills but few tall mountains.
clue.cz-solid-edge-lines-no-centre-title: Solid Edge Lines, No Centre Line
clue.cz-solid-edge-lines-no-centre-descr: Many Czech roads have continuous white edge lines but no painted centre line.
clue.xx-general-01-53-arrow-signs-descri: Directional signs in Czechia taper to a solid filled arrow tip.
clue.cz-inset-sign-borders-description: Czech road signs have coloured borders separated from the edge by a narrow background strip.
clue.cz-highway-sign-double-border-descr: Motorway signs feature a white inner border framed by a second border in the sign's main colour.
clue.cz-bright-red-street-signs-descript: Street signs are vivid red plates, either wide on walls or narrow on posts; sometimes blue.
clue.cz-black-signpost-caps-description: Czech sign poles have chunky black caps on top.
clue.cz-five-stripe-pedestrian-signs-des: Pedestrian crossing signs show a figure walking across five horizontal stripes.
clue.cz-thin-road-sign-font-description: Text on Czech road signs uses a noticeably lightweight typeface.
clue.cz-kilometre-markers-description: Czech distance markers are framed in black with a yellow outline and lack the horizontal dividing line of Slovak markers.
clue.cz-yellow-bicycle-signs-description: Cycle route markers in Czechia are yellow, replacing white bands used in hiking markers.
clue.cz-semi-detached-suburban-houses-de: Czech suburban homes are often mirror-image pairs sharing a dividing wall.
clue.cz-winter-gen-3-coverage-descriptio: Many Czech images show overcast, grey winter scenes sometimes dusted with snow.
clue.cz-railway-crossing-signs-descripti: Czech level-crossing signs are bare cross shapes without backing panels.
clue.cz-road-number-regions-description: Road numbers start with digits 1 to 6 indicating regions; 7, 8, and 9 radiate from Prague northwards.
clue.cz-cycle-path-numbers-description: Four-digit cycle route numbers follow a clockwise sequence starting in Southern Bohemia.
clue.cz-phone-area-codes-description: Czech phone numbers have 9 digits; the first 1-3 digits are geographic area codes.
clue.cz-moravian-wine-region-description: About 95% of Czech wine production is in Moravia, marked by vineyards.
clue.cz-northern-bohemia-hills-descripti: Northern Bohemia features rolling farmland interrupted by isolated cone-shaped hills, some with castles.
clue.cz-timber-framed-houses-description: Half-timbered houses are common along the northern border with Germany.
clue.cz-timber-post-supported-floors-des: Northernmost houses have dark wooden columns supporting upper floors or balconies.
clue.cz-dark-wooden-houses-white-stripes: Dark Wooden Houses with White Stripes
Dark timber houses with white plaster or mortar lines are common in northern Czechia.
clue.cz-moravian-town-houses-description: Moravian village houses face the road with long sides and have tall, wide front entrances.
clue.cz-selske-baroko-folk-baroque-descr: Selské Baroko features richly ornamented façades on modest village buildings near České Budějovice.
clue.cz-single-pane-windows-description: Simple single-pane windows are more frequent in northwestern Czechia.
clue.cz-blue-street-signs-east-descripti: Blue-background street name plates are concentrated in eastern Czechia, especially Ostrava.
clue.cz-slovak-style-white-street-signs-: White street signs with blue text inside a red border indicate proximity to Slovakia.
clue.cz-white-street-signs-red-text-titl: White Street Signs with Red Text
clue.cz-white-street-signs-red-text-desc: White plates with red lettering appear mostly in eastern and southern Czechia.
clue.cz-white-street-signs-blue-text-tit: White Street Signs with Blue Text
clue.cz-white-street-signs-blue-text-des: White plates with blue lettering are common in eastern and central-northern Czechia.
clue.cz-white-street-signs-black-text-ti: White Street Signs with Black Text
clue.cz-white-street-signs-black-text-de: White plates with black text are frequent in the southeast and resemble blue-text signs.
clue.cz-country-flag-description: The national flag of Czechia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.do-square-concrete-pole-description: Electricity poles are predominantly square concrete with a reverse-L bracket at the top.
clue.do-dark-smooth-asphalt-description: Roads are notably dark, smooth asphalt, darker than typical Caribbean surfaces.
clue.do-country-flag-description: The national flag of the Dominican Republic is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ec-licence-plate-description: Private plates in Ecuador are white in short and long formats. Taxis and buses use orange plates.
clue.xx-general-01-08-ecuadorian-bollard: In Ecuador, bollards are typically either thin and round with two red stripes or flat with two red reflectors.
clue.ec-double-guardrail-description: Paired guardrails running in parallel are common.
clue.ec-chevron-overuse-description: Road bends have a high density of chevron signs.
clue.ec-square-road-sign-description: White square information signs with a standard layout are used extensively.
clue.ec-kilometre-marker-description: Distance posts are green with the highway shield emblem.
clue.ec-teal-blue-sign-back-description: Some sign backs are painted teal blue; poles are thin metal.
clue.ec-one-way-street-sign-description: Directional signs feature the text "UNA VIA" inside arrow shapes indicating traffic flow.
clue.ec-grey-brick-architecture-descript: Houses are mostly grey cinder blocks with corrugated metal roofs.
clue.ec-hexagonal-tile-pavement-descript: Ecuadorian roads sometimes have interlocking hexagonal tiles.
clue.ec-elevation-terrain-description: The Andes run through the center, with flat terrain on the Pacific coast and Amazon basin.
clue.ec-banana-plantation-description: Large banana plantations are in the southwestern lowlands.
clue.ec-dry-coastal-belt-description: An arid coastal strip lies between Guayaquil and Manta.
clue.ec-flat-guayaquil-region-descriptio: The Guayaquil area is the flattest, especially along E-25 and E-48 highways.
clue.ec-amazon-region-description: Amazon lowlands are flat and densely vegetated with Cordia trichotoma trees and oil palms.
clue.ec-esmeraldas-province-description: Esmeraldas has Amazon-like vegetation but is hillier.
clue.ec-southern-mountain-road-descripti: Southern mountain roads have twisting paths with exposed reddish-brown earth.
clue.ec-chimborazo-province-description: Chimborazo is semi-arid with abundant pine trees.
clue.ec-taxi-province-letter-description: Taxi plates start with the province's initial letter; same for private plates.
clue.ec-northeastern-roadside-pipeline-d: A brown above-ground pipeline runs alongside some northeastern roads.
clue.ec-galapagos-island-description: Galápagos has volcanic landscapes with lava fields, scrubland, and craters; covered by trekker and boat imagery.
clue.ec-country-flag-description: The national flag of Ecuador is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.eg-sandstone-architecture-descripti: Built environment features sandstone construction from ancient monuments to medieval fortifications.
clue.eg-arabic-script-description: Egypt uses Arabic script. It appears on signs, identifiable by flowing connected letters and diacritical dots.
clue.eg-country-flag-description: The national flag of Egypt is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ee-wooden-utility-pole-description: Round wooden poles with diagonal braces are common; Estonia has varied pole types.
clue.ee-square-concrete-pole-description: Square concrete poles appear regularly, often with diagonal bracing.
clue.ee-trident-pole-top-description: Pole tops have a single insulator pointing upward and two extending sideways.
clue.ee-metal-pole-cap-description: Most wooden poles have a small metal cap at the top.
clue.ee-short-dash-edge-line-description: Road edge markings sometimes use unusually short dashes.
clue.ee-chevron-description: Curve warning boards have a red background with white directional arrows.
clue.ee-warning-speed-sign-border-descri: Warning and speed limit signs have a narrow red border running to the edge.
clue.ee-bus-stop-sign-description: Estonian bus stop signs show a bus icon with four windows.
clue.ee-blue-white-signpost-wrapping-des: Signposts are commonly wrapped with alternating blue and white bands.
clue.ee-estonian-language-description: Estonian uses umlauted vowels (Ä, Ö, Ü) and the letter Õ (O with tilde).
clue.ee-street-name-suffix-description: The words 'tänav' (street) and 'tee' (road) are uniquely Estonian.
clue.ee-oval-blue-house-number-descripti: Buildings often display blue oval-shaped house number plates.
clue.ee-architecture-description: Estonian buildings combine wooden cladding, white-rendered brick, and steep corrugated metal roofs.
clue.ee-directional-sign-description: Wayfinding signs are blue with white lettering and a white border; arrows sit inside the sign.
clue.ee-elevation-hill-description: The country is mostly flat with hills in the southeast and Lääne-Viru County.
clue.ee-russian-minority-ida-viru-descri: Ida-Viru County has a Russian-speaking majority with occasional bilingual Cyrillic-Estonian signs.
clue.ee-country-flag-description: The national flag of Estonia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.fk-carcass-island-description: Wide-open grassy plains with the sea clearly visible in many directions. The terrain can become stony and rugged in places.
clue.fk-west-point-island-description: Broad treeless grassland with a yellowish tint to the vegetation. Unlike Carcass Island, the ocean is not readily visible from most vantage points.
clue.fk-west-point-bay-boat-trekker-desc: A marine trekker captured from a boat in West Point Bay, showing golden-brown hillsides in the background and the MS National Geographic Explorer anchored in the bay.
clue.fk-new-island-beach-description: A stretch of sandy shoreline where figures wearing red and blue outdoor jackets can be spotted.
clue.fk-new-island-inland-description: The interior of New Island is characterised by exposed dark brown earth, sometimes criss-crossed by vehicle tracks.
clue.fk-new-island-cliff-description: Dramatic, sheer coastal cliffs dropping straight into the ocean are a prominent feature of New Island's trekker route.
clue.fk-country-flag-description: The national flag of the Falkland Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.fo-architecture-description: Timber houses with raised stone basements and corrugated metal or turf roofs.
clue.fo-faroese-language-description: Faroese uses special letters including Ø, distinguishing it from Icelandic.
clue.fo-yellow-guardrail-reflector-descr: Metal guardrails fitted with yellow reflectors, unique in northern Europe.
clue.fo-directional-sign-description: Wayfinding signs in the Faroe Islands have a yellow background with a black border.
clue.fo-klakkur-trekker-description: Two pyramid-shaped snow-capped peaks visible to the south from Klakkur.
clue.fo-gjogv-trekker-description: Southward view of village and snow-dusted mountain ridges from Gjógv.
clue.fo-koltur-boat-trekker-description: Grey inflatable 'RIB62' with passengers in high-visibility clothing en route to Koltur.
clue.fo-country-flag-description: The national flag of the Faroe Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.fi-middle-road-line-description: Centre lines appear as white dashes, solid white, solid yellow, or double yellow lines.
clue.fi-bollard-description: Tall black-and-white posts with a rectangular white reflector on front and two reflective dots on back.
clue.fi-finnish-language-description: Finnish has long words, frequent double vowels, and special characters ä and ö.
clue.fi-yellow-sign-background-descripti: Information and direction signs in Finland have yellow backgrounds.
clue.fi-yellow-stroke-sign-description: Red-bordered regulatory signs have a fine yellow line along the outer edge.
clue.fi-directional-sign-description: Wayfinding signs have white text and arrows on a solid blue field with a white border.
clue.fi-chevron-description: Curve warning boards are black panels with yellow arrow markings.
clue.fi-wooden-utility-pole-description: Plain timber poles with various top fittings; street lights often mounted directly on them.
clue.fi-lamp-mounting-style-description: Street lamps on wooden poles attach at the top with a double-bolt fixture; lamp arm extends horizontally.
clue.fi-blue-white-signpost-marking-desc: Traffic sign poles often have alternating blue and white bands wrapped around them.
clue.fi-boreal-forest-description: Thick coniferous forests dominated by pine and spruce, with birch trees having bright white bark.
clue.fi-gen-3-autumn-coverage-descriptio: Imagery often shows vivid orange and yellow foliage in autumn.
clue.fi-lake-description: Finland has many lakes appearing frequently across the landscape.
clue.fi-architecture-01-red-houses-descr: Along Sweden and Norway, Finland has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.
clue.fi-bus-stop-sign-description: Two standard designs: blue-and-white and yellow-and-black.
clue.fi-k-market-s-market-description: Two supermarket chains exclusive to Finland with recognisable branding.
clue.fi-regional-road-number-description: Local roads have three- or four-digit numbers; leading digit indicates geographic zone from south (1) to north (9).
clue.fi-lapland-snow-pole-description: Major roads in Lapland have snow poles with two elongated reflectors instead of one.
clue.fi-farmland-distribution-descriptio: Agricultural fields concentrate along western and southern coasts; interior is mostly forested.
clue.fi-wind-turbine-description: Wind farms cluster mainly along the western coastline.
clue.fi-stunted-northern-tree-descriptio: Northern trees are undersized with thin, spindly trunks, showing high-latitude growth.
clue.fi-gen-3-snow-coverage-description: Snow regularly appears only in the extreme northwest corner of Lapland.
clue.fi-swedish-language-area-descriptio: Coastal south and west communities use Swedish extensively, with bilingual Finnish–Swedish signs.
clue.fi-sami-language-description: Far north road signs show Finnish and Sámi names; Sámi includes the letter 'c'.
clue.fi-aland-swedish-only-description: Åland is exclusively Swedish-speaking with no Finnish on signs.
clue.fi-aland-road-feature-description: Åland roads have reddish asphalt and dashed outer lines like Sweden.
clue.fi-aland-licence-plate-description: Åland plates are white with blue text, no EU band, and shorter than Finnish plates.
clue.fi-aland-pedestrian-sign-descriptio: Some Åland crossing signs show four zebra stripes, matching Swedish design.
clue.fi-aland-bus-stop-description: Bus stops have a white plate with a four-digit number, sometimes topped with a semicircle.
clue.fi-helsinki-bus-description: Helsinki city buses are blue and white with a vertical split and operator logos.
clue.fi-country-flag-description: The national flag of Finland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.fr-licence-plate-description: Modern French plates are white rectangles with blue bands on left and right edges.
clue.fr-french-language-description: French uses diacritics like é, à, â, ë, œ, ç and the suffix '-ux'.
clue.fr-pointed-top-bollard-description: White cylindrical bollard tapering to a conical point with a reflector band.
clue.fr-double-band-bollard-description: White round bollard with two indented reflective rings, sometimes green or yellow.
clue.fr-wedge-shaped-bollard-description: Tapered wedge-profile post with broad rectangular white reflectors on both faces.
clue.fr-wooden-octagonal-metal-pole-desc: Rural areas have timber poles alongside slender octagonal metal ones.
clue.fr-french-pole-top-description: Diamond-shaped insulators supporting three wires, known as 'French pole tops', appear most commonly atop ladder poles.
clue.fr-arrowhead-pole-top-description: A variant with insulators on top creating an arrowhead silhouette, found only in France.
clue.fr-road-signs-01-road-numbers-descr: Yellow road signs beginning with “D” are specific to France and are often placed above direction signs or on town entry signs.
clue.fr-directional-sign-description: Local direction signs are white with a thick black border at the arrow point; highways use blue or green backgrounds.
clue.fr-town-entrance-sign-description: Settlements are announced by white signs framed with a red border and thin outer white rim.
clue.fr-road-sign-border-description: Regulatory signs have a red border with a narrow white outline; white sub-signs with black text often attached below.
clue.fr-flat-signpost-description: Traffic signs often mounted on flat rectangular posts; posts and sign backs may be painted in unusual, regionally distinctive colours.
clue.fr-short-signpost-description: Unusually short poles supporting traffic signs at low heights are common across France.
clue.fr-chevron-description: Curve warning boards use white arrows on a blue background, displaying one to five arrows.
clue.fr-pedestrian-sign-description: Crossing signs show a figure with a detached circular head walking over five zebra stripes, enclosed by a white-outline border.
clue.fr-kilometre-marker-description: Distance posts combine a yellow or red semicircle atop a white rectangle; major motorways use square markers topped in red.
clue.fr-dashed-outer-line-description: Edge markings on standard French roads are widely spaced, elongated white dashes.
clue.fr-offset-block-middle-line-descrip: Centre-line dashes formed by two staggered blocks, found only in France.
clue.fr-long-middle-dash-description: Centre line dashes noticeably longer than the European norm can indicate France.
clue.fr-end-passing-zone-arrow-descripti: Painted arrows indicating the end of an overtaking zone, accompanied by tightly spaced centre dashes.
clue.fr-red-white-red-flag-marker-descri: Tall narrow rectangles on sticks painted red-white-red stripes, reminiscent of the Austrian flag, appear on French roads.
clue.fr-architecture-description: Typical French houses are stone, unpainted or pale pastel, with simple gable roofs of orange tiles or dark slate; urban terraced houses line roads.
clue.fr-blue-house-number-description: Address plaques are predominantly blue with serif typeface and ornate numerals.
clue.fr-french-car-brand-description: Peugeot, Renault, and Citroën make up roughly half of all vehicles on the road.
clue.fr-administrative-division-descript: Metropolitan France has 13 regions and 96 departments; department logos appear on public infrastructure.
clue.fr-telephone-area-code-description: Phone numbers are ten digits; first pairs indicate broad zones, with 06–09 for mobile and non-regional.
clue.fr-postal-code-description: Five-digit postal codes start with the department number, also shown on licence plates.
clue.fr-department-logo-description: Nearly every department has a unique logo appearing on bus stops, distance markers, and signs.
clue.fr-occitanie-region-logo-descriptio: A red-and-yellow emblem combining an Occitan cross with vertical stripes identifies Occitanie.
clue.fr-pyrenees-orientales-senyera-flag: Pyrénées-Orientales uses red-and-yellow stripes (Senyera pattern) as its official flag and logo.
clue.fr-red-tinted-road-description: Asphalt with red, purple, or burgundy hues is concentrated between Paris and Dijon, roughly Burgundy.
clue.fr-dark-green-signpost-description: Sign poles and backs painted dark green appear mainly in Brittany, Paris area, and some southern regions.
clue.fr-eure-et-loir-signback-descriptio: In Eure-et-Loir, sign backs may have a green sticker with the department's logo on a dark green backing.
clue.fr-greyish-green-signback-descripti: Muted greyish-green sign backs on darker green posts are found in parts of Brittany, Pyrénées-Atlantiques, and near the Alps.
clue.fr-pas-de-calais-green-sign-descrip: Road signs have dark green posts with lighter green backs from matcha to turquoise. The green-and-blue triangle logo may appear.
clue.fr-brown-signback-description: Signs with brown poles and backs are characteristic of Seine-et-Marne.
clue.fr-paris-metro-street-sign-descript: Street plaques in Paris suburbs often include the municipality name in a modern design.
clue.fr-corsican-stone-barrier-descripti: Blocky crash barriers made from rough stone and mortar are common on Corsica.
clue.fr-topography-description: Highest peaks are in the southeast (Alps) and along the Spanish border (Pyrenees). North and Atlantic coast are flat to rolling; southern interior is hillier.
clue.fr-hedge-lined-road-northwest-descr: Narrow rural lanes hemmed by tall hedges are most common in the northwest, especially Normandy.
clue.fr-stone-pine-description: Umbrella-shaped stone pines line many roads along the Mediterranean coast, sometimes as far north as Nantes.
clue.fr-maritime-pine-forest-southwest-d: Dense maritime pine stands cover the flat Gironde and Landes departments in the southwest.
clue.fr-wine-region-description: Major vineyard regions include Bordeaux, Mediterranean coast, Champagne, Loire Valley, Alsace, and Corsica.
clue.fr-wind-turbine-description: Wind farms are more common in the northern half of France.
clue.fr-black-shingle-roof-description: Slate or dark shingle roofs dominate northwest of the Loire, near the Belgian border, south-centre, and the Pyrenees.
clue.fr-brittany-architecture-descriptio: Dark slate roofs, dark or brown stone walls, and light-coloured rendered buildings are characteristic of Brittany.
clue.fr-southern-rounded-roof-tiles-desc: Roofs in the south have curved overlapping tiles in terracotta to faded orange shades.
clue.fr-flemish-brick-house-north-descri: Rows of dark red brick terraced houses with white mortar joints cluster near the Belgian border.
clue.fr-paris-surroundings-stone-wall-de: Walls of rough cream-to-orange stones with red brick accents characterize towns around Paris.
clue.fr-french-riviera-description: Palm-lined avenues and pale multi-storey buildings with balconies typify the Côte d'Azur and southern coast.
clue.fr-basque-timber-framed-house-descr: White walls with bold, colorful timber framing matching shutters and gates are hallmarks of the Basque region.
clue.fr-alpine-architecture-description: Light masonry ground floors with large wooden upper storeys and balconies are typical in eastern mountain valleys.
clue.fr-alsace-germanic-architecture-des: Half-timbered facades, half-hip roofs, and fish-scale roof tiles are concentrated in Alsace.
clue.fr-minority-language-overview-descr: Six minority languages are regionally significant: Alsatian, Basque, Breton, Catalan, Corsican, and Occitan.
clue.fr-breton-language-description: A Celtic tongue with letters d, k, w, and ñ; 'straed' means street; bilingual signs reach east to Rennes.
clue.fr-plou-town-prefix-description: Place names starting with 'Plou-' cluster in northwest Brittany.
clue.fr-alsatian-language-description: An Alemannic German dialect in Alsace; bilingual signs use 'gasse' or 'strasse'.
clue.fr-occitan-language-description: A Romance language in southern France; street is 'carrièra' in Toulouse, 'carriero' in Avignon.
clue.fr-french-basque-language-descripti: Basque appears on bilingual signs near the Spanish border; street is 'karrika'.
clue.fr-corsican-language-description: A Romance language with Italian roots; words often end in vowels like -u, -iu, -ju.
clue.fr-catalan-pyrenees-orientales-desc: Catalan signage in Pyrénées-Orientales; frequent cedilla (Ç); street is 'carrer'.
clue.fr-town-name-suffixes-toponymy-desc: Town name endings vary by region and help narrow down locations in France.
clue.fr-river-based-town-name-descriptio: Many towns include a river name in '-sur-[river]' format; coastal towns end in '-sur-mer' or '-plage'.
clue.fr-lavender-field-description: Southeastern France has lavender plantations appearing as rows of small grey-green bushes when not in bloom.
clue.fr-thin-b-type-guardrail-north-desc: Thin guardrails appear on motorways in northern France around Le Mans, Tours, Paris, Reims, and Metz.
clue.fr-country-flag-description: The national flag of France is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.de-german-language-description: Signs are in German, identifiable by Ä, Ö, Ü, and ß characters.
clue.de-white-sticker-wooden-poles-descr: Nearly every wooden utility pole has a small rectangular white sticker on its shaft.
clue.de-diverse-pole-tops-description: Common German pole tops include horizontal crossarms with staggered insulators, inverted-triangle supports, and T-shaped arrangements.
clue.de-dark-sign-backs-description: Road sign backs are often black or dark grey, with a small inverted red triangle sticker on most signs.
clue.de-yellow-h-bus-stops-description: Bus stops feature a yellow-and-green 'H' symbol.
clue.de-high-bollard-density-description: Bollards appear roughly every 50 metres along nearly every road.
clue.de-yellow-town-entry-signs-descript: Town boundaries are marked by yellow signs with black text framed in metal, showing town, municipality, and county.
clue.de-blue-kilometre-markers-descripti: Distance markers are blue rectangles with rounded corners and a thin white border.
clue.de-five-stripe-pedestrian-signs-des: The German pedestrian crossing sign shows a figure walking across five stripes.
clue.de-no-stopping-arrow-signs-descript: No Stopping and No Waiting signs often include white directional arrows on the sign face.
clue.de-phone-area-codes-description: A map of German telephone area codes, useful for narrowing down regions.
clue.de-postal-code-map-description: An overview of German postal code zones, helpful for region guessing when visible on signs or buildings.
clue.de-baden-wuerttemberg-state-flag-de: Horizontal stripes of black and gold (yellow).
clue.de-bavaria-state-flag-description: Horizontal stripes of white and blue.
clue.de-berlin-state-flag-description: Horizontal stripes of red, white, and red with the Berlin bear.
clue.de-brandenburg-state-flag-descripti: Horizontal stripes of red and white with the red eagle.
clue.de-bremen-state-flag-description: Eight horizontal red and white stripes with a chequered pattern.
clue.de-hamburg-state-flag-description: A red flag with a white castle
clue.de-hesse-state-flag-description: Horizontal stripes of red and white.
clue.de-lower-saxony-state-flag-descript: Horizontal stripes of black, red, and gold with a white horse.
clue.de-mecklenburg-vorpommern-state-fla: Horizontal stripes of blue, white, and red with a with a yellow line in the middle. A version includes the region's coat of arms (a bull's head and a red griffin).
clue.de-north-rhine-westphalia-state-fla: Horizontal stripes of green, white, and red.
clue.de-rhineland-palatinate-state-flag-: Horizontal stripes of black, red, and gold with the coat of arms.
clue.de-saarland-state-flag-description: Horizontal stripes of black, red, and gold with the Saarland coat of arms.
clue.de-saxony-state-flag-description: Horizontal stripes of white and green.
clue.de-saxony-anhalt-state-flag-descrip: Horizontal stripes of yellow and black with the coat of arms.
clue.de-schleswig-holstein-state-flag-de: Horizontal stripes of blue, white, and red.
clue.de-thuringia-state-flag-description: Horizontal stripes of white and red.
clue.de-state-coats-arms-description: Each federal state has its own heraldic coat of arms, seen on official buildings or signs.
clue.de-town-name-suffixes-description: Certain place-name endings are concentrated in specific parts of Germany, aiding region guessing.
clue.de-22-bavaria-description: Bavarian cycle route signs have a white background with a bold red border and text, often with a red bicycle symbol and directional arrows.
clue.de-22-north-rhine-westphalia-descri: Cycle route signs have a white background with a red border and text, including a red bicycle symbol and directional arrows.
clue.de-22-saxony-description: Saxony's cycling signs have a white background with a thin green border and green text, sometimes with a green bicycle symbol.
clue.de-22-lower-saxony-description: Lower Saxony cycle route signs are white with a green border and text, featuring a green bicycle symbol and directional arrows.
clue.de-22-schleswig-holstein-descriptio: Cycle route signs have a white background, green border, green text, and a green bicycle symbol.
clue.de-22-brandenburg-description: Cycle route signs have a white background, red border, red text, and a red bicycle symbol.
clue.de-23-bavaria-description: Street sign backs are folded with ribbed edges, giving a reinforced, corrugated look.
clue.de-23-north-rhine-westphalia-title: North Rhine-Westphalia Flat Street Sign Backs
clue.de-23-north-rhine-westphalia-descri: Street sign backs are completely flat and smooth metal.
clue.de-23-saxony-description: Street sign backs are folded or ribbed with bent or reinforced edges.
clue.de-23-lower-saxony-title: Lower Saxony Flat Street Sign Backs
clue.de-23-lower-saxony-description: Street sign backs are flat, smooth metal with no ribbing or folding.
clue.de-23-schleswig-holstein-descriptio: Street sign backs are flat and smooth without ribbed or folded reinforcement.
clue.de-23-brandenburg-description: Street sign backs are folded or ribbed with visibly bent or reinforced edges.
clue.de-24-bavaria-description: Road signs attach to posts with a single, slim vertical metal bar down the center.
clue.de-24-north-rhine-westphalia-title: North Rhine-Westphalia Double Bar Sign Connector
clue.de-24-north-rhine-westphalia-descri: Road signs attach with two parallel vertical metal bars for a wider, robust look.
clue.de-24-saxony-description: Road signs feature a T-shaped metal bracket with a horizontal bar atop a vertical bar.
clue.de-24-lower-saxony-title: Lower Saxony Double Bar Sign Connector
clue.de-24-lower-saxony-description: Road signs attach with two vertical metal bars, sometimes with narrower spacing.
clue.de-24-schleswig-holstein-descriptio: Road signs mount with a single, central vertical metal bar.
clue.de-24-brandenburg-description: Road signs use a T-shaped metal bracket with horizontal and vertical bars for mounting.
clue.de-german-alps-description: The most mountainous terrain lies along the southern border with Austria.
clue.de-baltic-pines-description: Scots pines with orange-toned bark concentrate in the northeastern states.
clue.de-white-painted-tree-trunks-descri: Roadside trees have lower trunks painted white, mainly in the northeast.
clue.de-vineyard-regions-description: Most vineyards cluster in the southwest, with some pockets further east.
clue.de-northwestern-brick-houses-descri: Exposed red or brown brick houses concentrate in the northwest.
clue.de-thatched-roofs-rock-walls-descri: Straw-thatched roofs and dry-stone walls are common in North Frisian Islands and Schleswig-Holstein.
clue.de-black-slate-fish-scale-walls-des: Building façades clad in overlapping black slate tiles resembling fish scales are widespread in central Germany.
clue.de-east-german-socialist-housing-de: Large prefabricated apartment slabs from the socialist period mark former East German states.
clue.de-dark-reflector-bollard-descripti: Bollards with noticeably darker reflectors appear in certain regions.
clue.de-nrw-green-cap-bollard-descriptio: Some bollards have coloured plastic caps, mostly green, in North Rhine-Westphalia.
clue.de-lvr-branded-green-cap-descriptio: Green bollard caps stamped with 'LVR' and a coat of arms appear in southern North Rhine-Westphalia.
clue.de-bavarian-wooden-bollard-descript: Cylindrical timber bollards with painted tips are a Bavarian speciality.
clue.de-orange-road-post-description: Plain orange marker posts are common in Bavaria and some other states.
clue.de-green-tree-marker-description: Miniature green tags nailed to roadside trees are typical of Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
clue.de-bavaria-three-section-road-marke: White rectangular plaques divided into three panels, with the left panel showing the current road, are specific to Bavaria.
clue.de-lower-saxony-rectangular-marker-: Unadorned rectangular road markers with softly rounded corners appear in Lower Saxony.
clue.de-metallic-border-road-marker-desc: Road markers surrounded by a thin metal frame occur in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony.
clue.de-45-rhineland-palatinate-descript: Triangular rough, unpainted stone posts topped with a white plate.
clue.de-45-saxony-description: Triangular rough, unpainted stone posts with a white plate attached.
clue.de-45-saarland-description: Triangular marker posts fully painted white, sometimes with a white plate.
clue.de-45-thuringia-description: Triangular roadside posts painted entirely white, sometimes with a white plate.
clue.de-45-baden-w-rttemberg-title: Baden-Württemberg Short White or Grey Triangular Posts
clue.de-45-baden-w-rttemberg-description: Short triangular posts usually white, sometimes grey, sometimes with a white plate.
clue.de-45-north-rhine-westphalia-title: North Rhine-Westphalia White Triangular Posts Without Plates
clue.de-45-north-rhine-westphalia-descri: Triangular roadside posts painted fully white without any plates.
clue.de-white-bollard-plate-description: Simple white information plates mounted on bollards in certain states.
clue.de-black-disk-bollard-base-descript: Bollards atop round black base disks typical of former East German states.
clue.de-rhineland-palatinate-orange-plat: Information plates on bollards are orange instead of white in Rhineland-Palatinate.
clue.de-baden-wuerttemberg-grey-plate-de: Bollard information plates may be grey instead of white in Baden-Württemberg.
clue.de-red-capped-white-post-descriptio: Slim white posts topped with a red cap, common in former East Germany, especially Saxony-Anhalt.
clue.de-fully-yellow-post-description: Solid yellow marker posts specific to Brandenburg.
clue.de-yellow-post-white-plate-descript: Yellow posts with attached white information plates indicate Saxony-Anhalt.
clue.de-east-german-round-concrete-pole-: Cylindrical concrete utility poles mainly found in former East Germany.
clue.de-trident-pole-top-description: Three-pronged pole-top assemblies in Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt, and Baden-Württemberg.
clue.de-triangle-pole-top-description: Inverted-triangle pole-top braces concentrated in western Germany.
clue.de-thick-centre-bar-pole-top-descri: Pole tops with a bulging horizontal crossarm midpoint in former East German states.
clue.de-curved-bar-pole-top-description: Pole-top crossarms that arc gently, a Bavaria-specific feature.
clue.de-aldi-nord-vs-aldi-sued-descripti: Germany is split between Aldi Süd in the south and Aldi Nord in the north, each with distinct branding.
clue.de-sorbian-language-sign-descriptio: Bilingual signs featuring Sorbian appear near the Polish and Czech borders.
clue.de-saxony-half-timbered-arch-house-: Half-timbered houses with arched ground-floor openings concentrated in Saxony.
clue.de-country-flag-description: The national flag of Germany is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-general-01-20-green-sticker-desc: In Germany, most cars have a green circular sticker on the bottom right of the windshield.
clue.gh-misc-01-ghana-tape-description: One of the most (in)famous hints in Geoguessr is the tape on the top-right bar that can be seen when looking down. It can only be found in Ghana.
clue.gh-white-road-line-description: Where present, road markings are always white; many paved roads lack markings.
clue.gh-wooden-pole-description: Utility poles are timber posts with metal crossbars carrying three porcelain insulators.
clue.gh-national-flag-colour-description: Kerbs, poles, and fences are often painted red, gold, and green, sometimes with the black star from the flag.
clue.gh-striped-signpost-description: Traffic sign poles have alternating black-and-white bands in urban areas; plain metal posts in the countryside.
clue.gh-paved-vs-unpaved-road-descriptio: Map showing which roads are surfaced and which are dirt tracks across Ghana.
clue.gh-northern-savannah-description: Northern Ghana features savannah with open grassland, sparser trees, and drier, paler soil.
clue.gh-mountain-range-lake-volta-descri: Hill and mountain ranges are concentrated around Lake Volta.
clue.gh-dense-forest-description: Thick tropical forest with abundant palms is found in southwest and eastern Ghana.
clue.gh-coastal-palm-tree-description: Tall palms line much of the coastline, especially along the western shore.
clue.gh-east-accra-coast-description: The coastal strip east of Accra along the N1 is flat, open, and sparsely vegetated, appearing almost arid.
clue.gh-nature-reserve-car-description: Several nature reserves use a different Google vehicle, white with visible side mirrors, though the characteristic Ghana roof-rack tape remains in place.
clue.gh-country-flag-description: The national flag of Ghana is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.gi-yellow-rear-licence-plate-descri: Vehicles display yellow rear plates, matching the UK system.
clue.gi-english-language-description: English is the primary language on official signage in a Mediterranean coastal setting.
clue.gi-mediterranean-architecture-descr: Dense pastel-coloured buildings with louvred window shutters, usually painted green, blue, or brown.
clue.gi-christmas-decoration-description: Street View coverage was captured in December, showing festive Christmas decorations throughout the town.
clue.gi-barbary-macaque-description: Wild Barbary macaques roam the Rock, the only free-living monkey population in Europe.
clue.gi-country-flag-description: The national flag of Gibraltar is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.gr-greek-alphabet-description: Greek is written in its distinctive script with rounder, softer lowercase forms.
clue.gr-harp-shaped-pole-top-description: Many Greek utility poles have a metal frame resembling a harp atop them.
clue.gr-five-vertical-insulator-descript: Five insulators arranged vertically, bolted to the pole or harp-shaped frames.
clue.gr-round-shade-pole-lamp-descriptio: Compact lamps fixed to poles, capped by a circular shade over the bulb.
clue.xx-general-01-24-double-white-lines: You will often see worn double white center lines in Greece.
clue.gr-yellow-road-marking-description: Yellow road lines appear frequently in Greece.
clue.gr-chevron-sign-description: Curve warning boards display white arrows on a black field.
clue.gr-warning-sign-description: Triangular hazard signs have a red border with a yellow interior.
clue.gr-town-entry-sign-description: Settlement entrance boards are white with bold blue horizontal bands at top and bottom.
clue.gr-kilometre-marker-description: Small blue roadside posts show 'km' in Greek and Latin alphabets with the distance.
clue.gr-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Pedestrian figures walk across two horizontal dotted lines.
clue.gr-miniature-roadside-shrine-descri: Tiny church-like structures on pedestals appear frequently alongside roads.
clue.gr-architecture-description: Stone buildings with white or pastel walls and orange tile roofs; islands feature white walls with blue doors and windows.
clue.gr-mountainous-terrain-description: Greece is heavily mountainous with narrow, twisting highland roads.
clue.gr-red-soil-description: Exposed red-tinted earth is widespread in the landscape.
clue.gr-generation-3-winter-autumn-cover: Imagery often shows dull, grey, overcast winter and autumn scenes.
clue.gr-island-coverage-map-description: Numerous small islands with limited Street View; mainland and Crete have more coverage.
clue.gr-phone-area-code-description: Landline numbers start with 2, followed by region-indicating digits.
clue.gr-flat-agricultural-valley-descrip: Broad lowland plains around Thessaloniki and Larissa; smaller valleys scattered in north and central mainland.
clue.gr-western-mountain-description: Highest peaks and most high-altitude roads are in the western mainland.
clue.gr-cycladic-white-blue-house-descri: White-walled buildings with blue doors and shutters are found on central Cycladic islands.
clue.gr-barren-central-island-descriptio: Smaller central islands have arid, treeless terrain with low scrub and bare rock.
clue.gr-olive-grove-description: Olive cultivation is concentrated along the coast, especially Crete and southern Peloponnese.
clue.gr-citrus-orchard-description: Citrus farming centers in coastal lowlands, mainly southern Peloponnese.
clue.gr-thessaloniki-taxi-description: Thessaloniki taxis have blue bodies with white roofs.
clue.gr-country-flag-description: The national flag of Greece is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.gl-coverage-overview-description: Street View in Greenland is fragmented into many isolated pockets along the southern western coastline, each with distinctive vehicles, weather, and terrain.
clue.gl-unusual-street-view-vehicle-desc: Each location features its own quirky vehicle, from red tractors to snowmobiles with large boxes.
clue.gl-white-cabin-red-roof-boat-west-c: A boat with a white cabin topped by a red roof appears at numerous west-coast towns, mainly around Aasiaat.
clue.gl-red-square-cabin-boat-west-coast: A vessel with a distinctive red square-shaped cabin visits several west-coast settlements, densest near Akunnaaq.
clue.gl-black-box-boat-northern-east-coa: A boat with a black box near the bow and a chequered pattern navigates the northern east coast.
clue.gl-bright-red-boat-east-coast-descr: A vivid red boat operates near two east-coast settlements: off Tiilerilaaq and Kuummiit.
clue.gl-country-flag-description: The national flag of Greenland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.gu-tropical-vegetation-description: Guam has thick, low-growing tropical vegetation.
clue.gu-east-asian-russian-signage-descr: Commercial signs often feature Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and Russian text.
clue.gu-hilly-south-description: The southern part of Guam is hillier and more rugged.
clue.gu-flat-north-description: Northern Guam is mostly flat and low-lying.
clue.gu-country-flag-description: The national flag of Guam is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.gt-tropical-rainforest-description: Much of the terrain is dense tropical rainforest.
clue.gt-architecture-description: Stone buildings painted pastel with corrugated metal or white cinder-block walls.
clue.gt-road-marking-description: Solid white edge lines with a single yellow centre line; markings are thinner than Mexico's.
clue.gt-topography-description: A central mountainous belt with flat terrain to the south and north.
clue.gt-flat-southern-farmland-descripti: Southern lowlands are flat agricultural land, more developed than northern flat areas.
clue.gt-central-highlands-description: The middle band is dominated by mountainous terrain.
clue.gt-gently-rolling-north-description: Northern Guatemala has gentle hills and undulating ground.
clue.gt-oil-palm-plantation-description: Oil palm cultivation is in the southwest coast and north of the central mountains.
clue.gt-solid-green-utility-pole-descrip: Poles painted entirely green appear mainly in the southeast and scattered eastern areas.
clue.gt-pole-plate-route-code-descriptio: Many green poles have a white plate with the first two characters indicating the road.
clue.gt-forward-facing-roof-bar-descript: Most Guatemalan cars have an upper-right roof bar angled toward the front.
clue.gt-backward-facing-roof-bar-southea: In southeastern Guatemala, the upper-right roof bar points toward the rear.
clue.gt-blue-rope-lower-bar-description: Backward-bar regions often have a blue rope wrapped around the lower-right roof bar.
