clue.gt-missing-black-bar-cap-descriptio: Some southern and far northeast areas have backward-facing bars without a black cap.
clue.gt-phone-code-6-guatemala-departmen: Numbers starting with 6 belong to the Guatemala Department.
clue.gt-country-flag-description: The national flag of Guatemala is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ha-licence-plate-description: Hawaiian plates are white with an arched rainbow; front plates are mandatory.
clue.ha-hawaiian-language-description: Hawaiian place names appear on signs, using eight consonants and vowel endings.
clue.ha-lush-tropical-vegetation-descrip: Dense tropical greenery lines Hawaiian roadsides.
clue.ha-volcanic-topography-description: Hawaiian terrain features volcano-shaped slopes, cliffs, valleys, and craters.
clue.ha-architecture-description: Homes are light-coloured wooden structures with dark volcanic rock retaining walls.
clue.ha-yellow-pole-band-description: Some Hawaiian utility poles have wide yellow bands painted around them.
clue.ha-guitar-pick-highway-shield-descr: State highway markers are guitar pick-shaped with yellow-painted posts.
clue.ha-raised-pavement-marker-pattern-d: Hawaiian road reflectors follow a pattern: one, four close, then one again.
clue.ha-kauai-description: Kauai has deep red earth, steep hills, and dense jungle-like growth.
clue.ha-oahu-description: Oʻahu features steep green hills visible from suburban areas.
clue.ha-molokai-description: Molokaʻi has vivid red soil, dry vegetation, and a prominent eastern volcano.
clue.ha-lanai-coastal-description: Lānaʻi's coast is hilly with dry grass and scrubby bushes, few buildings.
clue.ha-maui-central-isthmus-description: Maui's central valley is dry grassland between two mountain ranges.
clue.ha-maui-coastal-area-description: Maui's coast is greener with banana plants, palms, and mountain backdrops.
clue.ha-big-island-interior-description: Big Island's interior has grassy plains with lava rock and volcanic summits.
clue.ha-big-island-coastal-description: Big Island's coast is lusher with trees and ferns; towns are mostly here.
clue.hk-licence-plate-description: Front plates in Hong Kong are white and rear plates are yellow..
clue.hk-dense-urban-skyline-description: A tightly packed metropolis with modern towers and bustling streets crowded with traffic and pedestrians.
clue.hk-green-mountainous-hinterland-des: Hilly subtropical greenery beyond the urban core with roads extending into rural highlands.
clue.hk-exterior-air-conditioner-descrip: Wall-mounted air-conditioning units are ubiquitous on apartment buildings.
clue.hk-grey-lamp-post-wide-base-title: Grey Lamp Posts with Wide Base
clue.hk-grey-lamp-post-wide-base-descrip: Cylindrical grey street lamps flaring at the base, often with a small white sticker.
clue.hk-rural-wooden-utility-pole-descri: Round timber utility poles appear only in rural areas, often carrying meters or transformers.
clue.hk-no-striped-kerb-description: Painted kerb stripes are virtually absent; grey pedestrian guardrails are common instead.
clue.hk-yellow-pedestrian-crossing-descr: Crosswalks and some junctions feature yellow paint markings.
clue.hk-road-marking-description: White centre lines; white or yellow edge lines; concrete road surfaces common.
clue.hk-bilingual-road-sign-description: White rectangular directional signs with thick black border and English and Chinese text.
clue.hk-give-way-sign-description: Inverted white triangle with heavy red border and bilingual give-way text.
clue.hk-mountainside-retaining-wall-desc: Exposed weathered rock faces along hillside roads, sometimes with wire netting and small plaques.
clue.hk-fire-hydrant-description: Typically red with domed top and three outlets; shape is a reliable identifier.
clue.hk-yellow-traffic-bollard-descripti: Yellow posts topped with blue circle and white directional arrow at crossings and lane dividers.
clue.hk-bright-orange-litter-bin-descrip: Vivid orange waste bins stand on pavements throughout the territory.
clue.hk-double-decker-bus-description: Most public buses are double-deckers with various color schemes; minibuses have green or red roofs.
clue.hk-boxy-village-house-description: Low-rise, boxy multi-storey houses typical of small villages in the northern New Territories.
clue.hk-mong-kok-surrounding-kowloon-des: Dense grid-pattern streets with older apartment blocks above ground-floor shops.
clue.hk-northwestern-rice-paddies-descri: Flat lowlands near the China border with waterlogged rice fields and Shenzhen skyline visible.
clue.hk-caribbean-coast-tung-chung-descr: Matching residential towers forming a wall-like facade with palm trees lining the streets.
clue.hk-country-flag-description: The national flag of Hong Kong is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.hu-licence-plate-description: Elongated white EU-format plates; taxis have yellow, electric vehicles green plates.
clue.hu-chevron-sign-description: Curve warning boards with white arrows on red; less common black on white variant.
clue.h-general-01-street-signs-descripti: Street names in Hungary usually end with the word "utca".
clue.hu-green-kilometre-marker-descripti: In Hungary, small green kilometre markers are common along the roads.
clue.hu-very-tall-sign-post-description: Road sign poles are unusually tall, often taller than the Street View camera.
clue.hu-four-bolt-sign-mounting-descript: Signs fastened with four bolts in a tall rectangular pattern.
clue.hu-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Hungarian pedestrian crossing signs have a walking figure with a belt low on the body crossing five zebra stripes.
clue.hu-road-number-shield-description: Hungarian routes use green signs; M motorways use blue, both with compact shield-shaped emblems.
clue.hu-green-directional-sign-descripti: Destination boards are green with a thin white inner border; motorways use the same layout on blue.
clue.hu-gen-3-winter-coverage-descriptio: Imagery was captured during colder months, showing grey, leafless scenes.
clue.hu-architecture-description: Suburbs have pale stone or rendered single-storey houses with red clay tiles; central districts have older multi-storey buildings.
clue.hu-yellow-bicycle-lane-line-descrip: Road markings are white except bicycle lane lines, which are yellow.
clue.hu-phone-area-code-description: Landline area codes are two digits; Budapest's code is 1.
clue.hu-road-number-system-description: Route numbers radiate clockwise from Budapest, indicating direction from the capital.
clue.hu-town-name-prefix-description: Many settlement names have distinctive prefixes that narrow down the region.
clue.hu-metal-framed-street-sign-descrip: Street name plates with thick metal borders are typical in western Hungary.
clue.hu-arrow-shaped-street-sign-descrip: Blue or green arrow-shaped name plates on utility poles indicate Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg county in the northeast.
clue.hu-flat-southeast-farmland-descript: Southeastern Hungary is flat agricultural land with wide open fields.
clue.hu-northern-western-hills-descripti: Forested hills and low mountains cover northern and western Hungary, with tallest peaks along the northern border.
clue.hu-puszta-grassland-description: Flat, marshy natural grasslands around Hortobágy National Park, left wild and often waterlogged.
clue.hu-tornanadaska-snowy-road-descript: Road east of Tornanadaska with persistent snow, roadside bollards, and a parallel railway line.
clue.hu-country-flag-description: The national flag of Hungary is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ic-licence-plate-description: Plain white plates with blue lettering, no blue EU-style strip.
clue.ic-yellow-bollard-description: Yellow delineator posts with a single white reflector on most rural roads.
clue.ic-barren-treeless-landscape-descri: Countryside lacks trees, covered by dark grey volcanic soil.
clue.ic-volcanic-geology-description: Landscape shaped by tectonic and volcanic forces: rugged peaks, geothermal pools, lava fields, rift valleys, and rock pillars.
clue.ic-yellow-directional-sign-descript: Destination boards have yellow backgrounds with a white inset panel showing route numbers.
clue.ic-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Pedestrian figure crosses four zebra stripes; sign background often has a faint yellow tinge.
clue.ic-icelandic-language-description: Features letters ð (Ð), þ, æ, and accented vowels á, é, í, ó, ö, ú, ý.
clue.ic-street-name-sign-description: White plates with black text, often edged by a thin metal rim, mounted on lamp posts or traffic-light poles.
clue.ic-all-white-road-marking-descripti: All road markings—centre lines, edge lines, lane dividers—are white.
clue.ic-chevron-sign-description: Curve warning boards show yellow arrows on a black field.
clue.ic-yellow-warning-sign-description: Hazard signs use a yellow background.
clue.ic-road-numbering-system-descriptio: Route 1 is a ring road; other routes start with digits 2–9 assigned clockwise by region.
clue.ic-westfjords-description: Narrow fjords surrounded by moderately high, flat-topped mountains.
clue.ic-eastfjords-description: Eastern coast fjords with taller, more rugged mountains than the Westfjords.
clue.ic-northern-valleys-west-akureyri-d: Valleys between tall, often snow-dusted peaks opening north to northeast.
clue.ic-inland-volcanic-desert-descripti: Desolate dark volcanic gravel expanses with almost no plant life in eastern interior highlands.
clue.ic-southwest-agricultural-lowland-d: A broad, level farming area with farmsteads, meadows, and pastures. Surrounding mountains appear unusually distant.
clue.ic-reykjavik-description: The capital sits on the southern shore of a bay, on mostly flat ground with gentle hills and a large urban footprint.
clue.ic-akureyri-description: Iceland's second city occupies a north–south valley along the western shore of a bay, flanked by mountain ranges.
clue.ic-southern-coast-glacier-descripti: Tongues of ice from the Vatnajökull ice cap spill down towards the sea along the southern coastline.
clue.ic-divided-multi-lane-highway-descr: Dual carriageways and roads wider than two lanes are rare, mostly around Reykjavík and near major intersections.
clue.ic-country-flag-description: The national flag of Iceland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.is-volcanic-geology-description: A dramatic landscape of rugged peaks, geothermal pools, lava fields, rift valleys, and rock pillars shaped by tectonic and volcanic forces.
clue.is-yellow-directional-sign-descript: Road destination boards have a yellow background with a white inset panel showing the route number.
clue.xx-general-01-44-pedestrian-crossin: In Iceland, you will see pedestrian crossing signs with four stripes at the bottom and a subtle yellow hue.
clue.is-street-name-sign-description: White plates with black text, often edged by a thin metal rim, mounted on lamp posts or traffic-light poles.
clue.is-all-white-road-marking-descripti: All road markings in Iceland are white.
clue.is-chevron-sign-description: Curve warning boards show yellow arrows on a black field.
clue.is-yellow-warning-sign-description: Warning signs in Iceland use a yellow background.
clue.is-road-numbering-system-descriptio: Route 1 is the ring road; other routes start with digits 2–9 corresponding to regions clockwise from the south.
clue.is-westfjords-description: Narrow fjords hemmed by moderately high mountains with flat summits.
clue.is-eastfjords-description: Eastern fjords with taller, more rugged flanking mountains.
clue.is-northern-valley-west-akureyri-de: Multiple valleys between tall, often snow-dusted peaks opening north to northeast.
clue.is-inland-volcanic-desert-descripti: Desolate dark volcanic gravel expanses with virtually no plant life.
clue.is-southwest-agricultural-lowland-d: Broad farming area with farmsteads, meadows, and distant surrounding mountains.
clue.is-reykjavik-description: Capital on the southern shore of a bay, mostly flat with gentle hills and a large urban footprint.
clue.is-25-rang-r-ing-eystra-description: Street View coverage uses bright red pickup trucks distinctive to southwestern Iceland.
clue.is-25-rang-r-ing-ytra-description: Street View coverage uses bright red pickup trucks distinctive to southwestern Iceland.
clue.is-25-keflav-k-description: Street View imagery collected using bright red pickup trucks specific to southwestern Iceland.
clue.is-25-reykjanesb-r-description: Street View coverage uses bright red pickup trucks exclusive to southwestern Iceland.
clue.is-25-northeastern-region-descripti: Street View imagery uses white pickup trucks unique to northeastern Iceland.
clue.is-southern-coast-glacier-descripti: Ice tongues from Vatnajökull ice cap spill down to the sea along the southern coast.
clue.is-divided-multi-lane-highway-descr: Dual carriageways and roads wider than two lanes are rare, mostly around Reykjavík.
clue.is-country-flag-description: The national flag of Iceland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.in-regional-scripts-description: Distinct writing systems help narrow down the state or region in India.
clue.in-licence-plate-description: Indian plates are usually white; yellow plates are commercial vehicles, green plates are electric vehicles.
clue.in-black-white-striped-signposts-de: Road signposts in India are painted in alternating black and white stripes.
clue.in-utility-poles-description: Indian utility poles are concrete square columns topped with a trident-shaped fixture.
clue.in-marathi-script-description: Marathi in Maharashtra uses Devanagari script, distinguished by the character ळ.
clue.in-punjabi-gurmukhi-script-descript: Gurmukhi script in Punjab has rounder letters and a broken horizontal bar, with key letters like ਨ, ਲ, and ਅ.
clue.in-gujarati-script-description: Gujarati script lacks the horizontal line across the top of words found in Hindi.
clue.in-bengali-script-description: Bengali script features many left-pointing triangular forms within its characters.
clue.in-assamese-script-description: Assamese script, based on Bengali, includes unique characters like ৰ and ৱ.
clue.in-kannada-script-description: Kannada script has flowing curves, small circles, and wavy tails on many characters.
clue.in-telugu-script-description: Telugu script resembles Kannada but has checkmark-style diacritics above letters.
clue.in-tamil-script-description: Tamil script blends curves, straight strokes, right angles, and dot-shaped diacritics.
clue.in-oriya-script-description: Oriya script is rounded with broad semi-circular arcs and sweeping curve diacritics.
clue.in-malayalam-script-description: Malayalam features smoothly rounded characters with inverted U-shaped forms.
clue.in-manipuri-meitei-script-descripti: Meitei script has many vertical strokes and sharp right-angled forms.
clue.in-mizo-language-latin-script-descr: Mizo is commonly written in Latin script in Mizoram.
clue.in-english-only-meghalaya-descripti: Meghalaya signage is almost entirely in English with no local script.
clue.in-yellow-black-tuk-tuks-descriptio: Yellow tuk tuks with black rooftops indicate Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, or Tamil Nadu.
clue.in-gujarat-concrete-holey-poles-des: Concrete utility poles with holes appear only in Gujarat and nearby union territories.
clue.in-two-section-poles-description: Utility poles split into two segments are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
clue.in-sikkim-mesh-poles-description: Metallic lattice mesh utility poles are typical of Sikkim.
clue.in-kerala-metal-holey-poles-descrip: Perforated metal utility poles are widespread in Kerala.
clue.in-thin-grey-metal-poles-descriptio: Slender grey metal poles, often in pairs, are common in northeastern states and Himalayan zones.
clue.in-punjab-mint-green-electricity-co: Mint green electricity meter boxes with small square windows signal Punjab.
clue.in-window-shaped-pole-tops-descript: Compact metal pole tops shaped like window frames are typical of Punjab and Haryana.
clue.in-karnataka-trident-pole-tops-desc: Poles with a top central insulator and two lower ones are typical of Karnataka.
clue.in-manipur-metal-trident-poles-desc: Metal poles topped with a trident arrangement are exclusive to Manipur.
clue.in-inverted-triangle-pole-tops-desc: Upside-down triangular attachments beneath pole tops are common in Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.
clue.in-madhya-pradesh-inverted-a-poles-: Metal brackets shaped like upside-down A's below pole tops are specific to Madhya Pradesh.
clue.in-trapezoid-pole-connector-descrip: Inverted trapezoid connectors link crossbars to poles, mainly in Chhattisgarh.
clue.in-west-bengal-rectangle-pole-tops-: Pole tops with tall, narrow rectangular frames are characteristic of West Bengal.
clue.in-west-bengal-double-crossbar-pole: Poles with two horizontal crossbars joined by vertical supports are seen in West Bengal.
clue.in-northeast-even-uneven-pole-tops-: A distinctive pole arrangement with one even and one uneven crossbar top on the same pole in northeastern states.
clue.in-chevron-shaped-pole-attachment-d: Diagonal bars in a '<' shape on poles, common in Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh.
clue.in-assam-meghalaya-double-crossbar-: Poles with two crossbars and two insulators each, found in Assam, Meghalaya, and Mizoram.
clue.in-assam-bent-trident-poles-descrip: Trident-style pole top with the centre prong bent at a right angle, exclusive to Assam.
clue.in-goa-stacked-crossbar-poles-descr: A shorter crossbar above a longer one on the same pole, specific to Goa.
clue.in-tamil-nadu-pole-tree-markings-de: A black stripe flanked by two white stripes painted on poles and tree trunks, indicating Tamil Nadu.
clue.in-delhi-pole-stripes-description: Poles marked with five or more narrow alternating black and yellow bands, typical of Delhi.
clue.in-bihar-pole-stripes-description: Poles with four broader black and yellow bands, distinctive to Bihar.
clue.in-bihar-red-white-tree-paint-title: Bihar Red and White Tree Paint
clue.in-bihar-red-white-tree-paint-descr: Tree trunks painted with four alternating red and white stripes near the base, mainly in Bihar.
clue.in-kerala-yellow-pole-markings-desc: Compact yellow markings on utility poles, common in Kerala.
clue.in-central-india-rounded-roof-tiles: Semi-cylindrical clay tiles laid in irregular rows on rooftops can be found across central India.
clue.in-southern-india-flat-orange-roof-: Southern India Flat Orange Roof Tiles
Vivid orange flat tiles with a central ridge, prevalent in Tamil Nadu.
clue.in-west-bengal-diamond-protrusion-r: Flat roofing tiles with a small diamond-shaped raised element at the centre, typical of West Bengal.
clue.in-west-bengal-large-metal-hip-roof: West Bengal Large Metal Hip Roofs
Broad hip-style roofs made from corrugated metal sheeting in West Bengal and nearby areas.
clue.in-northeast-metal-roofs-triangle-d: Sheet metal roofs with a small triangular detail near the apex, widespread in Northeast India.
clue.in-northeast-square-panel-houses-de: Houses built from square wall panels divided by slender beams, characteristic of Northeast India.
clue.in-thatched-roof-huts-description: Thatched huts along the eastern coast and northern plains, using hay or dried palm fan leaves.
clue.in-sikh-gurdwaras-punjab-descriptio: Temples with white domed roofs, decorated walls, and the Khanda emblem, concentrated in Punjab.
clue.in-wealthy-homes-goa-kerala-title: Wealthy Homes in Goa and Kerala
clue.in-wealthy-homes-goa-kerala-descrip: Modern, affluent residential architecture common in prosperous Goa and Kerala.
clue.in-chir-pines-description: Trees with smooth conical or spherical canopies of long needles, found in Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and western Arunachal Pradesh.
clue.in-khasi-pines-description: Pines with long needles and irregular, rough crowns, growing in Meghalaya and Manipur.
clue.in-euphorbia-cacti-fences-descripti: Hedgerows of Euphorbia neriifolia cacti used as natural fencing in Gujarat, western Maharashtra, and southern Rajasthan.
clue.in-palmyra-palms-description: Tall palms with spherical fan-leaf canopies, common in southern and eastern India.
clue.in-areca-palms-description: Slender-trunk palms with compact crowns along the southwestern coast, northeastern states, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
clue.in-date-palms-description: Typical palms of the arid central interior where tropical palms are scarce.
clue.in-oil-palm-plantations-description: Primarily in Andhra Pradesh's narrow panhandle near the eastern Telangana border.
clue.in-tea-plantations-description: Located in northeastern states and the far southern hills.
clue.in-sugarcane-description: Grown mainly in northern Uttar Pradesh and parts of the southwest.
clue.in-cotton-description: Cultivated across western India, especially Gujarat and Maharashtra.
clue.in-canola-description: Grown chiefly in and around Rajasthan.
clue.in-himalayan-mountains-description: India's tallest mountain range, towering over all other terrain.
clue.xx-general-01-11-dry-landscape-desc: Some parts of the northern Himalayan region administered by India are known for dry, high altitude landscapes with very little vegetation.
clue.in-northern-plains-ganges-valley-de: Vast flat farmland with highly fertile soil in the Ganges Valley.
clue.in-maharashtra-dark-soil-descriptio: Dark-coloured earth concentrated in Maharashtra and nearby areas.
clue.in-red-soil-description: Red soil along the southern west coast and Chhattisgarh–western Odisha corridor.
clue.in-western-rajasthan-desert-descrip: Arid, sandy terrain dominating western Rajasthan.
clue.in-western-ghats-ridgelines-descrip: Flat, plateau-like ridges in western Maharashtra, drier in the north and greener in the south.
clue.in-mizoram-green-valleys-descriptio: Deep green valleys with low vegetation, flanked by eroded hills and small peaks.
clue.in-northeast-wooden-stick-fences-de: Rustic fences of thin wooden sticks woven into a square grid, common in northeastern states.
clue.in-buddhist-prayer-flags-descriptio: Colourful prayer flags visible in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.
clue.in-andaman-nicobar-pole-stickers-de: Dark stickers with digits and a central arrow on utility poles, unique to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
clue.in-elevated-railways-description: Above-ground metro and rail lines in major cities like Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, and Mumbai.
clue.in-grey-brick-roofs-telangana-karna: Rooftops of thin grey stone or brick slabs, with similar grey rock in walls and stockyards on the Telangana/Karnataka border.
clue.in-white-clay-huts-bihar-up-descrip: Mud-walled huts coated in white paint in northwest Bihar and northeast Uttar Pradesh.
clue.in-central-bihar-cross-pattern-huts: Timber-framed huts with criss-cross lattice walls in central Bihar.
clue.in-japanese-cedar-trees-description: Tall trees with slender, bushy canopies near the Sikkim-West Bengal boundary and Meghalaya.
clue.in-barren-western-uttarakhand-descr: Hillsides northwest of Dehradun are stripped of vegetation due to deforestation and erosion.
clue.in-gujarat-salt-flat-description: Expansive salt pans and coastal marshlands with little plant life and shallow water.
clue.in-southern-tamil-nadu-red-soil-des: Flat, scrubby terrain with intensely red earth in southern Tamil Nadu.
clue.in-country-flag-description: The national flag of India is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.id-road-marking-description: Centre lines can be white or yellow; edge lines are always white.
clue.id-utility-pole-description: Cylindrical steel or concrete poles, some painted black with red-and-white bands. Crossbars may be symmetrical or asymmetrical.
clue.id-bollard-description: Common designs include black-and-white square or round-topped posts and yellow-and-black variants with red reflectors.
clue.id-red-white-banner-description: Strings of small red and white pennants, the national colours, hung along roads throughout the archipelago.
clue.id-cigarette-advertisement-descript: Tobacco billboards with the word 'PERINGATAN' is a common sight in Indonesia.
clue.id-front-licence-plate-motorcycle-d: Indonesian motorcycles carry a front licence plate, unlike other Southeast Asian countries.
clue.id-general-01-kabupaten-description: Indonesia is divided into hundreds of regencies know as Kabupaten (Kab. for short). This term is unique to Indonesia.
clue.id-cardinal-direction-word-descript: Addresses and province names often include directional terms: Utara (North), Timur (East), Selatan (South), Barat (West), Tengah (Central).
clue.id-triangle-pole-connector-descript: A triangular brace connects the vertical pole to its horizontal crossbar in some provinces, particularly in western Java.
clue.id-trident-pole-top-description: A three-pronged 'trident' crossbar design mainly in Central Java and Yogyakarta.
clue.id-bali-rectangular-pole-attachment: Poles in Bali sometimes have a distinctive rectangular bracket at the top.
clue.id-lesser-sunda-extra-long-pole-sup: Pole tops feature an elongated diagonal brace; some have two supports on the Lesser Sunda Islands.
clue.id-north-central-sulawesi-pole-brac: An additional bracket beneath the horizontal crossbar is typical in North and Central Sulawesi and Gorontalo.
clue.id-central-sulawesi-secondary-pole-: Slender black secondary poles beside main utility poles with two strips of tape near the top.
clue.id-satellite-dish-direction-descrip: Satellite dishes aim towards the equator; dish direction indicates relative position to it.
clue.id-central-sulawesi-tricolour-bolla: Roadside posts painted black, white, and yellow horizontal bands are specific to Central Sulawesi.
clue.id-painted-fence-sulawesi-descripti: Roadside fences painted white with blue or red highlights are common on Sulawesi.
clue.id-green-bridge-railing-kalimantan-: Bridge guardrails and side panels painted green are characteristic of South and Central Kalimantan.
clue.id-oil-palm-plantation-description: Vast palm oil estates are concentrated on Sumatra and Kalimantan, rare on Sulawesi.
clue.id-rice-paddy-description: Most rice cultivation is on Java, with secondary areas in South Sulawesi and South Sumatra.
clue.id-dry-lesser-sunda-landscape-descr: Nusa Tenggara islands are arid, with brown sparse vegetation, driest on Sumba.
clue.id-north-sumba-savannah-description: Open grassland like African savannah appears in northern Sumba.
clue.id-red-soil-batam-bangka-belitung-t: Red Soil on Batam and Bangka Belitung
clue.id-red-soil-batam-bangka-belitung-d: Reddish earth is common on Batam Island and Bangka Belitung off Sumatra's east coast.
clue.id-clay-tile-roof-java-description: Terracotta roof tiles are mainly a Javanese feature.
clue.id-corrugated-metal-roof-descriptio: Sheet-metal roofing predominates in northern and outer islands like Kalimantan, Sulawesi, and Sumatra.
clue.id-bugis-roof-vent-south-sulawesi-t: Bugis Roof Vents in South Sulawesi
clue.id-bugis-roof-vent-south-sulawesi-d: Horizontal louvred openings in triangular gable ends are nearly exclusive to South Sulawesi.
clue.id-sumba-high-peaked-roof-descripti: Sumba houses have extremely steep, towering roof peaks unique in Indonesia.
clue.id-north-sumatra-batak-roof-descrip: Batak houses have curved boat-like roofs with gentler upward sweep and no spires.
clue.id-kalimantan-wooden-shingle-roof-d: Roofs covered in small overlapping wooden shingles are distinctive in Kalimantan.
clue.id-gable-horn-roof-description: Roofs topped with horn-like finials at the gable peak, common in South Sulawesi, Riau, and Central/South Kalimantan.
clue.id-regional-licence-plate-code-desc: Plate prefixes indicate region: single letters on western Java, two letters on eastern Java and other islands.
clue.id-christian-minority-region-descri: Churches and Christian iconography appear in minority areas like parts of Sulawesi, Papua, NTT, and North Sumatra.
clue.id-country-flag-description: The national flag of Indonesia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.iq-iraqi-national-museum-descriptio: Entire Street View coverage is a single trekker walk-through inside the Iraqi National Museum in Baghdad.
clue.iq-courtyard-date-palm-description: Small patio with date palms and a diagonal path, the only outdoor scene.
clue.i-general-01-dashed-outer-lines-des: Irish roads often have dashed yellow outlines.
clue.ie-architecture-description: Rural houses are cream with dark slate roofs; urban streets have terraced row houses.
clue.ie-diamond-shaped-warning-sign-desc: Irish hazard warnings use yellow diamond-shaped boards, unique in Europe.
clue.ie-chevron-sign-description: Curve warnings show yellow arrows on black background.
clue.ie-pole-warning-sticker-description: Yellow hazard stickers on poles show a lightning bolt without electrocuted figure.
clue.ie-green-white-bollard-description: Roadside posts in Ireland are painted green and white.
clue.ie-rounded-corner-farm-gate-descrip: Metal field gates almost always have rounded top corners.
clue.ie-boreen-grass-centre-lane-descrip: Narrow rural tracks often have a grass strip down the centre.
clue.ie-green-hedgerow-landscape-descrip: Lush farmland bordered by dense hedgerows dominates the country.
clue.ie-wooden-utility-pole-step-rung-ti: Wooden Utility Poles with Step Rungs
clue.ie-wooden-utility-pole-step-rung-de: Timber poles have thin horizontal metal climbing pegs up one side.
clue.ie-double-yellow-no-parking-line-de: Double yellow lines along kerbs indicate no-parking zones.
clue.ie-pedestrian-crossing-marker-descr: Crossings are marked by black-and-white striped posts topped with a yellow globe, like in the UK.
clue.ie-regional-road-number-description: Regional roads have three-digit numbers; the first digit indicates the area arranged anti-clockwise from Dublin.
clue.ie-phone-area-code-description: Landline numbers start with a two-digit area code whose first digit corresponds to a geographic region.
clue.ie-rugged-west-coast-description: The west coast has steep hills, low mountains, open moorland, brownish-yellow grass, and occasional bare rock.
clue.ie-donegal-gen-4-rural-road-descrip: Very narrow, unmarked roads with grassy centers in hilly terrain are typical of County Donegal.
clue.ie-wicklow-mountains-description: Upland area south of Dublin with minor roads having newer coverage and no sea views.
clue.ie-22-eastern-description: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the rear edge of the camera view, common in eastern Ireland.
clue.ie-22-county-donegal-description: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular marking at the rear of the camera view used in County Donegal.
clue.ie-22-county-londonderry-northern-d: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the rear edge of the camera image in County Londonderry.
clue.ie-22-county-tyrone-northern-descri: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular marking at the rear of the camera view in County Tyrone.
clue.ie-22-county-fermanagh-northern-des: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the back edge of the camera view in County Fermanagh.
clue.ie-22-county-antrim-northern-descri: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the rear of the camera view in County Antrim.
clue.ie-22-county-down-northern-descript: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the back edge of the camera view in County Down.
clue.ie-sligo-leitrim-tabletop-mountain-: Flat-topped mesa-like mountains rise above the landscape in northern counties Sligo and Leitrim.
clue.ie-hilly-cork-description: Cork is notable among major Irish cities for its markedly hilly topography.
clue.ie-country-flag-description: The national flag of Ireland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.im-hilly-farmland-landscape-descrip: Undulating green pastures crossed by narrow roads dominate the scenery.
clue.im-whitewashed-house-description: White-rendered walls on houses and boundary walls are common, giving an Irish feel.
clue.im-striped-kerb-description: Alternating black-and-white painted kerbstones appear intermittently along main roads.
clue.im-blue-bollard-description: Blue-painted roadside bollards are frequent in built-up areas.
clue.im-generally-hilly-terrain-descript: The island's interior is mostly hilly, with some flat pockets.
clue.im-flat-northern-plain-description: The northern tip is flat compared to the rest, with mountains visible on the southern horizon.
clue.im-blue-base-lamp-posts-parish-code: Blue-Base Lamp Posts with Parish Codes
Lamp posts have blue-painted bases and a blue sticker with two-letter parish codes outside Douglas.
clue.im-all-green-lamp-posts-description: Entirely green street lights are found mainly in Ramsey and Castletown, with some in other parishes.
clue.im-country-flag-description: The national flag of the Isle of Man is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.it-license-plates-01-double-stripes: The Italian license plates will have a blue strip on both sides. The front plates are also shorter than usual.
clue.it-italian-language-description: Recognisable by abundant double consonants, frequent 'i', accented vowels (ì, é, à), and words ending in vowels.
clue.it-mediterranean-landscape-descript: Gently rolling farmland with forested mountain valleys.
clue.it-architecture-description: Pastel stone houses with terracotta roofs and outward-swinging bi-fold wooden shutters.
clue.it-round-concrete-utility-pole-desc: Cylindrical concrete poles are widespread, unlike the wood or metal poles common in other Mediterranean countries.
clue.it-white-pole-sticker-description: Timber utility poles often have a small white identification sticker.
clue.it-concrete-trident-pole-top-descri: A three-pronged concrete frame tops most poles, Italy's common insulator mount.
clue.it-double-guardrail-description: Two guardrail beams stacked on the same posts are common along Italian roads.
clue.it-red-guardrail-reflector-descript: Italian guardrails have red reflectors on their faces.
clue.it-flared-guardrail-end-description: Guardrails typically end by flattening, widening, and curving away from the road.
clue.it-black-sign-back-description: The reverse side of road signs is often painted black or dark grey.
clue.it-road-signs-01-blue-signs-descrip: Directional signs in Italy tend to be bright blue with a white capitalised text.
clue.it-highway-sign-colour-description: National roads have blue signs with white-and-blue borders; motorways have green signs with white-and-green borders.
clue.it-kilometre-marker-description: White square stones show a Roman numeral on top (hundreds of metres) and an Arabic numeral below (kilometres from origin).
clue.it-road-number-prefix-description: Route numbers start with SS (state), SR (regional), or SP (provincial).
clue.it-chevron-sign-description: In Italy, curve warning boards show white arrows on a black background.
clue.it-street-name-sign-description: White plates with a narrow blue border and black lettering.
clue.it-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: A walking figure crosses five zebra stripes and has no visible belt.
clue.it-passo-carrabile-no-parking-sign-: No-parking signs labelled 'passo carrabile' are common in built-up areas.
clue.it-phone-area-code-description: Area code leading digits increase broadly from west to east, then southward.
clue.it-regional-flag-abruzzo-descriptio: The regional flag of Abruzzo is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-basilicata-descrip: The regional flag of Basilicata is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-calabria-descripti: The regional flag of Calabria is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-campania-descripti: The regional flag of Campania is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-emilia-romagna-des: The regional flag of Emilia-Romagna is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-friuli-venezia-giu: The regional flag of Friuli-Venezia Giulia is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-lazio-description: The regional flag of Lazio is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-liguria-descriptio: The regional flag of Liguria is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-lombardy-descripti: The regional flag of Lombardy is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-marche-description: The regional flag of Marche is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-molise-description: The regional flag of Molise is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-piedmont-descripti: The regional flag of Piedmont is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-puglia-description: The regional flag of Puglia is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-sardinia-descripti: The regional flag of Sardinia is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-sicily-description: The regional flag of Sicily is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-tuscany-descriptio: The regional flag of Tuscany is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-trentino-alto-adig: The regional flag of Trentino-Alto Adige is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-umbria-description: The regional flag of Umbria is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-aosta-valley-descr: The regional flag of Aosta Valley is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-regional-flag-veneto-description: The regional flag of Veneto is occasionally seen on public buildings and signs.
clue.it-south-tyrol-german-bilingual-sig: Road and street signs appear in both Italian and German in South Tyrol.
clue.it-aosta-valley-french-sign-descrip: French text appears alongside Italian, with street names pairing 'via' and 'rue'.
clue.it-po-valley-padan-plain-descriptio: A vast, flat agricultural basin in the north, often shrouded in haze.
clue.it-bari-peninsula-olive-grove-descr: The southeastern heel has olive plantations, pale rock walls, and reddish earth.
clue.it-alpine-mountain-description: Broad, towering mountain ranges separated by deep valleys in the far north.
clue.it-sicilian-landscape-description: Dry, undulating farmland with craggy rock formations defines much of Sicily's interior.
clue.it-sardinia-grey-rock-outcrop-descr: Grey boulders protrude from the ground, especially in northeast Sardinia.
clue.it-southern-cactus-description: Prickly-pear and other cacti grow abundantly in the far south: Sicily, southern Sardinia, and Apulia.
clue.it-citrus-orchard-description: Citrus cultivation is concentrated in eastern Sicily and southern Calabria.
clue.it-rice-paddy-description: Rice fields cluster in the western and central Po Valley, with some on Sardinia.
clue.it-tuscan-brown-grey-brick-building: Rough-hewn, unpainted brown-grey stone is typical in and around Tuscany.
clue.it-alpine-architecture-description: Sturdy white-walled buildings with exposed timber detailing are typical of the Alpine north.
clue.it-aosta-valley-grey-stone-building: Irregular grey stone masonry with an Alpine character marks Aosta Valley buildings.
clue.it-veneto-solid-wooden-shutter-desc: Heavy wooden shutters on black iron hinges are common in Veneto.
clue.it-apulian-flat-roofed-house-descri: Pale, flat-roofed two- or three-storey buildings give parts of Apulia a Middle-Eastern feel.
clue.it-slovene-bilingual-sign-descripti: Near Slovenia, road signs show both Italian and Slovene text.
clue.it-vulcano-white-stripe-description: A near-white band of exposed earth traces the upper slopes of Vulcano volcano, visible from afar.
clue.it-country-flag-description: The national flag of Italy is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ja-island-region-prefecture-descrip: Japan is divided into four major islands, regions grouping prefectures, and 47 prefectures.
clue.ja-japanese-writing-system-descript: Japanese uses kanji, hiragana with rounded strokes, and angular katakana scripts.
clue.ja-katakana-script-description: Katakana, angular and geometric, is used for foreign words in signage and ads.
clue.ja-useful-kanji-place-name-descript: Eight kanji recur in place names; compass and suffix kanji aid navigation.
clue.ja-architecture-description: Japan’s buildings range from traditional rural houses to ultramodern urban high-rises.
clue.ja-round-concrete-pole-description: Utility poles are round concrete with screw-like protrusions, often with electrical plates and reflectors.
clue.ja-pole-reflector-description: Pole reflectors are compact, elevated, with vertical or diagonal yellow and white stripes.
clue.ja-licence-plate-description: Vehicle plates are white with green characters; kei cars have yellow plates with black lettering.
clue.ja-road-line-description: Road markings combine solid white edges with dashed or solid white/yellow center lines; no yellow edge lines.
clue.ja-bollard-description: Default bollards are plain white posts with round reflectors; some show kanji or extra attachments.
clue.ja-white-guardrail-description: Plain white guardrails are the standard road barriers.
clue.ja-hexagonal-prefecture-road-shield: Prefectural routes use hexagonal shields with route numbers and kanji prefecture names.
clue.ja-common-infrastructure-descriptio: Distinctive triangular stop signs, school-zone crossings, and convex traffic mirrors are common.
clue.ja-retaining-wall-description: Retaining walls in remote countryside indicate Japan.
clue.ja-area-code-description: Telephone area codes on signs increase southward.
clue.ja-utility-pole-plate-description: Utility poles have region-specific identification plates.
clue.ja-regional-pole-reflector-pad-desc: Reflector pads on utility poles vary by region.
clue.ja-road-diamond-large-filled-descri: A large white diamond with a small central hole; wide and bold, common across Japan.
clue.ja-road-diamond-narrow-filled-descr: A filled diamond with narrow, elongated proportions.
clue.ja-road-diamond-tall-thin-descripti: A tall, thin diamond outline with a small center hole.
clue.ja-road-diamond-crossed-outline-med: A medium diamond with overlapping sides creating a crossed-line pattern.
clue.ja-road-diamond-crossed-outline-nar: A crossed-line diamond like the medium variant but taller.
clue.ja-road-diamond-crossed-outline-sta: A crossed-line diamond used in central and southern prefectures.
clue.ja-road-diamond-small-crossed-outli: A smaller crossed-line diamond with compact proportions.
clue.ja-road-diamond-very-small-descript: The smallest diamond variant, distinguished by its size.
clue.ja-road-diamond-kagawa-description: A clean, tall outline diamond with thin lines, specific to Kagawa Prefecture.
clue.ja-road-diamond-aomori-new-pattern-: A newer crossed-line diamond pattern appearing in Aomori alongside the traditional filled style.
clue.ja-road-diamond-thick-outline-descr: A thick-stroked outline diamond with a prominent centre hole and bold, heavy lines.
clue.ja-road-diamond-ishikawa-kumamoto-d: A clean outline diamond with moderate line weight, used in Ishikawa and Kumamoto.
clue.ja-road-diamond-crossed-outline-yam: A crossed-line diamond used in Yamanashi and as a newer pattern in Nagano.
clue.ja-road-diamond-nara-new-pattern-de: A newer, smaller crossed-line diamond appearing in Nara alongside the traditional style.
clue.ja-road-diamond-crossed-outline-iba: A newer crossed-line diamond appearing in Ibaraki and Niigata alongside their traditional style.
clue.ja-road-diamond-saga-new-pattern-de: A newer, small thick-outlined diamond appearing in Saga alongside the traditional very-small style.
clue.ja-road-diamond-shizuoka-descriptio: A clean outline diamond with thin, delicate lines, specific to Shizuoka Prefecture.
clue.ja-road-diamond-thin-outline-descri: A wide outline diamond with thick strokes but an open, airy feel. Used in several prefectures as a newer alternate pattern.
clue.ja-prefecture-signpost-sticker-desc: Signposts across Japan often display small stickers specific to individual prefectures.
clue.ja-chugoku-guy-wire-description: Guy wires in the Chugoku region have an orange cover with a large bulge near the bottom.
clue.ja-hokuriku-guy-wire-title: Hokuriku Guy Wires: Black-Yellow Bottle Stripes
clue.ja-hokuriku-guy-wire-description: Guy wires in the Hokuriku area have a bottle-shaped cover with black and yellow stripes.
clue.ja-kansai-guy-wire-title: Kansai Guy Wires: Yellow with Flat Top
clue.ja-kansai-guy-wire-description: Guy wires in the Kansai (Kinki) region have a yellow cover with a flat lid at the top.
clue.ja-chiba-guy-wire-title: Chiba Guy Wires: Wide Black-Yellow Stripes
clue.ja-chiba-guy-wire-description: Guy wires in Chiba Prefecture have wide alternating black and yellow stripes.
clue.ja-chugoku-orange-arrow-pole-descri: In Chugoku, an orange arrow is visible above the highest plate on utility poles.
clue.ja-shikoku-orange-black-pole-band-d: Utility poles in Shikoku often have alternating orange and black bands wrapped around them.
clue.ja-kansai-120-pole-attachment-descr: In Kansai, pole hardware with roughly 120-degree angular spread is common.
clue.ja-shikoku-90-pole-attachment-descr: Compact right-angle brackets attached to utility poles appear regularly in Shikoku.
clue.ja-hokkaido-transformer-description: In Hokkaido, a cross-shaped bracket or lone transformer sits on horizontal bars; multiple transformers are on opposing sides of a square frame.
clue.ja-tohoku-transformer-description: Tohoku transformers have square mounting brackets and the Tohoku Electric Power logo, often on circular plates with zigzag or straight bars.
clue.ja-kanto-transformer-description: Kanto transformers with two or three insulators sit on wooden backing boards with dual bars or circular plates with T-shaped bars.
clue.ja-hokuriku-transformer-description: Hokuriku transformers are secured by slender metal bars and have compact, lantern-shaped insulators without other horizontal supports.
clue.ja-chubu-transformer-description: Chubu transformers have yellow numerals, black tap connectors, and are supported by large triangular bars or narrow metal brackets.
clue.ja-kansai-transformer-description: Kansai transformers sit on square frames with straight or zigzag bars along the bottom edge, sometimes attached to vertical supports.
clue.ja-chugoku-transformer-description: Chugoku uses a cross-shaped arm with a triangular brace and elongated or compact insulators; transformers have white labels with red numerals.
clue.ja-shikoku-transformer-description: Shikoku uses a cross-shaped arm with a half-triangle brace and cap-shaped insulators; transformers often have white labels with black numerals.
clue.ja-kyushu-transformer-description: In Kyushu, a horizontal bar ends with three insulators; transformers face opposite directions, 180 degrees apart.
clue.ja-okinawa-transformer-description: Okinawa poles have a T-shaped arm with transformers on directly opposing faces.
clue.ja-grey-insulator-block-description: Grey, insulator-like wire-routing blocks appear in Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, and Shikoku.
clue.ja-chubu-pole-top-description: A pole cap of four heavy bars crowned by a circular element is characteristic of Chubu.
clue.ja-hokuriku-pole-top-description: A tent-shaped pole cap with two filled sides is typical of Hokuriku.
clue.ja-chugoku-pole-top-description: Four slender, narrow bars at the top of the pole are a hallmark of Chugoku.
clue.ja-kanto-tuning-fork-pole-top-descr: A fork-shaped pole cap with an upper bar protruding beyond each side and horizontal crossbars beneath, common in Kanto.
clue.ja-chubu-tuning-fork-pole-top-descr: A fork-shaped pole cap with a compact upper bar and single horizontal crossbar below, frequent in Chubu.
clue.ja-kansai-tuning-fork-pole-top-desc: A fork-shaped pole cap with a thin wire upper bar and horizontal crossbar underneath, prevalent in Kansai.
clue.ja-snow-shoulder-arrow-description: Road-edge marker arrows guide drivers along snowy shoulders, appearing almost exclusively in Hokkaido.
clue.ja-kyushu-flat-bollard-description: Flat white bollards with a row of orange reflectors on one face, plain white on the reverse, characteristic of Kyushu and Yamaguchi.
clue.ja-shikoku-black-stripe-bollard-des: Bollards on Shikoku with a dark horizontal band beneath the reflector, freestanding or mounted.
clue.ja-tohoku-thick-bollard-description: Wide white posts with octagonal reflector and single yellow band below, common in Tohoku.
clue.ja-akita-prefecture-bollard-descrip: Similar to Tohoku bollards but with two yellow bands beneath the octagonal reflector.
clue.ja-toyama-prefecture-bollard-descri: Extendable bollard with one reflector and red band below, specific to Toyama.
clue.ja-okayama-prefecture-bollard-descr: Bollard with eight-sided reflector, red band below, and tapered slope, found only in Okayama.
clue.ja-aomori-prefecture-bollard-descri: Extendable post with single round reflector flanked by two yellow bands, found in Aomori.
clue.ja-tohoku-striped-bollard-descripti: Painted striped sleeves over bollards, tapering upward and lacking reflectors, common in Tohoku.
clue.ja-chugoku-snow-pole-description: Simple snow marker poles with slim tips, concentrated in northern Chugoku.
clue.ja-green-guardrail-band-kyushu-desc: Guardrails with green banding throughout Kyushu, especially Oita and Miyazaki.
clue.ja-yamaguchi-yellow-guardrail-descr: Bright yellow guardrails exclusive to Yamaguchi Prefecture.
clue.ja-hokkaido-chevron-guardrail-stick: Arrow-patterned chevron stickers on guardrail tips and posts, common in Hokkaido.
clue.ja-chugoku-red-yellow-guardrail-end: Red and yellow striped stickers on guardrail ends, widespread in Chugoku except Yamaguchi.
clue.ja-vertical-traffic-light-descripti: Traffic signals oriented vertically in Hokkaido and northwest coast; horizontal elsewhere.
clue.ja-kagawa-black-sign-description: Dark boards with two yellow dots, exclusive to Kagawa, sometimes with arrows.
clue.ja-kerosene-tank-claymore-descripti: Fuel storage tanks nicknamed "Claymores," common northward and in Hokkaido.
clue.ja-hot-water-propane-tank-descripti: Heating and cooking tanks common in northern and mountainous rural areas.
clue.ja-snow-prevention-road-shosetsu-de: Roads with small nozzles spraying heated groundwater to prevent snow, mainly on northwest coast.
clue.ja-ehime-cycling-route-description: Bicycle lanes marked by white outside and blue inside stripes, mainly along Ehime's coast.
clue.ja-red-tiled-roof-description: Houses with red roof tiles, common in Chugoku, especially Hiroshima and Shimane.
clue.ja-northern-flat-sloped-roof-descri: Northern roofs are flat or low-sloped with exterior ladders for snow removal.
clue.ja-okinawa-concrete-building-descri: Flat-roofed white concrete buildings define Okinawa architecture.
clue.ja-cabbage-hokkaido-description: Cabbage grows prolifically in Hokkaido and northern Honshu, often beside roads.
clue.ja-green-tea-plant-description: Neatly trimmed tea bushes with pole fans, mainly from Shizuoka and Kagoshima.
clue.ja-rice-paddy-description: Rice fields north of Tokyo with green shoots or golden husks in flooded paddies.
clue.ja-japanese-white-birch-description: Tree species concentrated in Chubu and Hokkaido, less so in Tohoku.
clue.ja-bamboo-description: Bamboo is more common in southern areas and less so northward.
clue.ja-chinese-silver-grass-kyushu-desc: Kyushu grass thrives across Kyushu island in large quantities.
clue.ja-sugarcane-description: Sugarcane grows almost entirely on Kyushu and Okinawa islands.
clue.ja-hokkaido-winter-coverage-descrip: Snowy winter Street View is scarce on Hokkaido, mostly in the south.
clue.ja-nobi-kanto-plain-description: Nobi and Kanto plains are flat expanses in mountainous Japan.
clue.ja-okinawa-shisa-lion-house-plaque-: Okinawa has Shisa guardian lions and house plaques with local lettering.
clue.ja-trekker-tripod-description: Many trekker and tripod camera setups create non-standard coverage.
clue.ja-country-flag-description: The national flag of Japan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.jp-island-region-prefecture-descrip: Japan is divided into four major islands, regions grouping prefectures, and 47 prefectures.
clue.jp-road-01-driving-direction-descri: In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.
clue.jp-japanese-writing-system-descript: Japanese uses kanji, hiragana with rounded strokes, and angular katakana scripts.
clue.jp-architecture-description: Building styles range from traditional rural houses to ultramodern urban high-rises.
clue.jp-round-concrete-pole-description: Utility poles are round concrete with threaded screw-like protrusions and often electrical plates.
clue.jp-road-line-description: Japanese road markings include solid white edges with dashed or solid white/yellow center lines.
clue.jp-white-guardrail-description: Plain white guardrails are the default road barrier throughout Japan.
clue.jp-hexagonal-prefecture-road-shield: Prefectural routes use hexagonal shields with route numbers and often kanji prefecture names.
clue.jp-common-infrastructure-descriptio: Triangular stop signs, school-zone crossings, and convex traffic mirrors are widespread.
clue.jp-retaining-wall-description: Retaining walls in remote countryside indicate you are in Japan.
clue.jp-area-code-description: Telephone area codes appear on signage and increase in value moving southward.
clue.jp-regional-pole-reflector-pad-desc: Reflector pads on utility poles vary in design by region.
clue.jp-road-diamond-large-filled-descri: A standard white hollow diamond with a continuous outline. This generic variant can be found throughout Japan.
clue.jp-road-diamond-narrow-filled-descr: This diamond variant has gaps in the upper-right and bottom-left corners of the outline and can be found in Hyōgo, Kyoto, Okayama and Miyagi prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-tall-thin-descripti: This diamond variant has two offset gaps along the upper-left and lower-right sides of the outline. It can be found in Mie and Kōchi prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-crossed-outline-med: This diamond variant has four gaps around the outline, creating four separate sections, and can be found in Gunma, Chiba and Gifu prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-crossed-outline-nar: This diamond variant has four gaps in the outline, dividing it into four separate sections. It can be found in Nara and Wakayama prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-crossed-outline-sta: This diamond variant has four gaps around the corners of the outline, creating four separate sections. It can be found in Shiga, Ibaraki, Saitama, Tochigi, Niigata and Okinawa prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-small-crossed-outli: This diamond variant has four gaps in the outline, with breaks along both the upper-right and lower-left sides. It can be found in Ōita and Toyama prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-very-small-descript: This diamond variant has gaps at the middle of both the left and right sides of the outline. It can be found in Tottori, Shimane and Saga prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-thick-outline-descr: A smaller version of the diamond with gaps at the upper-right and lower-left corners. It can be found in Hiroshima and Tokushima prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-ishikawa-kumamoto-d: This diamond variant has gaps at the top and bottom, with the upper gap offset to the left and the lower gap offset to the right. It can be found in Kumamoto and Ishikawa prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-crossed-outline-yam: This diamond variant has two gaps along the left side of the outline, creating three distinct sections. It can be found in Yamanashi and Nagano prefectures.
clue.jp-road-diamond-crossed-outline-iba: A newer crossed-line diamond in Ibaraki and Niigata alongside the traditional style.
clue.jp-road-diamond-thin-outline-descri: A thinner version of the standard continuous diamond. This variant can be found in Kagoshima, Aichi, Yamaguchi and Nagano prefectures.
clue.jp-prefecture-signpost-sticker-desc: Signposts across Japan display small stickers specific to individual prefectures.
clue.jp-chugoku-orange-arrow-pole-descri: In Chugoku, an orange arrow appears above the highest plate on utility poles.
clue.jp-shikoku-orange-black-pole-band-d: Utility poles in Shikoku often have alternating orange and black bands.
clue.jp-kansai-120-pole-attachment-descr: In Kansai, pole hardware has a roughly 120-degree angular spread.
clue.jp-shikoku-90-pole-attachment-descr: Compact right-angle brackets appear regularly on Shikoku utility poles.
clue.jp-hokkaido-transformer-description: Hokkaido transformers mount on cross-shaped brackets or horizontal bars, often opposite sides of a square frame.
clue.jp-tohoku-transformer-description: Tohoku transformers have square mounting brackets, the Tohoku Electric Power logo, and various support bar styles.
clue.jp-kanto-transformer-description: Kanto transformers sit on wooden backing boards with dual bars or circular plates with T-shaped bars.
clue.jp-hokuriku-transformer-description: Hokuriku transformers have slender metal bars and compact, lantern-shaped insulators without other horizontal supports.
clue.jp-chubu-transformer-description: Chubu transformers feature yellow numerals, black tap connectors, and large triangular or narrow metal supports.
clue.jp-kansai-transformer-description: Kansai transformers sit on square frames with straight or zigzag bars, sometimes attached to vertical supports.
clue.jp-chugoku-transformer-description: Chugoku transformers use a cross-shaped arm with a triangular brace and carry white labels with red numerals.
clue.jp-shikoku-transformer-description: Shikoku transformers have a cross-shaped arm with a half-triangle brace and cap-shaped insulators with white labels.
clue.jp-kyushu-transformer-description: Kyushu transformers mount on a horizontal bar ending with three insulators, facing opposite directions.
clue.jp-okinawa-transformer-description: Okinawa poles have a T-shaped arm with transformers on opposite faces.
clue.jp-grey-insulator-block-description: Grey wire-routing blocks appear in Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, and Shikoku, rarely in Hokkaido.
clue.jp-chubu-pole-top-description: A pole cap with four heavy bars crowned by a circular element is typical of Chubu.
clue.jp-hokuriku-pole-top-description: A tent-shaped pole cap with two filled sides is typical of Hokuriku.
clue.jp-chugoku-pole-top-description: Four slender, narrow bars atop the pole are a hallmark of Chugoku.
clue.jp-kanto-tuning-fork-pole-top-descr: A fork-shaped pole cap with a protruding upper bar and horizontal crossbars appears mainly in Kanto.
clue.jp-chubu-tuning-fork-pole-top-descr: A fork-shaped pole cap with a compact upper bar and single horizontal crossbar is common in Chubu.
clue.jp-kansai-tuning-fork-pole-top-desc: A fork-shaped pole cap with a thin wire upper bar and horizontal crossbar is prevalent in Kansai.
clue.j-general-01-02-overhead-arrows-des: This arrow above the road marks the road during heavy snow and is mainly seen in Hokkaido.
clue.jp-kyushu-flat-bollard-description: Flat, white bollards with a row of orange reflectors on one face are characteristic of Kyushu and Yamaguchi.
clue.jp-shikoku-black-stripe-bollard-des: On Shikoku, bollards have a dark horizontal band beneath the reflector and appear freestanding or mounted.
clue.jp-tohoku-thick-bollard-description: Tohoku's bollards are wide white posts with an octagonal reflector and a yellow band below it; black versions appear on highways.
clue.jp-tohoku-striped-bollard-descripti: Striped sleeves tapering to a narrower top and lacking reflectors are common over bollards in Tohoku, especially Akita.
clue.jp-chugoku-snow-pole-description: Simple snow marker poles with slim tips are concentrated in northern Chugoku and sporadically in Iwate.
clue.jp-green-guardrail-band-kyushu-desc: Guardrails with green bands appear throughout Kyushu, especially in Oita and Miyazaki.
clue.xx-road-01-01-yellow-guardrails-des: Yamaguchi Prefecture in Japan is recognized for its distinctive bright yellow roadside guardrails.
clue.jp-hokkaido-chevron-guardrail-stick: Arrow-patterned chevron stickers appear on guardrail tips and fence posts in Hokkaido.
clue.jp-chugoku-red-yellow-guardrail-end: Red and yellow striped stickers on guardrail ends are widespread in Chugoku, excluding Yamaguchi.
clue.jp-vertical-traffic-light-descripti: Traffic signals are vertical in Hokkaido and the northwestern coast; elsewhere they are horizontal.
clue.jp-kagawa-black-sign-description: Road side reflectors with dark boards and two yellow dots are exclusive to Kagawa.
clue.jp-kerosene-tank-claymore-descripti: Fuel storage tanks nicknamed "Claymores" are common northward, especially in Hokkaido and mountainous areas.
clue.jp-hot-water-propane-tank-descripti: Tanks for heating and cooking appear more often in northern and mountainous prefectures, common in rural areas.
clue.jp-snow-prevention-road-shosetsu-de: Rows of small nozzles spray heated groundwater to prevent snow buildup, mainly along the northwestern coast.
clue.jp-ehime-cycling-route-description: Bicycle lanes in Ehime have a white outer stripe and blue inner stripe, mostly along coastal roads.
clue.jp-red-tiled-roof-description: Houses with red roof tiles are common in Chugoku, especially Hiroshima and Shimane.
clue.jp-northern-flat-sloped-roof-descri: Northern roofs shift to flat or low-angle slopes with exterior ladders for snow removal.
clue.jp-okinawa-concrete-building-descri: Flat-roofed white concrete buildings define Okinawa architecture.
clue.jp-cabbage-hokkaido-description: Cabbage grows prolifically in Hokkaido and parts of northern Honshu, often visible beside roads.
clue.jp-green-tea-plant-description: Tea bushes grow in trimmed hedgerows with pole-mounted fans, mainly in Shizuoka and Kagoshima.
clue.jp-rice-paddy-description: Rice fields north of Tokyo show green shoots in season and golden husks at harvest, often flooded.
clue.jp-japanese-white-birch-description: This tree species is concentrated in Chubu and Hokkaido, with some presence in Tohoku.
clue.jp-bamboo-description: Bamboo is more common in southern Japan and less so heading north.
clue.jp-chinese-silver-grass-kyushu-desc: Known as Kyushu grass, it thrives across Kyushu in large quantities.
clue.jp-sugarcane-description: Sugarcane grows almost exclusively in southern Kyushu and Okinawa.
clue.jp-hokkaido-winter-coverage-descrip: Snowy winter Google Street View is scarce in Hokkaido, mostly in the southern part.
clue.jp-nobi-kanto-plain-description: The Nobi and Kanto plains are conspicuously flat expanses in mountainous Japan.
clue.jp-okinawa-shisa-lion-house-plaque-: Okinawa features Shisa guardian lion statues and house plaques with local lettering.
clue.jp-trekker-tripod-description: Trekker and tripod camera setups appear across many prefectures, creating non-standard coverage.
clue.jp-country-flag-description: The national flag of Japan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.jp-misc-01-vending-machines-descrip: Japan has millions of vending machines, making them a common sight here.
clue.je-architecture-description: Buildings mix northern-French and British styles with pastel walls and slate roofs.
clue.je-red-granite-description: Local red granite is used widely, giving buildings a warm reddish tone.
clue.je-cornish-palm-description: Cordyline australis palms are common ornamental garden plants.
clue.je-yellow-give-way-line-description: Junctions use yellow give-way lines instead of white.
clue.je-cycling-route-sign-description: Cycle network marked with 'Green Lane' markers and blue route plates with maps.
clue.je-asymmetric-sign-attachment-descr: Many road signs are off-centre on their posts.
clue.je-parish-coat-arms-street-sign-tit: Parish Coat of Arms on Street Signs
clue.je-parish-coat-arms-street-sign-des: Street signs display the parish's heraldic emblem.
clue.je-st-helier-capital-description: The capital has taller buildings, tighter streets, and a livelier urban feel.
clue.je-country-flag-description: The national flag of Jersey is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-general-01-03-black-google-car-d: In Jordan, the Street View coverage was captured by a black Google car.
clue.jo-licence-plate-description: Jordan has white plates in long and short formats; commercial vehicles have green left band.
clue.jo-road-marking-description: Yellow edge lines paired with a white centre line.
clue.jo-utility-pole-description: Three common types: concrete with diagonal brace, concrete with Y-shaped crossarms, and two-legged metal towers with coils.
clue.jo-arid-landscape-description: Dominated by barren desert with sparse Mediterranean greenery.
clue.jo-sandstone-architecture-descripti: Flat-roofed buildings clad in pale sandstone blocks.
clue.jo-poor-road-quality-description: Many roads have heat-buckled asphalt with warps and cracks.
clue.jo-coverage-area-description: Street View covers only the far western strip on major towns and roads.
clue.jo-amman-description: Jordan's capital, a hilly city of mid-rise apartments with an urban feel.
clue.jo-dead-sea-highway-65-north-descri: The Dead Sea is visible directly to the west along the northern section of Highway 65.
clue.jo-highway-65-south-description: A single-lane north–south highway with extended sandy stretches south of Feifa valley.
clue.jo-madaba-red-soil-field-descriptio: Flat farmland around Madaba stands out for its deep red earth.
clue.jo-aqaba-mountain-description: A chain of ragged, jagged peaks along the eastern and southern edges of Aqaba.
clue.jo-petra-trekker-coverage-descripti: Trekker imagery covers Petra’s rock-hewn city, reddish gorges, cliffs, and tourist clusters.
clue.jo-country-flag-description: The national flag of Jordan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.kz-kazakh-language-alphabet-descrip: Kazakhstan uses Cyrillic and Latin scripts; Kazakh has unique Cyrillic letters.
clue.kz-diverse-mostly-flat-landscape-de: Kazakhstan features varied terrain but mostly vast, open, flat rural scenery.
clue.kz-russian-style-infrastructure-des: Kazakhstan's built environment closely mirrors Russia's.
clue.kz-blue-street-sign-building-descri: Kazakh street signs are blue with white patterns, mounted on building facades, often bilingual or trilingual.
clue.kz-unique-90-degree-bollard-descrip: Distinctive bollards of two thin posts joined at a 90-degree angle.
clue.xx-general-01-46-tree-trunks-descri: The bottom of tree trunks in Kazakhstan are often painted white.
clue.kz-yellow-black-chevron-sign-descri: Kazakh road chevrons are predominantly yellow and black; T-intersections use red and white.
clue.kz-urban-gas-pipe-description: Above-ground gas pipes are common throughout Kazakh cities.
clue.kz-koshkar-muiz-ornamental-pattern-: The ram's-horn motif koshkar-muiz appears as decoration across Kazakhstan.
clue.kz-ornate-city-entrance-arch-descri: Many Kazakh cities feature decorative and ornate entrance arches.
clue.kz-limited-street-view-coverage-des: Coverage is sparse; major roads and cities are covered, rural roads often lack imagery.
clue.kz-seasonal-coverage-region-descrip: Imagery shows summer in west/central, autumn in northeast, and winter in southeast Kazakhstan.
clue.kz-driving-direction-map-descriptio: Knowing travel direction on rural roads helps narrow down locations.

clue.kz-qr-code-region-text-street-sign-: QR Code Region Text on Street Signs
Some blue street signs have region text beneath the QR code.
clue.kz-northern-birch-forest-descriptio: Dense birch forests alongside green fields are typical of northern Kazakhstan.
clue.kz-northwestern-green-steppe-descri: Wide grassy plains are typical of northwestern Kazakhstan, especially Akmola and Kostanay.
clue.kz-southwestern-sandy-desert-descri: Sandy terrain with sparse shrubs is typical of southwestern Kazakhstan.
clue.kz-southeastern-snow-capped-mountai: Tall snow-capped mountains appear in southeastern Kazakhstan.
clue.kz-snow-coverage-southeast-almaty-d: Snowy roads appear southeast, especially east of Almaty.
clue.kz-green-rolling-hill-north-bishkek: Green Rolling Hills North of Bishkek
Lush green rolling hills occur just north of Bishkek in southern Kazakhstan.

clue.kz-39-atyrau-region-description: Poles feature three horizontal bands: blue top, white middle, black bottom, with vivid colors.
clue.kz-39-akmola-region-description: Poles show a thin red stripe top, broad white middle, thin black bottom; white section is widest.
clue.kz-39-kostanay-region-description: Poles have narrow alternating thin turquoise and yellow horizontal stripes.
clue.kz-39-north-kazakhstan-region-descr: Utility poles have thin horizontal bands of white and light grey.
clue.kz-39-jambyl-region-description: Poles have three bold horizontal bands: red top, yellow middle, black bottom, similar width.
clue.kz-39-kyzylorda-region-title: Kyzylorda Pole and Lamp Post Paint
clue.kz-39-kyzylorda-region-description: Poles show thin yellow and red stripes top, broad white below; lamp posts are white with turquoise base.
clue.kz-baltic-pine-forest-description: Thick Baltic pine forests appear north of Shchuchinsk.
clue.kz-country-flag-description: The national flag of Kazakhstan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ke-road-line-description: Kenyan roads have solid white edge lines and yellow centre lines, solid or dashed.
clue.ke-green-directional-sign-descripti: Kenyan directional signs have green backgrounds with white borders and lettering; route numbers are white or yellow.
clue.ke-red-white-road-sign-description: Road signs in Kenya are mostly red and white.
clue.ke-county-name-signage-description: Signs often display Kenyan county names, useful for regional identification.
clue.ke-repurposed-van-description: Colourfully wrapped repurposed vans are common throughout Kenya.
clue.ke-eucalyptus-tree-description: Eucalyptus trees with long clustered leaves and smooth bark grow widely in Kenya.
clue.ke-topography-description: Eastern and northern Kenya is very flat; elevation rises steadily toward the southwest.
clue.ke-regional-climate-description: Kenya spans humid to very arid climate zones; use climate as a regional clue.
clue.ke-white-tape-roof-description: White tape strips appear on car roofs north and south of Nairobi.
clue.ke-mombasa-coast-description: Mombasa coast features white sandy soil, palm trees, and a coastal atmosphere.
clue.ke-far-west-kisumu-description: Northwest and southwest of Kisumu are agricultural with farms, grassy hills, and tall eucalyptus.
clue.ke-kitui-semi-arid-description: Kitui area is semi-arid, hilly or mountainous, with light orange sandy soil.
clue.ke-b9-northeast-description: The B9 northeast is unpaved with bright reddish-orange dirt and dense tree cover.
clue.ke-mount-kilimanjaro-description: Kilimanjaro's broad silhouette is visible south from much coverage north of the mountain.
clue.ke-mara-triangle-description: Flat to gently hilly savannah with no major mountains, covered by a white car.
clue.ke-aberdare-national-park-descripti: Grey-and-brown car with snorkel and rubber bands on roof rack appears near Aberdare.
clue.ke-mt-elgon-area-description: Between Kitale and Mt Elgon, same grey-and-brown car appears; redder soil and greener landscape.
clue.ke-kerio-lodwar-area-description: Between Kerio and Lodwar, same car appears in sandy, dry, sparsely vegetated landscape.
clue.ke-b8-succulent-description: A stretch of the B8 north of Kibaoni is lined with many succulent plants.
clue.ke-country-flag-description: The national flag of Kenya is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.kr-licence-plate-description: South Korea's plates: pre-2006 short green; post-2006 white (private) or yellow (commercial), in long and short formats.
clue.kr-autumn-winter-coverage-descripti: Much South Korean imagery was captured in autumn or winter, showing bare trees and muted colours.
clue.kr-spiked-pole-top-description: Most South Korean utility poles taper to a pointed spike at the top.
clue.kr-general-01-driving-direction-des: In South Korea they drive on the right side of the road.
clue.kr-road-line-description: South Korean roads have yellow centre lines and white edge lines.
clue.kr-red-block-marking-description: Red-painted block patterns occasionally appear on South Korean road surfaces.
clue.kr-yellow-warning-sign-description: South Korean triangular warning signs have a yellow background.
clue.kr-arrow-shaped-street-sign-descrip: South Korean street name signs are blue and arrow-shaped, hung from utility poles.
clue.kr-green-direction-sign-description: South Korean directional signs display white text on a green background.
clue.kr-pedestrian-crossing-description: South Korean zebra crossings often use alternating yellow and white stripes.
clue.kr-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Crossing signs are pentagonal on a blue background, unique to South Korea.
clue.kr-house-number-description: South Korean buildings have blue house-shaped address plaques with Hangul and Latin script.
clue.kr-wedge-shaped-bollard-description: Black-and-white wedge-shaped bollards with round yellow and grey reflectors appear along some roads.
clue.kr-mountainous-landscape-descriptio: South Korea's terrain is mostly hilly or mountainous, with elevation visible on the horizon.
clue.kr-red-brick-architecture-descripti: Red brick is a common building material throughout South Korea.
clue.kr-traditional-tiled-roof-descripti: Many South Korean buildings have traditional tiled roofs with upturned edges and decorative corners.
clue.kr-area-code-description: Phone area codes increase from north to south, 02 in Seoul up to 064 on Jeju Island.
clue.kr-jeju-island-volcanic-soil-descri: Jeju is a volcanic island with dark volcanic dirt and visible volcanic cones.
clue.xx-general-01-19-rock-walls-descrip: Jeju Island in South Korea is known for its many rock walls made from dark volcanic stone.
clue.kr-country-flag-description: The national flag of South Korea is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-license-plates-01-01-red-strip-d: Licence plates in Kyrgyzstan feature a red strip on the left side.
clue.kg-kyrgyz-cyrillic-script-descripti: Kyrgyz uses Cyrillic with extra letters Ө, Ү, and Ң.
clue.kg-white-painted-tree-pole-descript: Trees and concrete poles often have lower portions painted white.
clue.kg-red-white-kilometre-marker-descr: Kilometre markers have a red-and-white triangle pattern unique to Kyrgyzstan.
clue.kg-driving-direction-map-descriptio: Knowing which way the Google car drives on Kyrgyzstan's major roads helps narrow your position.
clue.kg-southern-mirror-clue-description: The car's side mirror shows less road and a more diagonal reflection in southern Kyrgyzstan.
clue.kg-black-dot-mirror-description: A small black dot on the car mirror indicates a specific Kyrgyzstan region.
clue.kg-divided-road-description: Divided roads in Kyrgyzstan cluster around Bishkek, with a major highway east to Balykchy.
clue.kg-snowy-northern-road-description: Northern roads often have heavy snow coverage and bright skies.
clue.kg-bishkek-capital-city-description: Bishkek features taller multi-storey buildings and upscale outskirts; mountains lie to the south.
clue.kg-south-bishkek-tian-shan-title: South of Bishkek, Tian Shan Mountains
clue.kg-south-bishkek-tian-shan-descript: South of Bishkek is hilly with snow-capped Tian Shan mountains visible to the south.
clue.kg-colourful-poles-bishkek-descript: Towns east and west of Bishkek have multi-coloured poles painted yellow, green, white, and sometimes red.
clue.kg-osh-second-largest-city-descript: Osh uses the southern mirror and has partly cloudy weather.
clue.kg-osh-trees-leaves-description: Most trees in Osh retain their leaves, unlike in Bishkek.
clue.kg-jalal-abad-overcast-description: Jalal-Abad shows the southern mirror and has distinct overcast skies with no cloud gaps.
clue.kg-talas-red-yellow-poles-title: Talas, Red and Yellow Striped Poles
clue.kg-talas-red-yellow-poles-descripti: Poles in Talas are white at the base with red and yellow stripes.
clue.kg-naryn-orange-ridge-snow-peaks-ti: Naryn, Orange Ridge and Snow-Capped Peaks
clue.kg-naryn-orange-ridge-snow-peaks-de: Naryn has a steep orange ridge to the north and snow-capped mountains to the south.
clue.kg-em-04-tian-shan-visible-title: EM-04: Tian Shan Mountain Range Visible
clue.kg-em-04-tian-shan-visible-descript: The Tian Shan mountains are visible to the south; terrain is otherwise flat.
clue.kg-em-04-southern-agricultural-desc: This southern section has extensive agriculture, lush roadside vegetation, and nearby hills.
clue.kg-em-11-red-soil-snow-naryn-title: EM-11: Red Soil and Snow South of Naryn
clue.kg-em-11-red-soil-snow-naryn-descri: Mountains and hills south of Naryn show a striking mix of snow and red soil.
clue.kg-em-09-overcast-east-cholpon-ata-: EM-09: Overcast East of Cholpon Ata
East of Cholpon Ata is overcast with mountains to the north, a lake to the south, and tall roadside trees.
clue.kg-em-10-sandy-shore-lake-mountains: EM-10: Sandy Shore with Lake and Mountains
Lake Issyk Kul and Tian Shan mountains are visible; soil is sandy and rocky.
clue.kg-em-10-sandy-terrain-southern-mou: EM-10: Sandy Terrain with Southern Mountains
Mountains dominate the south; sandy roadsides persist throughout.
clue.kg-em-10-dry-west-issyk-kul-title: EM-10: Dry Western End of Issyk Kul
clue.kg-em-10-dry-west-issyk-kul-descrip: The western end of Issyk Kul has drier terrain; lake and hills sit further from the road.
clue.kg-country-flag-description: The national flag of Kyrgyzstan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.la-licence-plate-description: Laotian plates are short and yellow; commercial plates white; government plates blue.
clue.la-striped-curb-description: Kerbstones painted in alternating red-white, yellow-white, or black-white stripes are common.
clue.la-utility-pole-description: Laotian utility poles are square concrete columns with vertical rows of small pinholes.
clue.la-black-white-bollard-description: Laos uses square concrete bollards with black bands on a white body.
clue.la-lamp-post-marking-description: Some Laotian lamp posts have diagonal red-and-white stripes stopping short of the base.
clue.la-red-white-concrete-bollard-descr: Cuboid concrete bollards painted red and white appear a few metres off the roadside.
clue.la-communist-flag-description: Laos occasionally displays red hammer-and-sickle flags.
clue.la-palm-tree-description: Palm trees are common in Luang Prabang's streetscape.
clue.la-flat-terrain-description: Savannakhet is exceptionally flat with slightly reddish soil.
clue.la-red-soil-dry-hill-description: Pakse has vivid red soil and dry, arid vegetation with parched hills nearby.
