clue.la-country-flag-description: The national flag of Laos is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.lv-hook-shaped-poletop-insulator-de: Latvian utility poles have hook-shaped insulators in an alternating left–right–left pattern.
clue.lv-chevron-description: Latvian chevrons are white with red arrows.
clue.lv-warning-speed-sign-border-descri: Latvian warning and speed signs have a thick red border with a thin white outline.
clue.lv-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Latvian crossing signs have five stripes and a pedestrian figure with long legs.
clue.lv-guardrail-white-red-reflector-ti: Guardrails with White or Red Reflectors
clue.lv-guardrail-white-red-reflector-de: Latvian guardrails are standard A-type with white or red reflectors.
clue.lv-latvian-language-description: A Baltic language with unique letters: vowels with macrons (Ā Ē Ī) and consonants with cedilla hooks (Ģ Ķ Ļ Ņ).
clue.lv-iela-street-label-description: The Latvian word for street is iela.
clue.lv-tall-rectangular-house-number-de: Latvian house number plates are often tall rectangles in several colours.
clue.lv-architecture-description: Latvian buildings mix wood and white brick under steep corrugated metal roofs; pastel-painted stone and wood-brick houses are common.
clue.lv-directional-sign-description: Latvian directional signs are blue with white text and stylised arrowheads.
clue.lv-open-plains-south-jelgava-descri: South of Jelgava features wide-open fields with less forest than elsewhere in Latvia.
clue.lv-country-flag-description: The national flag of Latvia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.lb-mediterranean-landscape-descript: Lebanon's terrain is Mediterranean, hilly, with rocky cliffs and green vegetation.
clue.lb-metallic-mesh-pole-description: Lebanon uses metallic mesh (lattice) utility poles, sometimes bright yellow; wooden poles also appear.
clue.lb-sandstone-brick-building-descrip: Many Lebanese buildings are made from pale sandstone blocks.
clue.lb-zahle-agricultural-field-descrip: Zahle area features flat farmland with mountains visible to the northwest.
clue.lb-snow-capped-mountain-description: Snow covers mountaintops or ground in northeastern mountains east of Tripoli.
clue.lb-flat-northern-plain-description: Northern Lebanon is flat and agricultural, with mountains visible to the southeast.
clue.lb-trekker-coverage-overview-descri: Lebanese trekker imagery is sparse, mostly around tourist sites, campuses, and trails.
clue.lb-beirut-description: The capital has many modern high-rises; urban structures or infrastructure are almost always visible.
clue.lb-country-flag-description: The national flag of Lebanon is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ls-licence-plate-description: Lesotho plates are long and white with blue text and a Mokorotlo hat symbol on the left.
clue.ls-road-line-description: Lesotho's edge lines are yellow and centre lines are white.
clue.ls-triple-centre-line-description: Some Lesotho roads have a unique triple centre-line: two solid lines flanking a dashed line.
clue.ls-agave-plant-description: Agave plants are widespread in Lesotho countryside.
clue.ls-traditional-basotho-blanket-desc: Many people, especially in rural areas, wear traditional Basotho woollen blankets.
clue.ls-free-roaming-livestock-descripti: Lesotho's roads are frequently shared with wandering cattle, horses, donkeys, and other farm animals.
clue.ls-flat-western-region-description: The western lowlands are flat or gently hilly with visible tabletop mountains, dense coverage, settlements, and agriculture.
clue.ls-mountainous-eastern-region-descr: In the east, roads run along grassy mountainsides with limited coverage on six main roads.
clue.ls-country-flag-description: The national flag of Lesotho is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.li-liemobil-bus-stop-description: Bus stop signs are green-and-white with a black frame and 'LIEMOBIL' across the top.
clue.li-direction-sign-description: Directional signs are white for minor roads and blue for major roads, each with a pointed arrowhead.
clue.li-pedestrian-sign-description: Pedestrian crossing signs have seven stripes and a tall rectangular shape.
clue.li-yellow-black-road-separator-desc: Striped road separators have a rounded top, small knob, and three bands of yellow and black.
clue.li-metal-sign-border-description: Road signs commonly have a round grey metal border.
clue.li-architecture-description: Architecture ranges from traditional Alpine chalets to modern structures, more modern in larger settlements.
clue.li-eastern-mountain-coverage-descri: Mountains are visible in every direction east of the central ridge.
clue.li-blue-street-sign-description: Blue street signs with a thin white border appear in the south and around Bendern.
clue.li-flat-black-sign-description: Plain flat black street signs indicate eastern Liechtenstein.
clue.li-brown-fraktur-sign-description: Brown street signs with traditional German-style typeface and white border are found in Vaduz and northern towns.
clue.li-country-flag-description: The national flag of Liechtenstein is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-general-01-16-square-poles-descr: In Lithuania, utility poles are usually square concrete posts with a diagonal support beam.
clue.lt-poletop-style-description: Lithuanian poletops often have short horizontal rods holding insulators, sometimes in a trident pattern.
clue.lt-chevron-description: Lithuanian chevrons are white with red arrows; small variants have a red outline.
clue.lt-kilometre-marker-description: Lithuanian blue L-shaped km markers are mounted at a 45° angle toward the road.
clue.lt-warning-speed-sign-border-descri: Lithuanian warning and speed signs have a thin red border with a thin white outline.
clue.lt-guardrail-orange-reflector-descr: Lithuanian guardrails are standard A-type with orange reflectors.
clue.lt-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Lithuanian crossing signs show three stripes and a low-detail pedestrian figure.
clue.lt-bus-stop-sign-description: Lithuanian bus stop signs feature a bus icon with four windows.
clue.lt-lithuanian-language-description: A Baltic language with hooked vowels (Ą Ę Į Ų), Ė with a dot, and the letter Y.
clue.lt-gatve-street-label-description: The word for street is gatvė, often abbreviated as g. on signs.
clue.lt-place-name-ending-ai-description: Many Lithuanian town and village names end in -ai.
clue.lt-architecture-description: Buildings are light-coloured brick with steep corrugated metal roofs; wooden and pastel-painted stone houses also appear.
clue.lt-directional-sign-description: Directional signs are blue with white text and arrowheads with straight vertical back edges.
clue.lt-open-agricultural-landscape-desc: Lithuania has less forest cover, giving the countryside an open, agricultural feel.
clue.lt-topography-description: Although Lithuania is largely flat, the southeast is the hilliest region.
clue.lt-bilingual-polish-sign-southeast-: In southeastern Lithuania, bilingual Lithuanian-Polish signs occasionally appear.
clue.lt-country-flag-description: The national flag of Lithuania is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.lu-bollard-description: Black-and-white wedge-shaped bollards with grey reflectors; some have a lower indent.
clue.lu-chevron-description: Chevrons are black with yellow arrows; a blue-and-yellow variant also appears.
clue.lu-upside-down-trident-poletop-desc: Common pole tops shaped like inverted tridents.
clue.lu-multilingual-signage-description: French dominates public signage; German and Luxembourgish also appear.
clue.lu-luxembourgish-language-descripti: Closely related to German with umlauts, double vowels, and accented é.
clue.lu-town-entrance-sign-description: Yellow framed, often bilingual signs showing road number and speed limit.
clue.lu-square-cornered-frame-descriptio: Metal frames around signs and road infrastructure are common.
clue.lu-street-name-sign-description: Typically short, white-backed signs; a common variant has slanted blue corners.
clue.lu-blue-white-signpost-reflector-de: Some signposts have bulky round blue-and-white reflectors.
clue.lu-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Pedestrian signs display five vertical stripes.
clue.lu-bus-stop-sign-description: Blue bus stop signs with a bus icon showing six windows.
clue.lu-rolling-hill-landscape-descripti: Landscape dominated by green rolling hills with farmland and forest patches.
clue.lu-local-road-number-description: Three-digit local road numbers grouped geographically by first digit.
clue.lu-topography-description: Northern half is higher and hillier than the flatter south.
clue.lu-vineyard-description: Vineyards are concentrated in the southeast.
clue.lu-country-flag-description: The national flag of Luxembourg is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-license-plates-01-02-black-licen: In Macau, cars have black licence plates.
clue.mo-lamp-post-description: Macau uses cylindrical grey lamp posts with black-painted bases.
clue.xx-general-01-07-portuguese-signs-d: Portuguese often appears alongside Chinese on signs in Macau, reflecting its history as a Portuguese colony.
clue.mo-bilingual-street-sign-descriptio: White signs with blue borders show Chinese and Portuguese street names, unique to Macau.
clue.mo-casino-gambling-description: Casinos and gambling ads are everywhere, often with extravagant architecture.
clue.mo-dense-northern-half-description: Northern Macau has tightly packed apartments, narrow gridded streets, and cars lining both sides.
clue.mo-hilly-southern-area-description: Southern Macau is hilly and rural, with narrow roads winding through trees and distinctive lamp posts.
clue.mo-country-flag-description: The national flag of Macau is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-general-01-02-north-macedonian-b: One type of bollard in North Macedonia has a trapezoid shape, colored white and black, with a red reflective strip.
clue.mk-guardrail-description: North Macedonian guardrails are A-profile with red reflectors.
clue.xx-general-01-01-north-macedonian-s: In North Macedonia, road signs are yellow and black, and town names appear in both Latin and Cyrillic alphabets.
clue.mk-macedonian-cyrillic-description: A Slavic language in Cyrillic with unique letters Ѓ and Ќ; road signs include Latin transliterations.
clue.mk-highway-dominated-rural-coverage: Rural coverage is mostly confined to highways due to limited road mapping.
clue.mk-landscape-description: Countryside has dry grasslands with low hills and scattered trees.
clue.mk-greek-lamp-pole-description: Distinctive lamp style on utility poles, also found in Greece and Serbia.
clue.mk-yellow-warning-sign-description: Warning signs have yellow backgrounds instead of white.
clue.mk-winter-coverage-city-description: Winter imagery appears in Skopje, Tetovo, Prilep, Bitola, and Ohrid.
clue.mk-divided-road-overview-descriptio: Several highways are divided with distinct median features.
clue.mk-obituary-posters-description: Cities have distinct public obituary poster styles on utility poles, identified by colour, orientation, and border design.
clue.mk-prilep-obituary-description: Vertical black posters with incomplete borders.
clue.mk-tetovo-obituary-description: Vertical black posters with two variants of cross placement.
clue.mk-prilep-rectangular-lamps-descrip: Long rectangular lamp fixtures exclusive to Prilep.
clue.mk-prilep-rocky-hills-description: Two extremely rocky, bare hills visible from parts of Prilep.
clue.mk-country-flag-description: The national flag of North Macedonia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.mg-french-malagasy-language-descrip: Madagascar's official languages are French and Malagasy, which uses the Latin alphabet and long, multi-syllable words.
clue.mg-limited-trekker-coverage-descrip: Street View in Madagascar is sparse, mainly along or near the west coast, mostly from trekkers with two exceptions using a Street View car.
clue.mg-southern-atolls-broad-leaved-pal: Atolls are small and have broad-leaved palms, a tree type rare elsewhere on the island.
clue.mg-country-flag-description: The national flag of Madagascar is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.my-thick-yellow-road-bars-descripti: Bold yellow bars painted across roads are nearly exclusive to Malaysia.
clue.my-pole-stickers-description: Malaysian utility poles often have black or white stickers, sometimes with red-and-white or red-and-blue bands below.
clue.my-bollards-description: Malaysian bollards combine black, white, grey, and red colours with consistent layout variants.
clue.my-hexagonal-yellow-highway-shields: Directional signs feature hexagonal yellow highway shields found only in Malaysia.
clue.my-kilometre-markers-description: Malaysian km markers use a distinctive white-and-blue scheme, often with the hexagonal highway shield.
clue.my-malay-language-description: Malay is written in Latin script and is very close to Indonesian.
clue.my-chinese-characters-description: Chinese script appears frequently on Malaysian signage, reflecting its significant ethnic Chinese population.
clue.my-black-white-signposts-descriptio: Malaysian sign poles are almost always painted with alternating black-and-white stripes.
clue.my-black-white-kerbs-description: Kerbs painted in black-and-white are a common Malaysian roadside feature.
clue.my-12-johor-description: Road signs in Johor feature a large capital 'J' at the start of the route number.
clue.my-12-kedah-description: Kedah state roads have a bold 'K' prefix before the road number.
clue.my-12-kelantan-description: Kelantan state roads use a 'D' prefix on their signs.
clue.my-12-melaka-description: Melaka state roads start with a capital 'M'.
clue.my-12-negeri-sembilan-description: Negeri Sembilan state roads begin with a large 'N'.
clue.my-12-pahang-description: Pahang state roads use a 'C' prefix on their signs.
clue.my-12-perak-description: Perak state roads have an 'A' prefix at the start of road numbers.
clue.my-12-perlis-description: Perlis state roads have an 'R' prefix before the route number.
clue.my-12-penang-description: Penang state roads start with a 'P' prefix.
clue.my-12-sabah-description: Sabah state roads use an 'SA' prefix before the route number.
clue.my-12-sarawak-description: Sarawak state roads have a 'Q' prefix at the start of the route number.
clue.my-12-selangor-description: Selangor state roads feature a 'B' prefix before the route number.
clue.my-12-terengganu-description: Terengganu state roads start with a 'T' prefix.
clue.xx-general-01-40-marked-poles-descr: In mainland Malaysia, electricity poles often have black stickers on them.
clue.my-tel-tnb-stickers-johor-descripti: Black pole stickers with "TEL TNB" text are exclusive to Johor.
clue.my-white-pole-stickers-sarawak-desc: White stickers on electricity poles are found only in Sarawak.
clue.my-double-circle-lamp-posts-mainlan: Lamp posts with two small circles on the support arm are mainly on Peninsular Malaysia.
clue.my-triangular-lamp-post-support-mai: Lamp posts braced by a triangular sheet-metal support are mainly a mainland feature.
clue.my-2-1-insulator-poles-sarawak-desc: Wooden electricity poles with a 2-1 insulator layout and long diagonal support are exclusive to Sarawak.
clue.my-parallel-poletops-sabah-descript: Thin metal poles with two parallel horizontal arms at the top are exclusive to Sabah.
clue.my-boomerang-lamp-posts-sarawak-des: Lamp posts with a boomerang-shaped sheet-metal support are found in Sarawak.
clue.my-s-logo-bins-negeri-sembilan-mala: S-Logo Bins, Negeri Sembilan / Malacca / Johor
Rubbish bins with an "S"-like logo are found in Negeri Sembilan, Malacca, and Johor.
clue.my-leaf-logo-bins-perlis-kedah-desc: Rubbish bins with a leaf-like logo are found in Perlis and Kedah.
clue.my-alam-flora-bins-pahang-kl-putraj: Alam Flora Bins, Pahang / KL / Putrajaya
Bins with a sunny landscape logo and "Alam Flora" text are found in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya.
clue.my-yellow-street-name-signs-johor-d: Yellow arrow-shaped street name signs are specific to Johor.
clue.my-green-jkr-street-signs-sabah-des: Green arrow-shaped street signs with a yellow hexagonal JKR symbol are found in Sabah.
clue.my-mountainous-sabah-flat-sarawak-d: Sabah is mountainous with steep roads; Sarawak is generally flatter.
clue.my-isolated-rock-formations-perlis-: Dramatic rock formations rising sharply from flat terrain are found near the Thai border in Perlis.
clue.my-labuan-blue-bins-description: Blue cylindrical containers are common in urban areas on Labuan island.
clue.my-country-flag-description: The national flag of Malaysia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ml-coverage-overview-description: Mali has very limited coverage: ten small trekker segments across seven locations.
clue.ml-historic-mud-brick-mosque-descri: Tripod segments focus on historic mud-brick mosques with wooden sticks protruding from walls and adobe interiors.
clue.ml-pinpointable-vs-nonpinpointable-: Mosque exterior coverage including surrounding streets can appear in pinpointable maps. Interiors are not pinpointable.
clue.ml-arid-landscape-description: The country is very dry with sandy, barren settings that distinguish Malian tripod coverage.
clue.ml-sidi-yahiya-mosque-exterior-desc: Streets mix sand and bread-slice-shaped tiles. Buildings are peachy-orange bricks with brown undertones. The area feels busier than around Djingareyber mosque.
clue.ml-sidi-yahiya-mosque-interior-desc: Yellow-painted walls with unpainted bricks at the base. Courtyard has brick walls and bright square tile floor.
clue.ml-djingareyber-mosque-exterior-des: Brick buildings along a paved street with rectangular tiles.
clue.ml-djingareyber-mosque-interior-des: Yellow-painted walls, wide rounded archways, and red carpet throughout.
clue.ml-sankore-mosque-exterior-descript: Surrounded by very sandy ground with a prominent pyramid-shaped tower.
clue.ml-sankore-mosque-doors-description: Ornately carved wooden doors decorated with metal details.
clue.ml-sankore-mosque-interior-descript: Blue carpet, yellow-painted walls, and a low ceiling held up by wooden beams.
clue.ml-country-flag-description: The national flag of Mali is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.mt-licence-plate-description: Maltese plates have the European blue strip and commonly short plates.
clue.mt-limestone-rock-walls-description: Dry limestone rock walls line roads and fields across Malta and are very common.
clue.mt-architecture-01-limestone-descri: You will see a lot of walls and buildings made from limestone in Malta.
clue.mt-covered-balconies-description: Traditional enclosed balconies projecting from facades are a hallmark of Malta, often brightly painted.
clue.mt-language-01-nice-trick-for-malta: Triq is the Maltese word for street and it will only show up in Malta.
clue.mt-bus-stop-description: Maltese bus stops often display route numbers or destination names.
clue.mt-double-yellow-no-parking-lines-d: Double yellow kerb lines indicate no-parking zones in Malta.
clue.mt-maltese-language-description: Maltese uses Latin script with unique characters: Ċ/ċ, Ġ/ġ, Ħ/ħ, and Ż/ż on signage.
clue.mt-country-flag-description: The national flag of Malta is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.mq-coastal-southern-trekker-descrip: A walking trek along the southern coast passes orange-roofed houses, open stretches with ocean views, and ends at a car park with stalls.
clue.mq-country-flag-description: The national flag of Martinique is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.mx-licence-plate-description: Mexican licence plates are short, vary by state, and both front and rear plates are mandatory.
clue.mx-yellow-centre-road-lines-descrip: Mexican roads have solid white edge lines with a single continuous yellow stripe down the middle.
clue.mx-bollards-01-mexican-bollards-des: Mexico uses round, white bollards with a black base.
clue.mx-road-shield-description: National highways use curved shields with "MEXICO"; state roads use straight-edged shields with state initials.
clue.mx-all-caps-directional-signs-descr: Mexican directional signs feature large, bold, white uppercase lettering.
clue.mx-kilometre-markers-description: Mexican highway distance markers are white posts with black text and borders.
clue.mx-cacti-description: A huge diversity of cactus species makes them a common sight across Mexico.
clue.mx-thick-arrows-signs-description: Mexican road sign arrows are distinctly thick and bold.
clue.mx-yellow-painted-kerbs-barriers-de: Kerbs and bridge barriers are frequently painted yellow in Mexico.
clue.mx-rooftop-water-tanks-description: Wide cylindrical water tanks, usually black or white, are common on Mexican rooftops.
clue.mx-oxxo-pemex-brands-description: OXXO stores and Pemex fuel stations are common commercial brands along Mexican roads.
clue.mx-nahuatl-origin-place-names-descr: Many towns have Nahuatl-derived names with 'x', 'tl', and endings like '-ec' and '-tlan'.
clue.xx-general-01-17-electricity-meters: Mexico, along with several Central American countries, uses circular electricity meters.
clue.mx-american-car-brands-pickup-truck: American Car Brands and Pickup Trucks
US vehicle brands and pickup trucks are very popular on Mexican roads.
clue.mx-area-code-regions-description: The first digit of Mexican phone area codes corresponds to geographic regions.
clue.mx-postal-code-regions-description: Mexican postal codes are alphabetically ordered by state and often appear on street signs.
clue.mx-21-aguascalientes-description: Aguascalientes plates have a white background with a red stripe, state name, and grape cluster graphic.
clue.mx-21-baja-california-description: Baja California plates have a white background with blue accents and a coastline or whale tail image.
clue.mx-21-baja-california-sur-descripti: Baja California Sur plates have a white background with turquoise elements, cactus or desert motifs, and the state name.
clue.mx-21-campeche-description: Campeche plates have a white background with green and red elements, often featuring a Mayan pyramid or local emblem, and the state name in green.
clue.mx-21-chiapas-description: Chiapas plates have a white base with red and green details, typically showing the state outline or a jaguar head, and the state name in red.
clue.mx-21-chihuahua-description: Chihuahua plates feature a white background with blue and red elements, often displaying the state coat of arms and the name 'Chihuahua' in blue.
clue.mx-21-coahuila-description: Coahuila plates show a white background with green and red accents, including the state coat of arms and the word 'Coahuila' in green.
clue.mx-21-colima-description: Colima plates use a white background with blue and red features, often displaying a volcano or palm tree graphic and the state name in blue.
clue.mx-21-durango-description: Durango plates have a white background with green and gold elements, typically featuring a mountain or mining symbol and the state name in green.
clue.mx-21-guanajuato-description: Guanajuato plates display a white background with blue and red accents, often showing a colonial building or the state coat of arms, with 'Guanajuato' in blue.
clue.mx-21-guerrero-description: Guerrero plates feature a white background with green and red highlights, usually including an image of Acapulco bay or a local emblem, and 'Guerrero' in green.
clue.mx-21-hidalgo-description: Hidalgo plates have a white background with blue and green elements, often displaying a mountain or aqueduct motif and the state name in blue.
clue.mx-21-jalisco-description: Jalisco plates use a white background with blue and gold accents, typically featuring the state coat of arms and the name 'Jalisco' in blue.
clue.mx-21-mexico-city-description: Mexico City plates have a white background with pink and black elements, including the 'CDMX' abbreviation and city landmarks or the Angel of Independence.
clue.mx-21-mexico-description: Estado de México plates feature a white background with red and green accents, often showing the state coat of arms and the name 'Edomex' or 'Estado de México' in red.
clue.mx-21-michoac-n-description: Michoacán plates display a white background with green and red elements, typically featuring a butterfly or the state coat of arms, and 'Michoacán' in green.
clue.mx-21-morelos-description: Morelos plates have a white background with purple and green accents, often showing a flower or the state coat of arms, and 'Morelos' in purple.
clue.mx-21-nayarit-description: Nayarit plates use a white background with blue and green elements, typically featuring a beach or palm tree graphic and the state name in blue.
clue.mx-21-nuevo-le-n-description: Nuevo León plates feature a white background with blue and yellow accents, often displaying the state coat of arms and the name 'Nuevo León' in blue.
clue.mx-21-oaxaca-description: Oaxaca plates have a white background with green and red elements, typically featuring a Zapotec motif or the state coat of arms, and 'Oaxaca' in green.
clue.mx-21-puebla-description: Puebla plates display a white background with blue and red accents, often showing the state coat of arms and the name 'Puebla' in blue.
clue.mx-21-quer-taro-description: Querétaro plates use a white background with blue and gold elements, typically featuring an aqueduct or the state coat of arms, and 'Querétaro' in blue.
clue.mx-21-quintana-roo-description: Quintana Roo plates feature a white background with turquoise and yellow accents, often displaying a palm tree or beach scene and the state name in turquoise.
clue.mx-21-san-luis-potos-description: San Luis Potosí plates have a white background with green and red elements, typically featuring a mining motif or the state coat of arms, and 'San Luis Potosí' in green.
clue.mx-21-sinaloa-description: Sinaloa plates display a white background with red and green accents, often showing a tomato or the state coat of arms, and 'Sinaloa' in red.
clue.mx-21-sonora-description: Sonora plates feature a white background with orange and blue accents, typically displaying a desert scene or the state coat of arms, and 'Sonora' in orange.
clue.mx-21-tabasco-description: Tabasco plates have a white background with green and blue elements, often featuring a river or the state coat of arms, and 'Tabasco' in green.
clue.mx-21-tamaulipas-description: Tamaulipas plates use a white background with blue and green accents, typically displaying a mountain or the state coat of arms, and 'Tamaulipas' in blue.
clue.mx-21-tlaxcala-description: Tlaxcala plates feature a white background with red and green elements, often showing a bull or the state coat of arms, and 'Tlaxcala' in red.
clue.mx-21-veracruz-description: Veracruz plates have a white background with blue and green accents, typically featuring a harp or the state coat of arms, and 'Veracruz' in blue.
clue.mx-21-yucat-n-description: Yucatán plates display a white background with green and yellow elements, often showing a Mayan pyramid or the state coat of arms, and 'Yucatán' in green.
clue.mx-21-zacatecas-description: Zacatecas plates feature a white background with green and red accents, typically displaying a mining cart or the state coat of arms, and 'Zacatecas' in green.
clue.mx-prickly-pear-cacti-description: Prickly pear cacti, identifiable by their flat, oval-shaped pads, appear far more frequently in the central highlands.
clue.mx-pulque-agaves-description: Agave salmiana has broad, smooth, curling leaves forming a crown-like silhouette, thriving in the central valley and around San Luis Potosi.
clue.mx-blue-agave-fields-description: Extensive blue agave plantations for tequila are concentrated in Jalisco and Nayarit.
clue.mx-tree-yucca-description: Yucca filifera and Yucca decipiens grow as single-trunked trees with oblong rosettes of sharp green leaves, concentrated in San Luis Potosi, Zacatecas, and nearby states.
clue.mx-mexican-giant-cardon-cactus-desc: A prevalent Baja California cactus with large sprawling arms branching from a single trunk and ribbed surface.
clue.mx-saguaro-cactus-description: Found in western Sonora, featuring a tall main trunk with short, upward-curving arms.
clue.mx-organ-pipe-cactus-description: Cactus with long, slender stems emerging near ground level, mainly in Sonora and occasionally Baja California Sur.
clue.mx-blue-myrtle-cactus-description: Cactus with short arms curving uniformly upward, abundant in San Luis Potosi, Queretaro, and Hidalgo.
clue.mx-sugar-cane-description: Sugar cane is cultivated widely but most prevalent in Veracruz.
clue.mx-coconut-palm-description: Coconut palms line coastal areas, especially dense in Guerrero and Colima.
clue.mx-sabal-palm-description: Sabal palms have spiky, sun-shaped crowns giving a lollipop silhouette, growing along Mexico's east coast, Yucatan, and Nayarit.
clue.mx-attalea-rostrata-palm-descriptio: Large palm with erect, umbrella-like fronds, found mainly in Veracruz and Tabasco.
clue.mx-oil-palm-plantations-description: Orderly rows of oil palms concentrated in Chiapas, with scattered plantations in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.
clue.mx-boojum-trees-description: Trees with alien, tentacle-like trunks nearly exclusive to southern Baja California peninsula.
clue.mx-brittlebush-description: Low shrub with bright silver-grey foliage, common in Sonora near Hermosillo.
clue.mx-thin-white-barked-trees-descript: Slender trees with pale white bark across the Yucatan peninsula, especially in Quintana Roo.
clue.mx-golden-roadside-grass-tufts-desc: Lines of golden grass tufts growing immediately beside roads in Coahuila.
clue.mx-teardrop-grass-clumps-descriptio: Grass growing in rounded, teardrop-shaped clumps typical in and around Tlaxcala.
clue.mx-red-agricultural-fields-zacateca: Fields with distinctly red soil frequent in Zacatecas and southern Durango.
clue.mx-northern-pine-forest-description: Rocky, mountainous terrain with pine forests in western Chihuahua and Durango; northern pines are shorter and stunted.
clue.mx-dark-field-guanajuato-descriptio: Extremely dark-coloured agricultural fields common in Guanajuato.
clue.mx-reddish-brown-hills-northern-baj: Hills with reddish-brown tint and large boulders in northern Baja California peninsula.
clue.mx-bright-white-soil-quintana-roo-t: Bright White Soil in Quintana Roo
clue.mx-bright-white-soil-quintana-roo-d: Intensely white, almost blinding soil in the Yucatan peninsula, most common in Quintana Roo.
clue.mx-red-fields-northern-campeche-des: Red-earth farmland bordered by dense tropical forest in northern Campeche.
clue.mx-red-brick-buildings-description: Exposed red brick construction concentrated west of Mexico City in Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.
clue.mx-white-concrete-block-buildings-d: White concrete block structures cluster near Mexico City and become more common eastward.
clue.mx-mud-brick-buildings-description: Adobe-style mud brick construction prevalent in Durango and scattered across northern arid states.
clue.mx-northern-mexican-architecture-de: Homes with pastel facades, gated yards, and orange Spanish colonial roof tiles common in northern Mexico.
clue.mx-thatched-roofs-description: Buildings with thatched roofing are prevalent in the Yucatan peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosi.
clue.mx-light-coloured-rock-walls-descri: Low walls of pale limestone across the Yucatan peninsula, especially in Yucatan state.
clue.mx-cross-sign-backs-chihuahua-title: Cross on Sign Backs in Chihuahua
clue.mx-cross-sign-backs-chihuahua-descr: Road signs in Chihuahua have a thick cross printed on their reverse side.
clue.mx-red-banded-bollards-nayarit-desc: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit.
clue.mx-jalisco-bollards-crown-emblem-de: Some Jalisco bollards bear a crown symbol and the word "Jalisco".
clue.mx-acorn-shaped-white-insulators-de: Small white insulators resembling acorns sit atop power poles in coastal states, especially Michoacan, Colima, and Veracruz.
clue.mx-asymmetric-crossbar-poles-descri: Power poles with an off-centre crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.
clue.mx-wooden-poles-lowered-crossbar-de: Wooden utility poles with a noticeably lower crossbar are mainly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.
clue.mx-hanging-insulators-concrete-pole: Concrete power poles with insulators hanging below the crossbar are typical of the Yucatan peninsula.
clue.mx-wooden-hanging-insulator-poles-b: Wooden poles with hanging insulators are found on the Baja California peninsula.
clue.mx-single-support-beam-poles-durang: Utility poles with a lowered crossbar braced by a single diagonal support beam are specific to Durango.
clue.mx-mesh-body-poles-description: Utility poles with a lattice or mesh body are common in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.
clue.mx-white-centre-road-lines-tabasco-: Roads in Tabasco commonly use white centre lines instead of yellow.
clue.mx-red-barked-tree-fences-veracruz-: Living fences made from trees with reddish bark are characteristic of Veracruz.
clue.mx-black-tar-centre-lines-descripti: Black tar patches flanking yellow centre lines appear in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.
clue.mx-grainy-blue-grey-pavement-descri: Coarse-textured road surfaces with a blue-grey tinge are typical of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.
clue.mx-irregular-cobblestone-pavement-d: Streets paved with randomly arranged, irregular cobblestones are widespread in central Mexico, especially Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.
clue.mx-hexagonal-tile-pavement-descript: Streets surfaced with interlocking hexagonal tiles are distinctive of Puebla and Tlaxcala.
clue.mx-three-line-cobblestone-pavement-: A cobblestone pattern with three parallel lines of stones is mainly associated with Oaxaca.
clue.mx-mexicali-farmland-brown-wooden-p: Mexicali features flat farmland, a western ridge, Washingtonia palms, and brown wooden utility poles.
clue.mx-sierra-del-abra-tanchipa-ridge-d: A long, flat-topped ridge in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve is visible from roads in eastern San Luis Potosi.
clue.mx-country-flag-description: The national flag of Mexico is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.mc-location-description: A European microstate on the French Riviera, west of the Italian border.
clue.mc-licence-plate-description: Monaco plates are short and lack the blue EU strip.
clue.mc-hilly-terrain-description: Monaco's terrain is hilly with Mediterranean vegetation in open patches.
clue.mc-palm-tree-description: Ornamental palm trees line Monaco's streets and boulevards.
clue.mc-tunnel-description: Much of Monaco's coverage passes through tunnels.
clue.mc-parked-moped-description: Rows of parked mopeds line many Monaco streets.
clue.mc-country-flag-description: The national flag of Monaco is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.mn-licence-plate-red-soyombo-title: Licence Plates with Red Soyombo Symbol
clue.mn-licence-plate-red-soyombo-descri: Mongolian plates are mostly white with a red Soyombo emblem on the left side.
clue.mn-cyrillic-unique-letters-descript: Mongolian Cyrillic includes extra letters Ɵ and Ү and often uses doubled vowels like aa, ƟƟ, or ЭЭ.
clue.xx-general-01-42-tent-car-descripti: In Mongolia the google car is often visible. It takes many shapes but usually a tent can be seen packed on the car.
clue.mn-general-01-vast-landscapes-descr: The Mongolian landscape is often barren, featuring large open areas without much vegetation.
clue.mn-bollards-01-strike-description: The Mongolian bollard is reminiscent of a bowling pin.
clue.mn-dirt-alleys-wooden-fences-descri: Residential areas divided by unpaved dirt alleys lined with wooden fencing.
clue.mn-traditional-yurt-description: Round white yurts, traditional homes of Mongolian nomads, are common throughout the country.
clue.mn-livestock-herd-description: Large groups of roadside animals including horses, yaks, cattle, sheep, goats, and camels.
clue.mn-street-view-coverage-map-descrip: Sparse coverage concentrated along major highways and larger towns, densest around Ulaanbaatar.
clue.mn-driving-direction-away-ulaanbaat: Street View car generally heads outward from the capital, so driving direction points away from Ulaanbaatar.
clue.mn-topography-flat-east-mountainous: East and south are flat, north has rolling hills, west has large mountains and rocky terrain.
clue.mn-northern-forest-description: Forested areas with Siberian Larch, pine, and birch appear throughout northern Mongolia.
clue.mn-flat-grassy-plains-far-east-titl: Flat Grassy Plains in the Far East
clue.mn-flat-grassy-plains-far-east-desc: Narrow dirt tracks cut through vast, treeless grasslands in Mongolia's far east.
clue.mn-off-road-desert-coverage-south-t: Off-Road Desert Coverage in the South
clue.mn-off-road-desert-coverage-south-d: Unpaved desert tracks appear south or east of Mandalgovi.
clue.mn-paved-desert-road-south-title: Paved Desert Roads in the South
clue.mn-paved-desert-road-south-descript: A few paved highways cross the southern desert region.
clue.mn-arid-steppe-rangeland-southwest-: Arid Steppe Rangeland in the Southwest
Dry steppe rangeland with coarse soil, sparse grass, and scattered low shrubs.
clue.mn-dry-rugged-mountains-far-west-ti: Dry Rugged Mountains in the Far West
clue.mn-dry-rugged-mountains-far-west-de: Barren, rugged hills and mountains with no vegetation in the far west.
clue.mn-lake-river-west-title: Lakes and Rivers in the West
clue.mn-lake-river-west-description: Lakes and rivers appear more frequently in western Mongolia.
clue.mn-snow-coverage-near-ulaanbaatar-d: Snowy Street View imagery is concentrated around Ulaanbaatar.
clue.mn-fall-foliage-coverage-descriptio: Autumn imagery shows vivid orange trees and grass mainly between Lun and Hatgal, and near Ulaanbaatar.
clue.mn-rare-crop-field-selenge-tov-desc: Agricultural fields appear occasionally in Selenge and Töv provinces near Ulaanbaatar.
clue.mn-ulaanbaatar-cityscape-descriptio: The capital has high-rises, chain stores, heavy traffic, buses, pedestrians, maintained roads, and sprawling yurt suburbs on hills.
clue.mn-spare-tire-variation-description: The spare tire on the back right of the Street View truck divides Mongolia into four zones by tire type and presence.
clue.mn-light-blue-tent-forward-snorkel-: Light Blue Tent with Forward Snorkel
In eastern grasslands, the Street View truck has a light blue tent and a forward-facing snorkel intake.
clue.mn-orange-roof-rack-strap-descripti: Eastern Mongolia sub-areas can be identified by orange strap arrangements on roof racks, visible from above.
clue.mn-bright-silver-tent-description: A bright silver tent on the Street View truck is typical in central and northwestern Mongolia.
clue.mn-cage-roof-rack-description: Near Ulaanbaatar, some coverage shows a metal cage replacing the tent, often with a green camouflage sleeping bag on top.
clue.mn-gen-4-silver-truck-ulaanbaatar-t: White and Blue Truck in Ulaanbaatar
clue.mn-gen-4-silver-truck-ulaanbaatar-d: Some imagery in the capital uses a truck with an ornate blue-and-white roof decal.
clue.mn-western-mongolia-snow-peaks-glac: Western Mongolia features the tallest mountains with glaciers and snow, and a Street View car with a green or black bag on the roof.
clue.mn-shrubland-east-uvs-lake-descript: East of Uvs Lake has abundant small shrubs and patchy grass on flat terrain.
clue.mn-nighttime-coverage-description: After-dark imagery appears in four main areas, with the car heading toward the nearest town.
clue.mn-country-flag-description: The national flag of Mongolia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.me-chevron-description: Montenegro uses black-on-white and red-on-yellow chevrons.
clue.me-utility-pole-description: Montenegro uses simple round concrete or wooden utility poles.
clue.me-northern-agricultural-valley-des: Green valleys with deforested hillsides cleared for farming are common in northern Montenegro.
clue.me-dry-mountain-podgorica-descripti: Barren, treeless mountains characterise the area around and south of Podgorica. Vineyards are also common.
clue.me-pine-forest-description: Pine forests appear mainly in the east, with smaller patches in the north and north of Nikšić.
clue.me-podgorica-description: The capital and largest city, identifiable by modern buildings, wide roads, and updated infrastructure.
clue.me-cemi-river-valley-terrace-descri: Distinctive staircase-like terraced mountainsides line the Cemi River Valley.
clue.me-country-flag-description: The national flag of Montenegro is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.n-general-01-road-lines-description: Like many countries in Southern Africa, Namibia uses roads with single yellow outer lines and white center lines.
clue.na-green-directional-signs-yellow-r: Green Directional Signs with Yellow Road Numbers
Directional signs are green with yellow route numbers using A, B, C, D, M, and sometimes F designations.
clue.na-small-stone-bollards-description: Short stone bollards are common along Namibian roadsides and intersections.
clue.na-green-white-metal-bins-descripti: Cylindrical metal rubbish bins painted green and white appear at rest stops and junctions.
clue.na-limited-coverage-minor-roads-des: Street View in Namibia is concentrated along major highways with scattered minor road coverage.
clue.na-pavement-type-driving-direction-: Pavement Type and Driving Direction Map
Map showing road surface types and Google car travel direction on major routes.
clue.na-telephone-area-codes-region-desc: Namibian area codes help pinpoint regions or cities.
clue.na-tall-lush-tree-north-title: Tall Lush Trees Indicate the North
clue.na-tall-lush-tree-north-description: Tall, leafy trees on both sides of the road indicate northern Namibia.
clue.na-agricultural-land-oshakati-descr: Northern Namibia near Oshakati has cultivated fields with light sandy soil and fan palms.
clue.na-botswana-like-landscape-east-win: East of Windhoek features flat, dry terrain with reddish earth, short grass, shrubs, and acacia trees.
clue.na-arid-mountain-west-south-title: Arid Mountains in the West and South
clue.na-arid-mountain-west-south-descrip: Western and southern Namibia have barren, dry mountains and rocky hills.
clue.na-greener-hill-northwest-descripti: Northwest hills and mountains have more vegetation with shrubs and trees.
clue.na-coastal-sandy-terrain-dune-descr: Flat sandy coastal areas with dunes occur around and north of Swakopmund and near Luderitz and Oranjemund.
clue.na-southeast-ridge-rollercoaster-ro: Southeast has small parallel ridges with red sandy soil; roads crossing them feel bumpy.
clue.na-60-kunene-region-title: Kunene C46 Poor Pavement & No Yellow Edges
clue.na-60-kunene-region-description: Near Ruacana, C46 lacks yellow edge lines, has poor cracked pavement, and dry flat terrain.
clue.na-60-omusati-region-title: Omusati C46 Low Sun & No Yellow Edges
clue.na-60-omusati-region-description: In Omusati, C46 lacks yellow edges, has poor pavement, flat terrain with sparse trees, and low sun.
clue.na-60-ohangwena-region-description: C41 in Ohangwena lacks yellow edges, runs northwest, with cloudier skies and flat terrain.
clue.na-60-kavango-west-region-title: Kavango West B10 Dense Vegetation & Moon
clue.na-60-kavango-west-region-descripti: East of Nkurenkuru, B10 lacks yellow edges, has dense vegetation, and a visible moon to the east.
clue.na-60-kavango-east-region-title: Kavango East B10 E-W Road with Heavy Vegetation
clue.na-60-kavango-east-region-descripti: West of Eenhana, B10 runs east-west without yellow edges, bordered by heavy vegetation.
clue.na-60-namibia-title: Namibia D3615 Faded Yellow Edge Lines
clue.na-60-namibia-description: D3615 has extremely faded yellow edge lines, a white dashed centre line, and dry surroundings.
clue.na-country-flag-description: The national flag of Namibia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.np-devanagari-script-description: Nepali text uses Devanagari, with a horizontal bar atop words and prominent vertical strokes.
clue.np-utility-pole-trident-top-descrip: Flat areas have square concrete poles; mountains use slender metal ones. Pole tops often have a trident shape.
clue.np-flat-south-mountainous-north-des: Southern Nepal is flat farmland; northern half has high-altitude mountain roads with dramatic elevation changes.
clue.np-building-style-triangle-decorati: Buildings range from colourful blocky structures to smaller houses with triangular ornamental motifs.
clue.np-black-white-striped-signpost-des: Sign poles feature alternating black and white stripes along their length.
clue.np-white-buddhist-stupa-description: White-painted Buddhist stupas, sometimes with painted eyes, are unique to Nepal.
clue.np-district-name-address-descriptio: District names often appear in postal addresses in English alongside Devanagari.
clue.np-flat-southern-plain-mountainous-: The far southern strip is flat; central and northern regions have steep, rugged terrain.
clue.np-dry-western-hill-description: Western hills have an arid look with large stretches of bare, unvegetated hillside.
clue.np-areca-palm-southeast-description: Areca palms with slender trunks and compact crowns grow mainly in southeastern lowlands.
clue.np-canola-field-yellow-flower-descr: Canola with vivid yellow blossoms grows in southern pockets of western Nepal.
clue.np-chir-pine-tree-description: Chir pines have smooth conical crowns with long needles, prevalent in the west and near Kathmandu.
clue.np-japanese-cedar-far-east-descript: Japanese cedars in far eastern Nepal are tall with narrow, feathery crowns.
clue.np-tea-plantation-far-east-descript: Tea cultivation occurs only in far eastern Nepal on mountain slopes and flatlands.
clue.np-rounded-roof-tile-description: Fully rounded clay roof tiles are common south of Kathmandu and westward.
clue.np-west-bengal-roof-tile-diamond-de: Tiles with small diamond-shaped bumps are concentrated in far western plains.
clue.np-irregular-rectangular-roof-tile-: Rectangular stone tiles laid unevenly are typical of western mountain towns and central areas.
clue.np-corrugated-metal-roof-descriptio: Corrugated sheet metal roofs are common between Birgunj and Janakpur.
clue.np-roof-railing-western-nepal-descr: Dark concrete railings run along roof edges in parts of western Nepal, especially Tulsipur valley.
clue.np-stick-fence-eastern-plain-descri: Fences made from sticks, varying in quality, are common in the eastern flatlands.
clue.np-sheet-metal-roof-triangular-wind: Sheet Metal Roofs with Triangular Window
Roofs in the far east are sheet metal with a small triangular window below the ridge and an outward-angled section beneath it.
clue.np-hip-roof-tiny-metal-ridge-title: Hip Roofs with Tiny Metal Ridge Protrusion
clue.np-hip-roof-tiny-metal-ridge-descri: Sheet metal hip roofs with a small metal protrusion at the ridge are found west of and around Biratnagar.
clue.np-mosque-southern-nepal-descriptio: Mosques cluster in Muslim-majority pockets along the southern belt near Janakpur, Birgunj, Nepalgunj, and Biratnagar.
clue.np-cross-topped-utility-pole-east-d: Utility poles with a cross-shaped attachment near the top are common in eastern Nepal.
clue.np-yellow-water-tank-east-descripti: Yellow rooftop water tanks are predominantly found in eastern Nepal.
clue.np-country-flag-description: The national flag of Nepal is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.nl-dutch-language-description: Dutch is a Germanic language with frequent double vowels and distinctive letter combinations like 'ij'.
clue.nl-dutch-bollard-description: Dutch bollards are plain white posts with a red reflector.
clue.nl-no-utility-pole-description: Street-level utility poles are essentially absent in the Netherlands; only large high-voltage towers appear.
clue.nl-abundant-waterway-description: Canals, ditches, dikes, dams, and bridges are constant, reflecting Dutch water management.
clue.nl-tree-lined-rural-road-descriptio: Dutch rural roads are often bordered by rows of trees on both sides, creating a tunnel effect.
clue.nl-organised-urban-planning-descrip: Dutch towns have neat, orderly layouts with well-maintained roads and uniform row houses.
clue.nl-all-white-road-marking-descripti: Dutch road lines are entirely white, with common dashed edge lines and occasional green centre lines.
clue.nl-bicycle-path-description: Dedicated cycling lanes run alongside many roads, often reddish-pink; cycling is a primary transport mode.
clue.nl-sidewalk-tile-description: Sidewalks typically use uniform square grey tiles in an offset pattern; historic areas may have brick paving.
clue.nl-striped-speed-bump-description: Dutch speed bumps have alternating long and short white warning stripes on brick or asphalt.
clue.nl-brick-rumble-strip-description: Rural roads often have brick-paved rumble strips along edges, unique to the Netherlands.
clue.nl-blue-street-sign-white-text-titl: Blue Street Signs with White Text
clue.nl-blue-street-sign-white-text-desc: Street name signs are nearly always blue with white lettering; common suffixes include -straat, -weg, -laan.
clue.nl-direction-sign-description: Motorist direction signs are blue with white text; cyclist signs are white with a red border.
clue.nl-blue-town-entry-sign-description: Town entry signs are blue, often with decorative frames and supplementary signs.
clue.nl-green-road-marker-description: Roadside kilometre markers are green with road numbers in coloured boxes: red for highways, yellow for regional roads.
clue.nl-road-sign-edge-behind-title: Road Sign Edges Visible from Behind
clue.nl-road-sign-edge-behind-descriptio: Dutch road signs have edges wrapping around to the back, creating a visible border.
clue.nl-striped-signpost-marking-descrip: Signpost poles often have black-and-white or blue-and-white striped bands.
clue.nl-bulky-yellow-signpost-title: Bulky Yellow Signposts on Traffic Islands
clue.nl-bulky-yellow-signpost-descriptio: Road signs on traffic islands are often mounted on thick, bright yellow posts.
clue.nl-striped-road-barrier-description: Red-and-white striped barriers are common along Dutch roads, especially rural areas.
clue.nl-brick-architecture-description: Buildings are mostly red-brown brick with roofs of orange or dark grey tiles.
clue.nl-row-house-description: Nearly half of Dutch homes are row houses (terraced houses).
clue.nl-windmill-turbine-description: Traditional windmills and modern wind turbines are common sights.
clue.nl-landline-area-code-description: Dutch landline numbers start with three- or four-digit area codes that are geographically grouped.
clue.nl-28-drenthe-description: Drenthe's N-road markers have a yellow box with the road number and often a 'DR' abbreviation or provincial logo.
clue.nl-28-flevoland-description: Flevoland's N-road markers show a yellow road number box, sometimes with 'Flevoland' or the province's blue-green logo.
clue.nl-28-friesland-description: Friesland's N-road markers have a yellow box with the road number and often 'FR' or Frisian flag motifs.
clue.nl-28-gelderland-description: Gelderland's N-road markers feature a yellow box with the road number and sometimes 'GLD' or the provincial logo.
clue.nl-28-groningen-description: Groningen's N-road markers show a yellow box with the road number and often 'GR' or the provincial flag pattern.
clue.nl-28-limburg-description: Limburg's N-road markers have a yellow box with the road number and sometimes 'LB' or a Limburg lion emblem or flag colors.
clue.nl-28-north-brabant-description: North Brabant's N-road markers feature a yellow box with the road number and sometimes 'NB' or the province's checkerboard flag motif.
clue.nl-28-north-holland-description: North Holland's N-road hectometre markers show a yellow road number box, sometimes with 'NH' or the province's blue and yellow flag colors or lion emblem.
clue.nl-28-overijssel-description: Overijssel's N-road hectometre markers use a yellow box for the road number, sometimes with 'OV' or the province's wavy red-yellow-blue flag motif.
clue.nl-28-south-holland-description: South Holland's N-road hectometre markers feature a yellow road number box, sometimes with 'ZH' or the province's red lion emblem or flag colors.
clue.nl-28-utrecht-description: Utrecht's N-road hectometre markers display a yellow box with the road number, sometimes including 'UT' or the province's red-and-white flag motif.
clue.nl-28-zeeland-description: Zeeland's N-road hectometre markers feature a yellow road number box, sometimes with 'ZL' or the province's blue-and-white wavy flag motif or lion emblem.
clue.nl-provincial-flag-description: Friesland and Noord-Brabant flags appear frequently. The unofficial flag of the Achterhoek region is also sometimes visible.
clue.nl-frisian-bilingual-sign-descripti: In Friesland, many town entry signs show both Dutch and Frisian place names. Street names ending in -wei or -strjitte are uniquely Frisian.
clue.nl-limburg-streetlight-sticker-desc: Street lights in Limburg have tall, vertical white stickers with three to four digits.
clue.nl-north-brabant-streetlight-sticke: Street lights in North Brabant have horizontal white stickers showing one or two digits.
clue.nl-polder-landscape-west-north-desc: Western and northern regions are flat, marshy polders criss-crossed by many small waterways.
clue.nl-farmland-landscape-south-east-de: Southern and eastern regions have flat farmland with waterways but less marshy terrain.
clue.nl-low-hill-southern-limburg-descri: Southern Limburg features gentle rolling hills contrasting with the rest of the flat country.
clue.nl-veluwe-forested-region-descripti: The Veluwe in central Gelderland is wooded with old-growth forest, heathland, and sandy ground.
clue.nl-flevoland-reclaimed-polder-descr: Flevoland was reclaimed from the sea, with straight roads, vast fields, wind turbines, and no historic buildings.
clue.nl-coastal-dune-description: Sand dunes line most of the Dutch North Sea coastline.
clue.nl-wadden-island-description: The Wadden Islands have extensive sand dunes and tourism-related signage or infrastructure.
clue.nl-large-farm-roof-north-title: Large Farm Roofs in the North
clue.nl-large-farm-roof-north-descriptio: Northern farmhouses have oversized, sweeping roofs.
clue.nl-rolling-shutter-southern-house-d: Window rolling shutters are more common in the southern half of the country.
clue.nl-country-flag-description: The national flag of the Netherlands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.nz-licence-plate-description: New Zealand plates are white with black lettering, appearing almost entirely white when blurred.
clue.nz-concrete-utility-poles-single-gr: Concrete Utility Poles with Single Groove
NZ's main poles are concrete with a single long vertical groove and small silver possum guards.
clue.nz-white-sign-post-description: NZ directional and warning signs are typically mounted on white posts; warning signs are yellow diamonds.
clue.nz-blue-street-sign-description: New Zealand street signs are predominantly blue with white text, especially in rural areas.
clue.nz-road-line-marking-description: NZ outer road lines are generally white; centre lines are single white dashes or solid double yellow lines.
clue.nz-chevron-sign-description: NZ curve chevrons are black arrows on yellow with a thin black border.
clue.nz-green-directional-sign-descripti: New Zealand highway direction signs are green with state highway numbers inside a red shield.
clue.nz-bridge-marker-red-crest-descript: NZ bridge markers show highway numbers inside a red shield and a yellow marker with the river or bridge name.
clue.nz-fern-forested-area-description: Ferns are very common in New Zealand's wooded and forested areas.
clue.nz-state-highway-numbering-system-d: New Zealand's two-digit state highway numbers run north to south sequentially.
clue.nz-phone-number-area-code-descripti: NZ phone numbers have seven digits preceded by a two-digit area code; numbers starting with 02 are mobile.
clue.nz-fonterra-farm-sign-numbering-des: The leading digit on Fonterra dairy farm signs corresponds to a regional numbering pattern.
clue.nz-waikato-northland-landscape-desc: These regions feature dry conditions and rolling hills; Northland is notably hilly.
clue.nz-west-coast-temperate-rainforest-: The West Coast and parts of Tasman have lush temperate rainforests and rugged, densely green terrain.
clue.nz-southland-otago-landscape-descri: Flatter parts of Southland and Otago have a cold climate with gently sloping alpine hills and sparse, stunted vegetation.
clue.nz-southern-alps-mountain-range-des: A massive snow-covered mountain chain runs through most of the South Island with thinning vegetation further south.
clue.nz-hawkes-bay-landscape-description: Dry, golden-grass-covered hills with sunny conditions and a white Street View car.
clue.nz-bright-sandy-cliff-description: Pale, sandy cliff faces common in central Manawatu-Whanganui and parts of Taranaki, Waikato, and Hawke's Bay.
clue.nz-glacial-lake-queenstown-descript: Numerous glacial lakes with striking teal, crystal-clear water around Queenstown in the Southern Alps region.
clue.nz-gen-2-coverage-gravel-road-north: Unpaved gravel roads are frequent in the Northland region.
clue.nz-tall-hedge-tree-row-canterbury-t: Tall Hedge and Tree Rows in Canterbury
clue.nz-tall-hedge-tree-row-canterbury-d: Tall rows of hedges and trees are common across the flat Canterbury Plains with mountains visible to the west.
clue.nz-very-tall-hedge-bay-plenty-title: Very Tall Hedges in Bay of Plenty
clue.nz-very-tall-hedge-bay-plenty-descr: Exceptionally tall hedges are characteristic around Tauranga in the Bay of Plenty.
clue.nz-vineyard-description: Grape vineyards are prevalent in Marlborough and Hawke's Bay.
clue.nz-corn-field-description: Corn cultivation is found almost exclusively on the North Island.
clue.nz-new-zealand-flax-neat-rows-south: New Zealand Flax in Neat Rows
NZ flax planted in orderly, straight rows indicates the Southland region.
clue.nz-olive-brown-square-possum-guard-: Most utility poles in Marlborough have long, square-shaped olive-brown possum guards alongside shorter silver ones.
clue.nz-long-cylindrical-silver-possum-g: Many utility poles in Southland have tall, cylindrical silver possum guards.
clue.nz-holey-pole-description: Concrete poles with a pattern of holes are common in Southland and Auckland.
clue.nz-square-concrete-pole-no-groove-d: Square-profile concrete poles lacking vertical grooves are most common in Southland.
clue.nz-off-centre-crossbar-pole-descrip: Utility poles with uneven, asymmetrical crossbars appear in Otago, Marlborough, Wellington, and Taranaki.
clue.nz-tall-metal-bar-insulator-extensi: Poles with centre insulators atop tall vertical metal bars are frequent near the Auckland-Waikato border and elsewhere in Waikato.
clue.nz-white-painted-crossbar-descripti: Some concrete poles in eastern Waikato and Whanganui have white paint on the middle section of wooden crossbars.
clue.nz-yellow-cow-tag-pole-gisborne-des: Most poles in Gisborne have a small yellow tag resembling a cattle ear tag.
clue.nz-yellow-danger-triangle-warning-s: Pole stickers with a yellow hazard triangle flanked by white rectangles appear in Hawke's Bay, Taupo-Rotorua corridor, northern Waikato, and south of Auckland.
clue.nz-medium-black-vertical-sticker-5-: Medium black vertical stickers with five digits appear on poles in West Coast, Tasman, southern Canterbury, and southern Northland.
clue.nz-long-black-vertical-sticker-6-di: Long Black Vertical Sticker (6 Digits with Square)
Tall black vertical stickers with six digits and a small black square appear across much of the North Island and in Southland and Otago.
clue.nz-small-black-horizontal-pole-stic: Compact black horizontal stickers with multiple numbers are common in Taranaki and Wellington.
clue.nz-small-white-horizontal-pole-stic: Small white horizontal stickers with several numbers appear in various North Island locations.
clue.nz-solid-white-edge-line-no-centre-: Solid White Edge Lines without Centre Lines
Roads with solid white edge markings but no centre line are most common in Gisborne.
clue.nz-green-stripe-bollard-southern-ca: NZ bollards with a green stripe instead of red are common in southern Canterbury and eastern Southland.
clue.nz-black-stripe-bollard-wellington-: Bollards with a black stripe replacing red are frequent in Wellington.
clue.nz-tightly-spaced-wooden-fence-post: Wooden fences with closely packed posts are prevalent on the North Island, northern South Island, and around Akaroa.
clue.nz-widely-spaced-wooden-fence-post-: Wooden fences with large gaps between posts are common on the South Island and in Taranaki.
clue.nz-thin-metal-fence-post-descriptio: Fences with slender metal posts are found almost exclusively on the South Island.
clue.nz-short-wooden-fence-post-extensio: Small pieces of wood attached to the top of fence posts slightly extend their height, often seen in Hawke's Bay and occasionally in Manawatu-Whanganui and Gisborne.
clue.nz-long-wooden-fence-post-extension: Longer wooden extensions on fence posts, taller than the short variant, are primarily found in Southland and Hawke's Bay, with occasional sightings in Otago.
clue.nz-fruit-farm-green-netting-descrip: Orchards draped in green protective netting are especially common around Tauranga and occasionally near Gisborne.
clue.nz-country-flag-description: The national flag of New Zealand is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-vehicles-01-01-call-the-police-d: A police vehicle, usually white or black, trails the Nigerian Street View car in nearly every coverage. The exact model may differ from images shown.
clue.ng-licence-plate-description: Nigerian plates are short and appear somewhat green through Google blur.
clue.ng-concrete-utility-pole-descriptio: Nigerian utility poles are concrete with vertical indents and a few horizontal supports.
clue.ng-poor-road-condition-description: Many Nigerian roads lack lines or have faded markings with potholes and cracked surfaces.
clue.ng-architecture-description: Nigerian houses are mostly single-storey with steep metal-sheet roofs and cinder-block walls.
clue.ng-city-state-name-signage-title: City and State Names on Signage
clue.ng-city-state-name-signage-descript: Storefronts and banners often display city or state names, aiding location identification.
clue.ng-topography-description: Nigeria is generally flat with subtle elevation changes. Hills appear from Abuja northward and near Enugu. The tallest peaks are on the Cameroon border (Mandara Range).
clue.ng-climate-zone-description: Nigeria's climate ranges from tropical rainforest in the south, drier savannah in the centre, to arid steppe in the north.
clue.ng-13-lagos-description: In Lagos, commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are bright yellow, often with black stripes or trim.
clue.ng-13-kano-description: Kano commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are typically green, sometimes with white or yellow accents.
clue.ng-13-rivers-description: In Rivers State, commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are usually blue, often with white or black roof sections.
clue.ng-13-kaduna-description: Kaduna commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are painted deep green, occasionally with yellow or black details.
clue.ng-13-oyo-description: Oyo commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are commonly wine red or maroon, often with white or yellow roofs.
clue.ng-13-enugu-description: In Enugu, commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are white with green stripes or accents.
clue.ng-13-anambra-description: Anambra commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are typically blue with white or yellow highlights.
clue.ng-13-borno-description: Borno commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are usually light or sky blue, sometimes with white or black accents.
clue.ng-13-delta-description: Delta commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are yellow and black, often in a two-tone pattern.
clue.ng-13-edo-description: Edo commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are painted red, sometimes with white or yellow roofs.
clue.xx-misc-01-islamic-outfits-descript: You are more likely to see women wearing hijabs and men dressed in traditional Islamic outfits in the northern regions of Nigeria.
clue.ng-haystack-kaduna-state-descriptio: Large haystacks are extremely common and almost exclusively found in Kaduna state.
clue.ng-kano-state-arid-cornfield-descri: An arid yet green agricultural landscape with abundant corn fields points to Kano state.
clue.ng-benue-state-green-grass-red-soil: Benue Green Grass and Red Soil
Lush green grass with reddish soil, scattered tall trees, and thatched huts characterise Benue state.
clue.ng-niger-state-crapcam-savannah-tit: Niger Scattered Trees and Red Soil
clue.ng-niger-state-crapcam-savannah-des: Scattered trees, reddish soil, and dry grass cover most of Niger state.
clue.ng-northwest-state-open-arid-landsc: Kebbi, Sokoto, Zamfara, and Katsina have an open, arid landscape with very sparse or no tree cover.
clue.ng-northeast-rocky-hill-description: Savannah terrain dotted with rocky hills appears across Plateau, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa, and northern Taraba.
clue.ng-monolithic-mountain-abuja-area-d: Large monolithic outcrops of exposed, weathered rock are common in and around Abuja.
clue.ng-29-lagos-description: In Lagos, the follow car is typically a white Toyota Hilux with blue police lights on the roof.
clue.ng-29-kano-description: Kano's follow car is usually a silver Toyota Hilux, sometimes with a black bull bar.
clue.ng-29-rivers-description: In Rivers State, the follow car is most often a dark blue Toyota Hilux with a red and blue police light bar.
clue.ng-29-oyo-description: Oyo's follow car is a white Toyota Hilux with no visible police lights or markings.
clue.ng-29-kaduna-description: Kaduna's follow car is a silver Toyota Hilux, often with a blue police light bar and sometimes a front bull bar.
clue.ng-country-flag-description: The national flag of Nigeria is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.mp-tropical-landscape-description: The islands feature dense, low tropical vegetation throughout.
clue.mp-abundant-road-reflectors-descrip: Roads have a very high density of reflectors, shared with Guam.
clue.mp-east-asian-language-signage-desc: Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and Russian text appear frequently on commercial signs.
clue.mp-commercial-area-description: Denser commercial zones are along Saipan's southern west coast.
clue.mp-country-flag-description: The national flag of the Northern Mariana Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.no-wooden-house-description: Norwegian homes are mostly wooden, often red-painted; black-painted houses are more common here than in neighbors.
clue.xx-license-plates-01-green-license-: In Norway, commercial license plates are green, and are often seen on vans.
clue.no-road-line-long-dash-title: Road Line Markings with Long Dashes
clue.no-road-line-long-dash-description: Smaller roads have white edge lines with long dashes; larger roads have solid edge lines and yellow center lines with an orange tint.
clue.no-dotted-road-line-title: Dotted Paint Pattern on Road Lines
clue.no-dotted-road-line-description: Norwegian road markings often use small dots of paint instead of solid lines.
clue.no-norwegian-language-char-descript: Norwegian uses special characters Æ, Ø, Å and writes "kk" where Swedish uses "ck".
clue.no-bollard-black-parallelogram-desc: Norwegian bollards are slender curved posts with a reflector inside a black parallelogram.
clue.no-orange-snow-pole-mid-reflector-t: Orange Snow Poles with Mid-Height Reflector
clue.no-orange-snow-pole-mid-reflector-d: Snow poles are orange with a narrow white reflector roughly at mid-height.
clue.no-wooden-snow-pole-reflector-title: Wooden Snow Poles with Painted Reflectors
clue.no-wooden-snow-pole-reflector-descr: Thin wooden snow poles with painted reflectors are common.
clue.no-guardrail-wooden-post-descriptio: Metal guardrails are often supported by wooden posts.
clue.no-pedestrian-crossing-four-stripe-: Pedestrian Crossing Signs with Four Stripes
Norwegian pedestrian signs show a figure with four stripes on the crossing.
clue.no-blue-passing-place-sign-descript: Smaller roads frequently display blue signs bearing a large white letter M, indicating passing places.
clue.no-bus-stop-sign-description: Norwegian bus stops are marked by a small blue sign featuring a white bus icon.
clue.no-sone-speed-zone-sign-description: White signs displaying the word "Sone" along with a speed limit are common in Norwegian urban areas.
clue.no-street-name-suffix-description: The most typical Norwegian street name endings are "vei" and "gate." When attached to a name, they become "-veien" and "-gata" or "-gate."
clue.no-centered-street-sign-post-descri: Street name signs in Norway are typically mounted centered on top of the sign post.
clue.no-bright-yellow-construction-sign-: Road construction zones in Norway use warning signs with a vivid yellow background.
clue.no-sign-mount-four-bolt-description: Norwegian road signs are fastened with four visible bolts arranged in a tall rectangular pattern.
clue.xx-general-01-64-black-and-yellow-d: In Norway, you can see black and yellow chevrons.
clue.no-distance-marker-sign-description: Small white square signs show a road number at the top and the distance to the nearest town below on mid-sized roads.
clue.no-wooden-utility-pole-black-cap-ti: Wooden Utility Poles with Black Caps
clue.no-wooden-utility-pole-black-cap-de: Utility poles in Norway are usually made of wood and often topped with a small black metal cap.
clue.no-lamp-mount-single-bolt-title: Lamp Mounting with Single Thick Bolt
clue.no-lamp-mount-single-bolt-descripti: Street lamps attached to wooden poles in Norway use a single thick bolt for mounting.
clue.no-grass-covered-roof-description: Traditional Norwegian buildings often feature living grass growing on their rooftops.
clue.no-road-number-first-digit-pattern-: The leading digit of Norwegian road numbers corresponds to geographic regions, with some exceptions.
clue.no-bilingual-sami-sign-north-title: Bilingual Sámi Signs in Northern Areas
clue.no-bilingual-sami-sign-north-descri: Parts of northern Norway display signs in both Norwegian and a Sámi language, identified by letters Á, Đ, and multiple consecutive vowels.
clue.no-bracken-fern-southern-norway-des: Bracken ferns with tall stems and wide leaf fronds grow predominantly in southern Norway.
clue.no-spruce-tree-description: Spruce trees are concentrated in the southern half of Norway, especially in the southeast and Trondheim region.
clue.no-pine-tree-description: Pines are most prevalent along coastal areas and far inland zones within southern Norway.
clue.no-oak-tree-description: Oak trees in Norway are almost entirely restricted to the far southern part of the country.
clue.no-maple-tree-description: Maples grow primarily in southern Norway, especially around Oslo's agricultural areas.
clue.no-bright-coloured-moss-description: Vivid, colourful moss is common from Lillehammer to Oppdal.
clue.no-three-major-farmland-region-desc: Norway's large agricultural zones are concentrated in the southeast, Trondheim surroundings, and south of Stavanger.
clue.no-southeast-farmland-oslo-descript: The biggest farmland stretch lies in the southeast around Oslo, with flat, gently rolling terrain and smooth forested hills.
clue.no-trondheim-area-farmland-descript: Agricultural land around Trondheim sits on steep, uneven hills more rugged than the southeast.
clue.no-stavanger-area-farmland-jaeren-d: Farmland south of Stavanger is relatively flat with wide fields and common rock walls made of large rounded stones.
clue.no-deep-fjord-tall-mountain-descrip: The deepest fjords flanked by towering mountains are concentrated between Bergen and Trondheim.
clue.no-lofoten-jagged-rocky-mountain-de: The Lofoten Archipelago features sharp rocky peaks with very sparse tree cover.
clue.no-northeast-norway-rolling-terrain: Northeastern Norway has gently rolling terrain with small birch trees and patchy grass.
clue.no-barren-highland-southwest-descri: Treeless highland plateaus with rocky mountains along the road characterize southwestern Norway.
clue.no-exposed-rock-south-coast-title: Exposed Rock on the South Coast
clue.no-exposed-rock-south-coast-descrip: Bare rock outcrops with small coastal pines and low bushes are typical of Norway's southern coastline.
clue.no-coastal-grassland-far-north-desc: Roads along the far northern coast pass through open grasslands with minimal vegetation and low, distant mountains.
clue.no-white-wooden-house-south-coast-d: Entire villages of all-white wooden houses are distinctive along Norway's southern coastline.
clue.no-black-snow-pole-bergen-trondheim: Snow poles painted black are common between Bergen and Trondheim.
clue.no-wide-black-pole-plate-southeast-: Small, wide black ID plates with alphanumeric characters appear on utility poles in southeastern Norway.
clue.no-rusty-guardrail-west-coast-descr: Rusty guardrails are prevalent along the southern half of Norway's west coast.
clue.no-svalbard-archipelago-description: Svalbard is a Norwegian Arctic archipelago with separate coverage and guide.
clue.no-russian-border-road-appearance-d: Roads near the Russian border have a humid, green look with overcast, foggy conditions and low birches and pines.
clue.no-country-flag-description: The national flag of Norway is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.om-arabic-language-description: Arabic is Oman's sole official language; signage often appears in Arabic and English.
clue.om-yellow-edge-line-white-centre-li: Yellow Edge Lines with White Centre Lines
Omani roads have yellow lines along edges and white lines down the centre.
clue.om-black-yellow-curb-description: Kerbs painted in alternating black and yellow segments are widespread on Omani roads.
clue.om-light-stone-architecture-ornate-: Light Stone Architecture with Ornate Fences
Omani homes are pale stone with decorative details, enclosed by matching stone fences with elaborate gates.
clue.om-blue-directional-sign-descriptio: Omani road signs are blue with white lettering, showing Arabic and English text.
clue.om-striped-signpost-description: Sign poles in Oman often have alternating black-and-white horizontal stripes.
clue.om-wooden-utility-pole-description: Wooden power poles in Oman have three distinct top designs, including a unique metal triangle above one variant.
clue.om-red-white-high-voltage-pylon-des: Electricity transmission towers painted red and white stripes are common across Oman.
clue.om-beah-garbage-bin-description: Omani rubbish bins are black plastic or grey metal with a three-leaf logo and 'be'ah' text.
clue.om-white-taxi-orange-panel-descript: Omani taxis are white with distinctive orange panels on both sides.
clue.om-northern-dry-mountain-descriptio: Northern Oman has arid, rocky mountain terrain resembling eastern UAE.
clue.om-southern-rolling-hill-salalah-de: The Salalah area features hilly terrain with rocky ground, scattered bushes, small trees, and green valleys.
clue.om-green-vegetation-north-nizwa-des: Mountains north of Nizwa have lush green bushes and jagged rocky peaks.
clue.om-acacia-tree-description: Short trees with flat, umbrella-shaped canopies, acacias are most prevalent in northern Oman and some coastal areas.
clue.om-date-palm-plantation-description: Groves of date palms are concentrated along Oman's northern coast.
clue.om-red-sandy-dune-description: Dunes with a reddish hue appear near the Saudi border and in Oman's central interior.
clue.om-country-flag-description: The national flag of Oman is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.pk-urdu-english-signage-description: Urdu is the national language on signs, using a script related to Arabic with softer fonts; English is also common.
clue.pk-licence-plate-description: Pakistani plates are short with region-specific designs, mostly showing Punjab designs with a green strip.
clue.pk-mughal-garden-description: Coverage includes large, orderly gardens enclosed by stone walls featuring historic temples or fortresses.
clue.pk-brightly-coloured-baggy-trouser-: Vibrantly coloured, loose-fitting trousers are extremely common on pedestrians.
clue.pk-jallo-hazy-suburb-description: An eastern suburb of Lahore with semi-urban, lower-income housing under a thick haze.
clue.pk-katas-hazy-hill-description: Coverage north of Sargodha with hilly terrain under a hazy sky.
clue.pk-patriata-pine-covered-hill-descr: Forested hills thick with tall pines northeast of Islamabad, partly captured from an aerial lift.
clue.pk-country-flag-description: The national flag of Pakistan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.pa-tropical-hilly-landscape-descrip: Panama features tropical landscape with palms, rolling hills, and a mix of dry fields and dense vegetation.
clue.pa-living-fence-post-description: Panamanian roadside fences are often built from small living trees, with remaining posts also wooden.
clue.pa-architecture-description: Panamanian buildings show Spanish colonial influence, with vivid painted concrete or brick walls and red metal-sheet or tile roofs.
clue.pa-road-line-description: Typical road markings are solid white edges with a yellow centre line; solid white edges with no centre line are nearly unique to Panama.
clue.pa-utility-pole-description: Panamanian utility poles are mostly round concrete with varying insulators; blue, white, or red numbers and metal plates are common.
clue.pa-eye-warning-sign-description: Red octagonal signs with a realistic eye illustration are unique to Panama.
clue.pa-phone-number-area-code-descripti: In Panama, the first digit of a 7-digit phone number indicates the region; two-digit codes provide more precision.
clue.pa-taxi-bus-plate-code-description: Leading digit on taxi and bus licence plates corresponds to a province in Panama.
clue.pa-colon-panama-city-lush-tropic-de: Dense green vegetation with palms and very tall grass characterizes areas around Colón and Panama City.
clue.pa-aguadulce-flat-agriculture-descr: Flat terrain with agricultural fields and distinctly brown or orange soil surrounds Aguadulce.
clue.pa-eastern-vertical-pole-plate-desc: Tall, narrow yellow or white plates fastened to poles with black zip ties appear in eastern provinces.
clue.pa-western-horizontal-pole-plate-de: Horizontal plates attached to poles are common in western provinces; eastern vertical plates override if both appear.
