clue.pa-yellow-border-plate-colon-descri: Thin yellow plates with a black border, vertical or horizontal, are most common in Colón Province.
clue.pa-wind-turbine-penonome-descriptio: Wind turbines are visible both south and north of Penonomé.
clue.pa-country-flag-description: The national flag of Panama is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.pe-licence-plate-description: Peruvian plates are white or yellow; taxis have split-coloured plates, yellow on top and white on bottom.
clue.pe-road-line-marking-description: Peruvian outer road lines are always white. Highways have single or double yellow centre lines. Rural mountain roads often lack a centre line.
clue.pe-triangular-concrete-bollard-desc: Peruvian bollards are usually red or yellow triangular concrete shapes; circular concrete variants also appear.
clue.pe-black-yellow-guardrail-descripti: Peruvian guardrails commonly have black-and-yellow diagonal stripes; other designs like sharp arrows also appear.
clue.pe-kilometre-marker-description: Concrete kilometre markers painted black and white are found along Peruvian roads.
clue.pe-road-signs-01-01-concrete-founda: Metal signs in Peru are standing on visible concrete plinths.
clue.xx-pole-01-02-peruvian-poles-descri: In Peru, you can often see concrete utility poles with three horizontal crossarms.
clue.pe-painted-pole-base-description: Some Peruvian utility poles have lower sections painted black or black-and-yellow stripes.
clue.pe-orange-painted-bridge-descriptio: Peruvian bridges are often painted orange.
clue.pe-semi-arid-mountain-landscape-des: Much of Peru has dry mountain ranges and valleys with sparse vegetation.
clue.pe-vehicles-01-tuk-tuks-description: Tuk Tuks are a common sight in Peru. They are usually referred to as mototaxi.
clue.pe-red-white-vehicle-sticker-descri: Wide red-and-white reflective stickers are common on taxis and commercial vehicles in Peru.
clue.pe-sol-currency-description: The Peruvian sol, written as S/, appears on shop signs and ads.
clue.pe-political-party-logo-description: Peruvian political party logos are often painted on walls and buildings.
clue.pe-terrain-overview-east-west-descr: Eastern Peru is generally flat; western Peru is mountainous.
clue.pe-climate-zone-description: Western coast is arid desert; eastern lowlands are tropical rainforest; Andes create transitional climates.
clue.pe-highway-numbering-system-descrip: Western highways increase in number from north to south; Routes 1, 3, and 5 are longest.
clue.pe-tumbes-off-road-landscape-descri: Tumbes off-road areas have sandy soil with green or dry shrubs.
clue.pe-southwestern-piura-dry-flat-terr: Southwest of Piura is dry, sparsely vegetated, mostly flat with gentle hills.
clue.pe-northwestern-piura-hilly-terrain: Northwest of Piura has similar vegetation but more hilly terrain.
clue.pe-coconut-tall-palm-tree-descripti: Coconut and tall palms grow in coastal farming areas north of Lima and near large coastal cities.
clue.pe-sugar-cane-field-description: Large sugar cane plantations are near northern coastal cities Chiclayo and Trujillo.
clue.pe-banana-plantation-description: Bananas grow in northern coastal agricultural zones, similar to sugar cane.
clue.pe-flat-highland-plateau-descriptio: Flat high-altitude terrain appears in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.
clue.pe-scrubby-mountain-far-north-title: Scrubby Mountains in the Far North
clue.pe-scrubby-mountain-far-north-descr: Far northern Peruvian mountains have low shrubs and scrubby trees, often arid near coast and Ecuador.
clue.pe-pine-plantation-high-elevation-d: Planted pine forests grow at higher elevations away from coastal deserts and Amazon basin.
clue.pe-rocky-outcrop-central-highland-t: Rocky Outcrops in the Central Highlands
clue.pe-rocky-outcrop-central-highland-d: Exposed rock faces are common on hillsides in central Peru from Lago Chinchaycocha south to Ayacucho.
clue.pe-jagged-mountain-peak-description: Tall, sharp rocky peaks are typical from Huaraz south to Cusco, away from the coast.
clue.pe-light-green-lichen-description: Pale green lichen patches cover rocks and ground at high altitudes in central and southern Peru.
clue.pe-dark-red-soil-description: Reddish-tinted earth appears notably around Cusco, Ayacucho, Cajamarca, and Tarapoto.
clue.pe-southern-coastal-desert-descript: From Ica down to Tacna, the landscape is a barren, flat desert with distant mountains to the east.
clue.pe-coastal-agricultural-valley-desc: Green farming valleys run southwest-to-northeast between barren mountains in central and southern Peru.
clue.pe-overhanging-roof-wooden-support-: Buildings with outward-extending roofs on wooden supports, often brightly painted, common in northern Peru.
clue.pe-open-front-tuk-tuk-description: Tuk-tuks with exposed front compartments mainly in northern Peru, especially near northern Amazonian regions.
clue.pe-moquegua-cylindrical-bollard-des: Cylindrical bollard topped a yellow stripe can be seen in the southern parts of Peru. A version with a black stripe is exclusive to southern Moquegua.
clue.pe-ruta-5n-san-alejandro-esperanza-: Well-maintained, straight, flat north–south road through dense rainforest.
clue.pe-ruta-28b-kimbiri-echarate-descri: Narrow paved hillside road following a river valley with faded or absent lane markings.
clue.pe-volcano-near-arequipa-descriptio: Volcanic peaks frequently visible in and around Arequipa in southeastern Peru.
clue.pe-lima-boulevard-description: Wide, long, straight streets split by concrete or grassy strips are most common in Lima.
clue.pe-pucallpa-street-grid-description: Pucallpa has a uniform street grid oriented WSW–ENE.
clue.pe-iquitos-description: Isolated northeastern city with overcast skies, three-wheeled tuk-tuks, and rolling Amazonian terrain.
clue.pe-cusco-description: Southern highland city encircled by mountains with red-brick and colonial Spanish architecture.
clue.pe-aguas-calientes-cusco-train-trek: Trekker follows railway line connecting Aguas Calientes with Cusco.
clue.pe-country-flag-description: The national flag of Peru is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.ph-licence-plate-green-tint-descrip: Many Philippine vehicles carry privately issued plates with a distinctive greenish tint.
clue.ph-octagonal-metal-pole-description: Utility poles with octagonal cross-section are common in the Philippines.
clue.ph-side-mounted-pole-insulator-desc: Single insulator atop a short vertical bar attached to the side of utility poles is common.
clue.ph-yellow-white-road-marking-descri: Philippine centre lines may be yellow, white, or a side-by-side combination.
clue.ph-yellow-kilometre-stone-descripti: Tall, square-shaped yellow road markers unique to the Philippines.
clue.ph-red-white-chevron-sign-descripti: Philippine road curve chevrons use red arrows on white backgrounds.
clue.ph-colourful-sign-post-description: Posts supporting road signs are frequently painted red, orange, or yellow.
clue.ph-tricycle-tuk-tuk-description: Motorised tricycles (tuk-tuks) are ubiquitous and often outnumber cars.
clue.ph-grain-drying-road-description: Harvested grain is often spread out on roads for drying.
clue.ph-regional-tricycle-design-descrip: Different islands and regions use distinct tricycle and tuk-tuk designs.
clue.ph-province-name-sign-description: Philippine province names appear often on signs and help with location.
clue.ph-phone-number-area-code-descripti: Landline numbers start with 0 plus regional code; mobile numbers start with 09.

clue.ph-pine-covered-mountain-northern-l: The mountain range in Northern Luzon features dry slopes with plentiful pine trees.
clue.ph-corn-field-description: Corn cultivation is a common sight all over the Philippines.
clue.ph-oil-palm-plantation-description: Nearly all oil palm plantations are on Mindanao.
clue.ph-sugarcane-field-description: Most sugarcane is grown on Negros and Panay.
clue.ph-pineapple-plantation-description: Large-scale pineapple farming is concentrated on Mindanao.
clue.ph-banana-plantation-description: Commercial banana plantations are almost exclusively in central and southern Mindanao.
clue.ph-moluccan-albizia-tree-descriptio: These trees have pale trunks and feathery pinnate leaves clustered near the crown, mainly on eastern and central Mindanao.
clue.ph-amakan-wall-diamond-pattern-desc: Houses with woven bamboo walls in a diamond pattern are found almost exclusively in the southern half of the Philippines.
clue.ph-amakan-sawali-wall-diagonal-weav: Amakan / Sawali Walls with Diagonal Weave
Woven bamboo walls with a diagonal pattern are most prevalent on Palawan and across the northern half of the country.
clue.ph-yellow-black-concrete-guardrail-: Concrete guardrails painted with alternating yellow and black stripes are specific to the Cordillera Administrative Region.
clue.ph-bicol-guardrail-three-black-stri: Bicol Guardrails with Three Black Stripes
White guardrails with a repeating set of three black stripes are unique to the Bicol region in southern Luzon.
clue.ph-chile-style-indented-concrete-po: Square concrete utility poles with a visible indent on each side are found mainly north of Manila and around Bacolod on Negros.
clue.ph-square-metal-mesh-pole-zamboanga: Square Metal Mesh Poles on Zamboanga
Utility poles built from square metal mesh are found primarily on the Zamboanga peninsula in Mindanao.
clue.ph-muslim-majority-western-mindanao: Muslim Majority Area in Western Mindanao
A region in western Mindanao has a Muslim majority population.
clue.ph-mountain-dew-bottle-decoration-d: Neon-green Mountain Dew bottles repurposed as decorations are common in northern Luzon.
clue.ph-country-flag-description: The national flag of the Philippines is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-general-01-54-jeepneys-descripti: In the Philippines it is common to find jeepneys in urban environments. They are often heavily decorated.
clue.pn-dense-tropical-forest-descriptio: Pitcairn Island is semi-tropical and thickly forested, with narrow dirt tracks winding through the trees.
clue.pn-red-soil-description: Pitcairn's exposed soil is characteristically deep red.
clue.pn-country-flag-description: The national flag of the Pitcairn Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.pl-licence-plate-description: Polish plates are long and white with the standard EU blue strip on the left.
clue.pl-double-white-centre-line-descrip: All road markings are white in Poland. Double centre lines are extremely common.
clue.pl-b-type-guardrail-red-reflector-d: Polish guardrails are fitted with circular red reflectors.
clue.pl-white-prohibitory-sign-descripti: Polish round prohibitory signs use a white background with a thicker red border.
clue.pl-town-entry-sign-description: Polish towns have two signs: a green one with the locality name and a white-and-black one with a stylised urban silhouette, both in a Polish typeface.
clue.pl-chevron-description: Polish chevrons are white boards with red arrows.
clue.pl-polish-language-description: A West Slavic language with unique diacritics like Ł, Ą, Ę, Ż, and Ń, and W replacing V.
clue.pl-flat-green-landscape-description: Poland features flat terrain with gentle hills, extensive agriculture, and moderate forest cover.
clue.pl-tree-lined-road-description: Rows of mature trees flanking both sides of roads are common across Poland.
clue.pl-tiled-sidewalk-description: Polish pavements commonly use neatly laid grey or light red paving tiles in various patterns.
clue.pl-architecture-description: Central European style with plain stone walls, pastel stucco, and orange, red, black, or brown roof tiles; detached homes and communist-era blocks.
clue.pl-roadside-christian-shrine-descri: Small roadside shrines and blue-white or yellow-white Catholic flags are frequent.
clue.pl-regional-road-numbering-descript: Three-digit regional road numbers cluster geographically; the first digit indicates the region, often shown in yellow boxes.
clue.pl-telephone-area-code-description: Polish landline numbers have 9 digits; the first two form an area code mapping logically across the country.
clue.pl-place-name-suffix-description: Suffixes like -owo, -ów, -ino/-yno, and -ew help identify regions within Poland.
clue.pl-22-pomeranian-voivodeship-descri: Signs show Polish above and Kashubian below, with Kashubian featuring distinctive diacritics and letters.
clue.pl-22-opole-voivodeship-description: Place-name signs show Polish above and German below, with German including umlauts and ß.
clue.pl-22-podlaskie-voivodeship-descrip: Signs show Polish above and Belarusian in Cyrillic below near the Belarusian border.
clue.pl-22-lublin-voivodeship-descriptio: Signs show Polish above and Belarusian in Cyrillic below in eastern Lublin villages.
clue.pl-22-masovian-voivodeship-descript: Signs show Polish above and Belarusian in Cyrillic below in eastern Masovian villages.
clue.pl-22-warmian-masurian-voivodeship-: Signs show Polish above and Lithuanian below, with Lithuanian-specific letters, near the Lithuanian border.
clue.pl-22-lesser-poland-voivodeship-des: Signs show Polish above and Lemko in Cyrillic below in southeastern Lesser Poland.
clue.pl-22-subcarpathian-voivodeship-des: Signs show Polish above and Lemko in Cyrillic below in southeastern Subcarpathian villages.
clue.pl-southern-hill-mountain-descripti: The southern border region has hilly terrain and some mountains.
clue.pl-wooden-house-podlaskie-descripti: Traditional wooden houses are concentrated in eastern Podlaskie Voivodeship.
clue.pl-tatra-mountain-zakopane-descript: Poland's highest peaks near Zakopane on the Slovak border.
clue.pl-country-flag-description: The national flag of Poland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.pt-portuguese-language-description: Portuguese uses distinctive letters like Ç, Ã, Õ, Â, and Ê; Ñ does not appear.
clue.pt-ladder-poles-tall-steps-descript: Concrete ladder poles have unusually tall steps, often with small see-through holes.
clue.pt-bollards-description: Bollards are wedge-shaped with thin white caps or flat with wide reflectors, usually white or sometimes orange.
clue.pt-white-directional-signs-descript: Direction signs are white with black arrows floating clear of the edges.
clue.pt-kilometre-markers-description: Kilometre markers are wide rectangular signs with a coloured left section and white right section; larger signs show road numbers.
clue.pt-black-white-waystones-descriptio: Small black-and-white stone markers are frequent along roads.
clue.pt-stop-sign-font-description: Stop signs use a noticeably large font.
clue.pt-black-yellow-chevrons-descriptio: Chevrons are black boards with yellow arrows.
clue.pt-pedestrian-signs-five-stripes-de: Pedestrian signs in Portugal show five stripes and a figure with a high belt.
clue.pt-a-type-guardrails-red-reflectors: In Portugal, guardrails have red reflectors.
clue.pt-white-sign-borders-description: Road signs typically have white borders.
clue.pt-diagonal-cobblestone-roads-descr: Cobblestone roads in Portugal have square stones laid diagonally to the road direction.
clue.pt-bright-cobblestone-sidewalks-des: Portuguese pavements often use bright, pale cobblestones.
clue.pt-white-houses-orange-roofs-descri: White stone houses with orange clay-tile roofs are typical in Portugal.
clue.pt-painted-window-door-borders-desc: Blue or yellow trim lines commonly outline windows, doors, and wall edges in Portugal.
clue.pt-decorative-tile-facades-descript: Portuguese buildings often have decorative mosaic tile (azulejos) facades.
clue.pt-telephone-area-codes-description: Portuguese landline numbers start with 2 for geographic area codes; 29 indicates Azores or Madeira.
clue.xx-architecture-01-portuguese-chimn: In southern Portugal, you will often see small chimneys that are either square or round in shape.
clue.pt-concrete-block-houses-north-desc: Northern Portuguese houses often use square concrete blocks with white mortar.
clue.pt-holm-cork-oak-fields-southeast-t: Holm and Cork Oak Fields, Southeast
clue.pt-holm-cork-oak-fields-southeast-d: Southeast fields have sparse holm and cork oaks, appearing dry in summer and lush in spring.
clue.pt-olive-plantations-east-descripti: Olive groves concentrate in eastern Portugal, especially northeast and southeast.
clue.pt-dense-eucalyptus-forests-northwe: Thick eucalyptus forests are mainly in northwest Portugal.
clue.pt-maritime-pine-forests-north-desc: Northern Portugal has maritime pines with grey bark and reddish undertones, bare lower trunks.
clue.pt-terraced-vineyards-douro-valley-: Steep terraced vineyards appear in the Douro wine region east of Porto.
clue.pt-citrus-plantations-south-coast-d: Citrus groves concentrate along Portugal's southern coastline.
clue.pt-serra-da-estrela-rocky-highland-: Rocky mountainous highland with yellow-and-black striped snow poles.
clue.pt-sandy-pine-coast-setubal-sines-t: Sandy Pine Coast, Setúbal to Sines
clue.pt-sandy-pine-coast-setubal-sines-d: Pine forests grow on very white sandy soil along the coast between Setúbal and Sines.
clue.pt-far-southwest-barren-flat-land-d: Flat, uncultivated land with low bushes, grass, and very few trees, appearing dry.
clue.pt-country-flag-description: The national flag of Portugal is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-general-01-38-stone-walls-descri: Across the Azores, you will often see dry stone walls crafted from dark volcanic rock.
clue.pr-area-code-787-description: Phone numbers use the 787 area code, shown as (787) XXX-XXXX.
clue.pr-no-front-licence-plates-descript: Most vehicles lack front licence plates.
clue.pr-divided-highways-description: Much of the rural area has wide divided highways.
clue.pr-highway-shields-description: Puerto Rico uses unique highway shield designs not found elsewhere in the US.
clue.pr-kilometre-markers-description: Kilometre markers are tall green signs with "km" at the top and a large vertical number below.
clue.pr-concrete-flat-roof-architecture-: Most houses are concrete with flat roofs and often metal security gates.
clue.pr-drier-southern-coast-description: The southern coast is noticeably more arid.
clue.pr-old-san-juan-description: Narrow streets, vibrant buildings, brick roads, and Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque architecture.
clue.pr-country-flag-description: The national flag of Puerto Rico is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.qa-road-lines-description: Qatari roads have solid white edge lines with white or yellow centre markings; outer yellow lines appear sometimes.
clue.qa-utility-poles-description: Qatari utility poles are round with three insulators, the middle raised, supported by a crossbar with diagonal braces.
clue.qa-chevrons-description: Qatari chevrons are white-on-red and white-on-blue boards.
clue.qa-zone-numbers-street-signs-descri: Qatar's numbered zones appear on street signs with a reference map.
clue.qa-long-antenna-southwest-descripti: The longest antenna variant is mostly in southwestern Qatar.
clue.qa-country-flag-description: The national flag of Qatar is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

clue.re-mountainous-volcanic-island-desc: Réunion is a volcanic island with coastal roads, lush green mountains, palms, ferns, pine trees, and flowering plants.

clue.ru-2-word-for-street-description: Russian word for street is улица (ulitsa), shortened to ул.
clue.ru-3-word-for-city-description: Russian word for city is город (gorod), shortened to г.
clue.ru-bollard-type-description: Russia has three main bollard styles: thin on a stick, black top with red reflector, and German-style.
clue.ru-wide-intersections-description: Many Russian intersections are wider than usual, with dense bollards.
clue.xx-general-01-41-black-socks-descri: In Russia, signposts often have their lower sections painted black.
clue.ru-concrete-pole-support-blocks-des: Concrete blocks commonly support utility poles in Russia.
clue.ru-pedestrian-crossing-signs-descri: Russian pedestrian signs show a simple figure with three stripes and often a yellow border.
clue.ru-black-white-striped-guardrails-d: Guardrails and barriers often have alternating black and white stripes.
clue.ru-soviet-era-apartment-blocks-desc: Russian urban housing mostly consists of large rectangular concrete blocks with plain facades.
clue.ru-rural-wooden-house-description: Russian rural homes are simple wooden structures with metal roofs.
clue.ru-ornate-window-frames-description: Traditional Russian houses, especially log cabins, feature richly carved decorative window frames often painted blue.
clue.ru-black-white-pole-shields-descrip: Pole shields with alternating black and white stripes appear frequently along highways in European Russia.
clue.ru-birch-tree-range-description: Birch trees with distinctive white peeling bark grow across much of Russia except the far south and far north of western regions.
clue.ru-dense-birch-forest-description: Tightly packed pure birch forests suggest areas east of the Urals, typically between Chelyabinsk and Novosibirsk Oblasts.
clue.ru-siberian-larch-description: Siberian larches with needle-like leaves dominate eastern Russia, becoming more prevalent further east and at higher elevations.
clue.ru-giant-butterbur-sakhalin-cabbage: Giant butterbur, or Sakhalin cabbage, is common in southern Sakhalin Oblast.
clue.ru-sosnowsky-hogweed-description: Heracleum sosnowskyi, a white-flowered plant, appears frequently around Moscow, Komi Republic, and Perm Krai.
clue.ru-fireweed-description: Abundant pink or red fireweed typically signals northern Russia, commonly found north of Moscow.
clue.ru-sunflower-field-description: Sunflower fields are prevalent near the Ukrainian border and in eastern oblasts like Ulyanovsk, Samara, and northern Orenburg.
clue.ru-blue-pod-lupines-description: Blue-pod lupines appear abundantly in northern Vladimir, eastern Ivanovo, and southwestern Kostroma Oblasts.
clue.ru-black-poplar-tree-description: Black poplars are typically found in southern Russia near the Ukrainian and western Kazakhstan borders.
clue.ru-russian-olive-tree-description: Russian olive trees are found along the Kazakhstan border.
clue.ru-roadside-larches-open-fields-des: Sparsely planted larches along roads with open rolling fields are typical of Tatarstan and neighboring regions.
clue.ru-sandy-roadside-description: Sandy roadsides are typical in Khanty-Mansi, Yamalo-Nenets, near Nizhny Novgorod, Karelia, Murmansk, and western Sakha.
clue.ru-red-soil-description: Red soil appears around Izhevsk, Perm, Arkhangelsk, Leningrad, Pskov, Volgograd, and Astrakhan.
clue.ru-kamchatka-grey-gravelly-soil-des: Kamchatka Peninsula has distinctive grey gravelly soil and many volcanoes, some close to roads near Klyuchi.
clue.ru-dark-gravelly-soil-east-yakutsk-: Dark Gravelly Soil East of Yakutsk
Extremely gravelly, sometimes dark soil characterizes terrain east of Yakutsk, starting around Keskil.
clue.ru-vladivostok-area-landscape-descr: Lush, diverse forests cover hilly terrain in the warmer Vladivostok region, often overcast.
clue.ru-hazy-coverage-near-mirny-descrip: Very hazy coverage appears east and south of Mirny, especially along the Vilyuy river, with orange or white haze.
clue.ru-buryatia-landscape-description: Buryatia features open grassy landscapes with shrubs and mountains, becoming lusher near Lake Baikal.
clue.ru-tuva-republic-dry-steppe-descrip: Dry steppe mountains with a long antenna typically indicate the Tuva Republic.
clue.ru-arctic-tundra-landscape-descript: The far north has flat terrain with very low vegetation, characteristic of tundra.
clue.ru-omsk-oblast-landscape-descriptio: Omsk Oblast shows green agricultural fields broken by isolated birch forest patches in summer.
clue.ru-caspian-steppe-description: The area west of the Caspian Sea is extremely dry and flat, especially in Kalmykia, Astrakhan, and Dagestan.
clue.ru-dagestan-grassy-field-descriptio: Grassy fields with bushy vegetation and small flowers in early spring are typical of Dagestan.
clue.ru-caucasus-mountain-range-descript: The Caucasus is a large mountain range with Mount Elbrus, Russia's tallest peak, on the Kabardino-Balkarian and Karachay-Cherkessia border.
clue.ru-roadside-rocks-karelia-murmansk-: Roadside Rocks in Karelia and Murmansk
Large rocks lining roads are common in Karelia and Murmansk, less so in Perm Krai and Buryatia.
clue.ru-murmansk-oblast-landscape-descri: Open, hilly terrain with low shrubbery and fireweed indicates Murmansk; shorter vegetation suggests further north.
clue.ru-telephone-area-codes-description: Russian area codes: start with 8 in the west, 3 in central areas, and 4 in the east or around Moscow.
clue.ru-licence-plate-regional-code-desc: Unblurred plates show a regional code on the right, ordered alphabetically by federal subject type.
clue.ru-distinctive-regional-bus-stop-de: Certain federal subjects have unique bus stop designs, notably Krasnoyarsk Krai, Chuvashia, Tatarstan, and Mari El.
clue.ru-thin-eastern-bollard-description: Very thin bollards on sticks appear in eastern Russia starting around Omsk.
clue.ru-black-traffic-sign-bottom-southe: Traffic signs with black-painted bottoms are found mainly in Stavropol, Chechnya, and western Dagestan.
clue.ru-signpost-edge-clip-description: Metal clips on signpost edges are typical of Leningrad Oblast and St. Petersburg.
clue.ru-outer-dashed-road-line-descripti: Dashed lines along road edges are mostly found in Kursk Oblast.
clue.ru-concrete-block-road-description: Roads made from individual concrete blocks appear in northern Russia, especially Komi, Nenets, and Yamalo-Nenets.
clue.ru-bilingual-town-direction-sign-de: Some republics show bilingual town and directional signs in Russian and a minority language.
clue.ru-dual-cyrillic-latin-town-name-de: Town names in both Cyrillic and Latin scripts appear near the Baltic border and around Moscow.
clue.ru-brown-tourist-sign-description: Brown tourist directional signs are common in Moscow Oblast and nearby regions.
clue.ru-white-limestone-brick-building-d: White limestone brick buildings indicate Dagestan and nearby areas.
clue.ru-red-brick-building-description: Red brick buildings are concentrated in southern Russia.
clue.ru-mosque-description: Mosques are most common in Muslim-majority areas: the North Caucasus republics, Tatarstan, and Bashkortostan.
clue.ru-mari-el-architecture-description: Historic Mari El buildings have green roofs, red brick, and white stone details.
clue.ru-large-red-brake-light-descriptio: Large red brake light on camera car is common in Kaliningrad and some older western coverage.
clue.ru-autumn-gen-3-coverage-descriptio: Autumn coverage appears in Kaliningrad, Bryansk, Tula, and Belgorod.
clue.ru-winter-gen-4-coverage-descriptio: Winter coverage is common in southern Russia from Ryazan to Dagestan.
clue.ru-spring-gen-4-coverage-descriptio: Spring coverage clusters around Kemerovo, Krasnoyarsk, Orenburg, Kamyshin, Lipetsk, and Moscow.
clue.ru-summer-gen-4-coverage-descriptio: Summer coverage is the most common and widespread.
clue.ru-autumn-gen-4-coverage-descriptio: Autumn coverage is rare, found near Kazan, Murmansk, and Ulan-Ude.
clue.ru-rural-gen-4-desert-coverage-nort: Flat rural desert-like roads west of the Caspian Sea appear only in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan.
clue.ru-tropical-plant-black-sea-coast-d: Tropical vegetation like palm trees appears only along Russia's Black Sea coast, mostly near Sochi.
clue.ru-kamchatka-trekker-coverage-descr: Most trekker coverage in Russia is from Kamchatka, identified by grey gravelly soil and volcanic terrain.
clue.ru-tatar-bilingual-sign-description: Bilingual street signs in Tatarstan use "урамы" (ур. abbreviated) for street instead of Russian "улица".
clue.ru-bashkir-bilingual-sign-descripti: Bilingual street signs in Bashkortostan use "урамы" for street, usually written in full.
clue.ru-chuvash-bilingual-sign-descripti: Bilingual street signs in Chuvashia use the Chuvash word "урамӗ" for street.
clue.ru-mari-bilingual-sign-description: Bilingual street signs in Mari El use the Mari word "урем" for street.
clue.ru-komi-bilingual-sign-description: Bilingual street signs in the Komi Republic use the Komi word "улича" for street.
clue.ru-yellow-pole-plate-tatarstan-desc: Yellow identification plates fastened to poles with metal bands are common in Tatarstan.
clue.ru-double-yellow-band-signpost-murm: In Murmansk and some Karelia roads, most signposts have two yellow bands wrapped around them.
clue.ru-cobblestone-pavement-description: Cobblestone roads are common in Kaliningrad, Nizhny Tagil, and Kizel.
clue.ru-extended-insulator-bar-pole-desc: Elongated insulator bars on utility poles appear in southern Chelyabinsk, eastern Orenburg, and southern Kemerovo Oblasts.
clue.ru-decorative-pedestrian-sign-holde: Ornamental pedestrian sign mounting brackets are unique to Pskov Oblast.
clue.ru-mid-line-rectangular-fence-chely: Rounded rectangular fences with a horizontal mid-line are unique to Chelyabinsk and eastern Orenburg Oblasts.
clue.ru-thin-rectangular-top-fence-samar: Fences with a thin rounded rectangular top are found in Syzran, Tolyatti, and Samara.
clue.ru-country-flag-description: The national flag of Russia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.rw-hazy-sky-tint-description: Rwandan coverage has a noticeable haze, especially visible in the sky.
clue.rw-architecture-description: Rwandan buildings are mainly brick and concrete houses with steep roofs and ventilation bricks.
clue.rw-red-tinted-soil-description: Most soil across Rwanda has a reddish tint.
clue.rw-banana-plant-description: Banana plants grow abundantly throughout Rwanda.
clue.rw-bollard-description: Rwandan bollards are red-and-white cylindrical shapes in several designs.
clue.rw-waystone-description: White concrete waystones mark Rwandan roadsides.
clue.rw-clean-street-description: Rwandan streets are tidy and free of litter.
clue.rw-black-white-kerb-description: Rwandan kerbs are painted with alternating black and white stripes.
clue.rw-security-fence-wall-description: Rwandan villa neighbourhoods have many tall security fences and perimeter walls.
clue.rw-district-code-street-sign-descri: Rwandan street names often include a two-letter district prefix.
clue.rw-lamppost-style-national-road-des: Lamp designs vary by national road: green roads have slightly curved arms; red roads have shorter arms with a sharp bend; blue roads have longer fully curved arms; grey roads rarely have lamps.
clue.rw-road-number-lamppost-description: National road numbers are painted in black on lampposts with sequential lamp numbers below.
clue.rw-tea-plantation-western-rwanda-de: Tea plantations are common in western Rwanda and a few other pockets.
clue.rw-northeast-rolling-open-landscape: The northeast has rolling hills with open agricultural or grassland areas.
clue.rw-northwest-volcano-description: Volcanoes and volcanic rocks are visible in the northwest corner.
clue.rw-kigali-luxury-villas-description: Wealthier Kigali neighborhoods feature many luxury villas.
clue.rw-butare-cobblestone-street-descri: Many roads in Butare are paved with cobblestones.
clue.rw-country-flag-description: The national flag of Rwanda is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.pm-licence-plate-description: Saint Pierre and Miquelon plates are white or yellow, short or long, with a blue EU strip on the left; front plates are optional.
clue.pm-colourful-wooden-house-descripti: Homes are boxy wooden panel buildings often painted in bold colours.
clue.pm-grassy-coastal-landscape-descrip: Flat to gently rolling grassland terrain with visible coastline.
clue.pm-saint-pierre-island-rural-trekke: A rural trekker on Saint-Pierre island with rockier terrain and tree-lined paths.
clue.pm-country-flag-description: The national flag of Saint Pierre and Miquelon is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.sm-rolling-agricultural-hills-descr: Gently undulating farmland with lush Mediterranean vegetation and narrow winding roads.
clue.sm-round-concrete-pole-description: Utility poles are mostly round concrete, identical to Italian types; wooden poles also appear.
clue.sm-yellow-burgundy-chevron-descript: Chevrons are yellow boards with burgundy-red arrows, unique to San Marino.
clue.sm-lime-green-bin-description: In San Marino, bright lime-green rubbish bins appear frequently along streets.
clue.sm-country-flag-description: The national flag of San Marino is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.sn-general-01-blue-plates-descripti: Senegal uses blue license plates, the only country in Africa to do so.
clue.sn-road-01-driving-direction-descri: In Senegal they drive on the right side of the road.
clue.sn-french-style-infrastructure-desc: Senegal uses French-pattern bollards, poles, signs, and road markings.
clue.sn-kilometre-marker-description: Senegalese kilometre markers are white posts with red tops showing road numbers and distances.
clue.sn-pink-bordered-town-sign-descript: Senegalese town entry signs are white with a thick pink outline and bold black lettering.
clue.sn-solar-powered-black-lamp-descrip: Black lampposts topped with solar panels appear frequently along Senegalese roads.
clue.sn-yellow-orange-taxi-description: Yellow-orange taxis with black-painted fenders are common in Senegal.
clue.sn-northern-savannah-desert-descrip: North of The Gambia, terrain is flat, arid with sparse, faded foliage trees.
clue.sn-southern-green-region-descriptio: South of The Gambia, vegetation is lush and green with palm trees near the coast.
clue.sn-diourbel-rural-coverage-descript: Extensive rural coverage with sandy unpaved roads and scattered trees around Diourbel.
clue.sn-northwestern-coastal-dune-descri: Gently rolling vegetated sand dunes characterise the northwestern coastline.
clue.sn-bakel-dry-hills-description: Dry terrain with gentle hills appears around Bakel and south to Nayé.
clue.sn-kedougou-greener-hills-descripti: Kedougou and Mako have more verdant vegetation and larger hills.
clue.sn-divided-highway-description: Senegal has two divided highways: Dakar–Touba and Dakar–Saly.
clue.sn-saloum-delta-marshland-descripti: Flat, slightly marshy terrain with low vegetation appears in the Saloum River Delta.
clue.sn-forest-thies-description: Slightly hilly area with dry brown vegetation, bright orange dirt roads, and noticeable haze.
clue.sn-dakar-description: Senegal's capital has dense urban fabric and taller, modern buildings.
clue.sn-country-flag-description: The national flag of Senegal is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.rs-chevrons-description: Serbian chevrons are black arrows on a white background.
clue.rs-licence-plate-description: Serbian plates are white with a blue strip on the left; agricultural vehicles have green plates.
clue.rs-serbian-cyrillic-script-descript: Serbian Cyrillic includes unique letters Ђ/ђ and Ћ/ћ.
clue.rs-serbian-latin-script-description: Serbian Latin uses the special letters Č, Ć, Đ, Š, and Ž.
clue.rs-topography-description: Vojvodina is flat; central-southern regions are hillier; mountains lie in southwest and southeast Serbia.
clue.rs-telephone-area-codes-description: Serbian area codes are two digits starting with 1 to 3, varying by region.
clue.rs-vojvodina-flat-agriculture-descr: Northern Serbia between Hungary and Belgrade is completely flat agricultural land.
clue.rs-central-northern-rolling-hills-d: Gentle rolling hills lie between Vojvodina and southern mountains.
clue.rs-southern-morava-river-basin-desc: Rolling landscape with larger hills and distant mountains.
clue.rs-lush-southern-mountains-descript: Dense green mountains appear along the Bulgarian and Kosovo borders.
clue.rs-autumn-coverage-description: Fall-colored coverage is found around Belgrade, south of Čačak and near Valjevo.
clue.rs-language-01-bilingual-descriptio: Serbian can be written in both Cyrillic or Latin letters. You can often find both written on signs here.
clue.rs-yellow-centre-lines-e-80-descrip: A short E-80 section north of Pirot has yellow centre lines.
clue.rs-country-flag-description: The national flag of Serbia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.sl-hilly-forested-landscape-descrip: Slovenia's terrain is very hilly and heavily forested, with patches of agriculture.
clue.sl-deep-forest-road-description: Many Slovenian roads run deep through dense forest.
clue.sl-architecture-description: Slovenian buildings are alpine-inspired with light walls, dark wood details, and semi-steep half-hipped roofs.
clue.sl-slovene-language-description: A Slavic language using special letters Č, Š, and Ž.
clue.sl-bollard-description: Slovenian bollards are white with black tops; front reflectors are red, back reflectors white.
clue.sl-directional-sign-description: Slovenian directional signs are yellow with a black border.
clue.sl-kilometre-marker-description: Slovenian kilometre markers show road number in a yellow rectangle, a second number, a black divider, and distance below.
clue.sl-chevron-description: Slovenian chevrons usually have red arrows on white; sometimes black arrows on white.
clue.sl-pedestrian-sign-description: Slovenian pedestrian signs show five stripes and a simply drawn person with no belt.
clue.sl-dashed-outer-road-line-descripti: Slovenian roads often have long dashed edge lines.
clue.sl-street-sign-description: Slovenian street signs are usually white with metal borders on posts; red variants attach to house walls.
clue.sl-red-house-number-description: Slovenian house number plates are typically red with white text.
clue.sl-kozolec-drying-rack-description: Open-sided wooden sheds with visible gaps, typical of Slovenia.
clue.sl-northwestern-alpine-region-descr: Slovenia's tallest mountains are in the alpine northwest.
clue.sl-eastern-plain-description: Flat or rolling agricultural fields with no mountains indicate eastern Slovenia.
clue.sl-adriatic-coast-description: White cliffs, Mediterranean vegetation, vineyards, and Mediterranean-style architecture near Slovenia's Adriatic coast.
clue.sl-southeast-valley-description: A wide east–west valley with mountains visible to north and south in southeastern Slovenia.
clue.sl-bilingual-italian-sign-descripti: Bilingual Slovenian-Italian signs appear in Slovenia's western coastal region.
clue.sl-country-flag-description: The national flag of Slovenia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.sg-licence-plate-description: Singaporean plates are mostly black with white text, unlike Malaysian and Indonesian plates.
clue.sg-directional-sign-description: Singaporean directional signs are green with white English text and expressway codes like TPE.
clue.sg-road-sign-white-backing-descript: All road signs are mounted on square white background panels, unique to Singapore.
clue.sg-rain-tree-description: Large rain trees line many main roads throughout Singapore.
clue.sg-road-surface-warning-description: Text warnings like "HUMP AHEAD" are painted directly on Singapore roads.
clue.sg-bus-stop-bollard-description: Concrete bollards with black-and-yellow bands protect every bus stop in Singapore.
clue.sg-bus-leaving-box-description: A yellow box with an arrow is sometimes painted on the road at Singapore bus stops.
clue.sg-traffic-light-description: Singaporean traffic lights have a standard design with a curved metal sheet with holes.
clue.sg-neighbourhood-name-street-sign-d: Suburban streets in Singapore often include their neighbourhood name.
clue.sg-country-flag-description: The national flag of Singapore is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.sk-wide-type-b-guardrail-descriptio: Broad guardrails are unique to Slovakia and Czechia.
clue.sk-paired-concrete-utility-pole-des: Broad cylindrical concrete poles often mounted side by side.
clue.sk-short-metal-bar-pole-top-descrip: Compact horizontal metal bars carrying line insulators.
clue.sk-inverted-triangle-pole-support-d: Two angled braces create upside-down triangle silhouette.
clue.sk-trident-pole-top-description: Three-pronged pole top with two outer arms angled upward.
clue.sk-bolt-mounted-lamp-post-base-desc: Chunky base plates secured by opposing pairs of bolts.
clue.sk-red-white-striped-temporary-sign: Square poles wrapped in alternating red and white bands.
clue.sk-striped-gas-water-marker-pole-ti: Striped Gas and Water Marker Poles
clue.sk-striped-gas-water-marker-pole-de: Slender roadside poles painted in coloured stripes indicating underground lines.
clue.sk-three-stripe-hiking-trail-marker: Coloured band between two white bands; sometimes arrow-shaped.
clue.sk-colourful-prefab-apartment-descr: Soviet-era panel buildings often repainted in vibrant colours and patterns.
clue.sk-diamond-roof-tiles-description: Roofing composed of small diamond-shaped tiles is widespread.
clue.sk-black-bridge-marker-sign-descrip: Dark plaques near bridge ends display the road number on the left side.
clue.sk-slovak-czech-language-difference: Slovak uses unique accented letters like L with caron (Ľ) and O with circumflex (Ô); Czech uses others like R with caron (Ř) and U with ring (Ů).
clue.sk-landscape-contrast-czechia-descr: Slovakia alternates between dramatic mountains and flat lowlands.
clue.sk-blue-directional-signs-small-arr: Blue Directional Signs with Small Arrows
Road direction signs have a blue background with compact white arrows.
clue.sk-sign-border-flush-edge-descripti: Painted borders run right up to the physical edge of Slovak road signs.
clue.sk-highway-signs-edge-flush-borders: Motorway signs in blue or green have a white border touching the panel edge.
clue.sk-white-house-number-sign-descript: Building numbers appear on white plaques with thin red or black borders.
clue.sk-sign-post-cap-styles-description: Sign post tops are open, capped with grey metal discs, or thin black caps.
clue.sk-pedestrian-crossing-sign-descrip: Signs feature five crossing stripes with either a simple figure or closely bunched stripes.
clue.sk-bold-road-sign-font-description: Road signs use a notably heavy, bold typeface.
clue.sk-two-section-kilometre-marker-des: Distance markers have upper and lower sections separated by a black line; road number is on top.
clue.sk-cycling-signs-marked-c-descripti: Cycle route signs display the letter C and resemble Czechoslovak hiking markers.
clue.sk-window-shutter-description: Houses with window shutters appear frequently.
clue.sk-hip-end-roofs-facing-road-descri: Residential buildings often have narrow gable ends facing the street with hipped roofs.
clue.sk-grey-metal-roof-description: Unpainted grey sheet-metal roofing is widespread, especially in the east.
clue.sk-gen-3-spring-coverage-descriptio: Most imagery was captured in spring.
clue.sk-railway-crossing-sign-white-back: Railway Crossing Sign with White Background
Level crossing warning signs are mounted on white rectangular panels.
clue.sk-double-sign-posts-small-signs-ti: Double Sign Posts on Small Signs
clue.sk-double-sign-posts-small-signs-de: Small road signs are often supported by two parallel posts.
clue.sk-new-wedge-bollard-red-reflector-: New Wedge-Shaped Bollard with Red Reflector
A new wedge-shaped bollard with a red front reflector is introduced.
clue.sk-wooden-poles-white-concrete-supp: Wooden Poles and White Concrete Supports
Wooden utility poles with white concrete braces appear somewhat often.
clue.sk-phone-number-area-codes-descript: Telephone numbers are ten digits with the first two or three digits as area codes.
clue.sk-road-numbering-system-descriptio: Roads have three- or four-digit numbers. Three-digit 500-560 and four-digit roads increase west to east.
clue.sk-topography-overview-description: Highest mountains are central and north; flattest terrain is southwest and southeast.
clue.sk-western-lowland-description: Southwestern plains have perfectly flat agricultural fields stretching to the horizon.
clue.sk-eastern-lowland-description: Broad farmland with distant hills or ridges defines the eastern lowland region.
clue.sk-hungarian-majority-areas-south-d: Southern areas have Hungarian-speaking populations with bilingual street names.
clue.sk-yellow-circle-markings-poles-des: Concrete poles with painted yellow circles are concentrated in Nitra and Trnava regions.
clue.sk-yellow-lamp-posts-blue-bases-tit: Yellow Lamp Posts with Blue Bases
clue.sk-yellow-lamp-posts-blue-bases-des: Lamp posts have yellow bodies with blue bases, mainly in the east.
clue.sk-northern-mountain-valley-descrip: Two broad valleys flanked by tall, jagged peaks lie in the north. The nearest mountain range side helps tell them apart.
clue.sk-pine-forest-far-west-description: Dense pine woodland is characteristic of western Slovakia.
clue.sk-rusyn-bilingual-signs-northeast-: Town entry signs in northeastern Presov may include Rusyn text in Cyrillic script.
clue.sk-zilina-trolleybus-description: Trolleybuses in Zilina have a green-yellow-white livery; overhead poles match in yellow and green.
clue.sk-country-flag-description: The national flag of Slovakia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.si-hilly-forested-landscape-descrip: Slovenia is very hilly and heavily forested with some agriculture.
clue.si-deep-forest-road-description: Many roads run deep through dense forest in Slovenia.
clue.si-slovene-language-description: Slovene is a Slavic language using special letters Č, Š, and Ž.
clue.si-kilometre-marker-description: Road number in a yellow rectangle top left, second number right, black divider, distance below.
clue.si-chevron-description: Red arrows on white background; sometimes black arrows on white.
clue.si-pedestrian-sign-description: Five stripes and a simply drawn person with no belt.
clue.si-dashed-outer-road-line-descripti: Long dashed edge lines on roads.
clue.si-kozolec-drying-rack-description: Open-sided wooden sheds with thin beams and visible gaps.
clue.si-northwestern-alpine-region-descr: Tallest mountains in the alpine northwest.
clue.si-eastern-plain-description: Flat or rolling agricultural fields with no mountains or tall hills.
clue.si-adriatic-coast-description: White cliffs, Mediterranean vegetation, vineyards, and Mediterranean-style architecture.
clue.si-southeast-valley-description: Wide east–west valley with mountains to north and south.
clue.si-bilingual-italian-sign-descripti: Slovenian-Italian bilingual signs in the westernmost coastal region.
clue.si-country-flag-description: The national flag of Slovenia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.za-yellow-edge-line-description: Most South African roads feature single yellow edge lines paired with white centre lines.
clue.za-triple-centre-line-description: South Africa has a pattern of three white centre lines: two solid outer lines bracketing a dashed inner one.
clue.za-bird-pole-description: South African poles often have 1–5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators resembling rows of perching birds.
clue.za-triangular-warning-sign-descript: South African warning signs are red-bordered triangles on a white background.
clue.xx-general-01-18-south-african-chev: South Africa uses red and white chevron signs, and small, thin chevrons with a single arrow are common across Southern African countries.
clue.za-provincial-licence-plate-descrip: Each South African province has its own plate design; Free State plates have a greenish tint, KwaZulu-Natal plates lean bluish.
clue.za-national-highway-map-description: South African N-roads appear with the letter N on signs and as blue pentagons with numbers on Google Maps.
clue.za-r-road-number-region-description: Three-digit R-roads in South Africa are roughly grouped geographically.
clue.za-telephone-area-code-description: South African landline numbers are 10 digits; the first three digits form the area code starting with 0.
clue.za-a-shaped-pole-top-western-cape-d: Poles with three bars forming an "A" shape appear almost exclusively in Western Cape.
clue.za-wide-a-shaped-pole-top-eastern-c: A wider version of A-shaped poles with bottom insulators attached directly to the A-frame appears in Eastern Cape.
clue.za-trident-pole-top-kwazulu-natal-d: Three-pronged trident pole tops are nearly unique to KwaZulu-Natal.
clue.za-alternating-horizontal-insulator: Three alternating insulators projecting horizontally from the pole top are concentrated in Limpopo, Gauteng, North West, and Mpumalanga.
clue.za-chevron-pole-top-northeast-descr: Two diagonal bars forming a "<" shape are found mostly in Limpopo and North West.
clue.za-metal-arm-pole-top-mpumalanga-de: One or two metal arms holding insulators are most common in Mpumalanga.
clue.za-red-sign-back-sticker-descriptio: Square red stickers on the rear of road signs appear frequently in Eastern Cape and nearby parts of Northern Cape and Free State.
clue.za-white-chevron-back-sticker-descr: White stickers on the rear of chevron signs are common in the Cape provinces.
clue.za-grainy-pink-pavement-limpopo-des: A coarse, slightly pinkish road surface reminiscent of Texas pavement.
clue.za-bird-nest-pole-northern-cape-des: Large communal bird nests atop utility poles are frequent in northern Northern Cape.
clue.za-dry-northeast-landscape-descript: Arid terrain with orange-red soil and shrub-covered hills or mountains characterises the northeast.
clue.za-rocky-mountain-western-cape-desc: Treeless rocky mountains with tall, steep sides and sharp peaks are distinctive to Western Cape.
clue.za-vineyard-western-cape-descriptio: Vineyards concentrate in coastal valleys of Western Cape, with clusters near Upington in Northern Cape.
clue.za-red-soil-desert-northern-cape-de: Dry expanses of red soil typify the Northern Cape interior.
clue.za-sugarcane-kwazulu-natal-descript: Sugarcane fields line much of the KwaZulu-Natal coast and patches along the Mpumalanga–Mozambique border.
clue.za-cook-pine-tree-southeast-coast-d: Distinctively tall Cook pines grow mainly between East London and Durban along the southeastern coast.
clue.za-pine-plantation-near-eswatini-de: Commercial pine plantations are concentrated west of Eswatini and in parts of southern KwaZulu-Natal.
clue.za-grassy-rolling-hill-western-cape: Green rolling grassland stretches between Cape Town and George, usually with tall ridges visible to the north or east.
clue.za-flat-subtropical-coast-mozambiqu: Noticeably flat terrain with lush green subtropical vegetation near the Mozambique border.
clue.za-metropolitan-m-route-description: In South Africa, major urban roads are designated with the letter M.
clue.za-informal-pole-advert-gauteng-des: Poles and public infrastructure around Gauteng are often plastered with informal advertisements.
clue.za-country-flag-description: The national flag of South Africa is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.es-licence-plate-description: Standard elongated white EU plates with a single blue strip on the left edge.
clue.es-bollard-description: Hollow posts with a yellow-orange reflector on the front; rear has two small white dots or is blank.
clue.es-ladder-wooden-pole-description: Common poles include concrete 'ladder' poles with step-like indentations and plain wooden poles.
clue.es-french-style-pole-top-descriptio: Pole tops have an inverted-triangle with a gently upward-curving horizontal crossbar.
clue.xx-general-01-60-road-markers-descr: Distance markers along Spanish roads are recognisable by their colourful borders and the road number printed at the top.
clue.es-guardrail-description: Spain uses rounded guardrails with yellow reflectors.
clue.es-stop-sign-font-description: Spanish stop signs use a distinctively small typeface for 'STOP'.
clue.es-sign-red-border-description: The red border on warning and prohibition signs runs right to the edge with no white outline.
clue.es-flat-signpost-description: Nearly all traffic signs, kilometre markers, and chevrons are mounted on flat-profile signposts.
clue.xx-road-signs-01-01-spanish-chevron: In Spain, you can find both black and white chevrons and blue and white chevrons.
clue.es-direction-sign-description: Wayfinding signs have a white background with multi-coloured road number boxes; motorways use blue.
clue.es-dashed-outer-road-line-descripti: Some rural roads feature dashed edge lines; many still use solid edge lines.
clue.es-spanish-language-description: Spanish is dominant; the letter Ñ is exclusive to Spanish.
clue.es-street-name-calle-description: 'Calle' is the standard Spanish word for street on urban signs.
clue.es-vado-permanente-sign-description: 'Vado permanente' no-parking plaques are mounted on garage doors and gates.
clue.es-landscape-diversity-description: Spain's scenery ranges from lush forests and plateaus to semi-deserts and mountains.
clue.es-mediterranean-climate-descriptio: Most of the country has a dry Mediterranean climate reflected in vegetation and agriculture.
clue.es-regional-road-code-description: Road markers carry region-specific letter codes; national roads use codes like E, AP, A, R, and N.
clue.es-telephone-area-code-description: Landline numbers start with 9 plus a two-digit regional code; mobiles start with 6.
clue.es-catalan-language-description: Catalan is used in Catalonia, Valencian Community, and Balearic Islands; identified by 'i' for 'and' and grave accents.
clue.es-catalan-street-name-carrer-descr: 'Carrer' is the Catalan word for street on signs in Catalonia and the Balearics.
clue.es-gual-permanent-sign-description: 'Gual permanente' signs are common in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands.
clue.es-basque-language-description: Basque is a language isolate spoken in the Basque Country and northern Navarre with distinctive Z and K usage.
clue.es-basque-street-name-kalea-descrip: 'Kalea' is the Basque word for street; Spanish 'calle' is also common.
clue.es-basque-bilingual-sub-sign-descri: Road signs often have bilingual plates with a black border; Basque usually on top in Basque Country.
clue.es-galician-language-description: Galician is closely related to Portuguese, spoken in Galicia, distinguishable by Ñ and no Ç.
clue.es-galician-street-name-rua-descrip: 'Rúa' is the Galician word for street, often accented.
clue.es-galician-town-name-article-descr: Galician place names often start with articles A, O, As, or Os.
clue.es-regional-flag-andalusia-descript: Green-white-green horizontal stripes with a central coat of arms.
clue.es-regional-flag-aragon-description: Four red stripes on yellow with coat of arms on the hoist side.
clue.es-regional-flag-asturias-descripti: Sky blue field with a yellow Cross of the Victory in the centre.
clue.es-regional-flag-balearic-islands-d: Four red stripes on yellow with a purple canton containing a white castle.
clue.es-regional-flag-basque-country-des: Red field with green diagonal cross behind a white upright cross.
clue.es-regional-flag-canary-islands-des: Three vertical stripes of white, blue, and yellow with a central coat of arms.
clue.es-regional-flag-cantabria-descript: Two horizontal stripes of white over red with a coat of arms in the upper hoist.
clue.es-regional-flag-castile-la-mancha-: Two vertical halves: red with yellow castle on hoist, white on fly.
clue.es-regional-flag-castile-and-leon-d: Chequered pattern of yellow castles on red and purple lions on white in 2x2 layout.
clue.es-regional-flag-catalonia-descript: Four horizontal red stripes on a yellow field (the Senyera), displayed throughout Catalonia.
clue.es-regional-flag-extremadura-descri: Three horizontal stripes of green, white, black with the coat of arms in the centre, displayed throughout Extremadura.
clue.es-regional-flag-galicia-descriptio: White field with a diagonal blue stripe and the coat of arms in the centre, displayed throughout Galicia.
clue.es-regional-flag-la-rioja-descripti: Four horizontal stripes of red, white, green, yellow with the coat of arms in the centre, displayed throughout La Rioja.
clue.es-regional-flag-madrid-description: Red field with seven five-pointed white stars arranged in a 4-3 pattern, displayed throughout Madrid.
clue.es-regional-flag-murcia-description: Red field with four yellow castles in the upper hoist and seven crowns in the lower fly, displayed throughout Murcia.
clue.es-regional-flag-navarre-descriptio: Red field with golden chains radiating from a central emerald coat of arms, displayed throughout Navarre.
clue.es-regional-flag-valencia-descripti: Four horizontal red stripes on yellow with a blue vertical band on the hoist containing a crown and heraldic motifs, displayed throughout Valencia.
clue.es-catalan-independence-flag-descri: An unofficial flag in Catalan-speaking areas, based on the red-and-yellow striped Senyera pattern.
clue.es-topography-description: Spain is mountainous with major ranges like the Pyrenees, Sierra Nevada, Cantabrian Mountains, Iberian System, and Sierra Morena. The Meseta Central is a high plateau. Four main rivers define drainage basins.
clue.es-green-northern-coast-description: The far north is lush with rolling hills, hedgerows, and verdant meadows.
clue.es-pyrenees-description: Mountain range along the French border with light-grey rock faces, pine forests, and stone-walled architecture.
clue.es-pyrenean-pine-forest-description: Dense tall pine forests cover much of the Pyrenees and smaller hills in the Basque Country or Navarre.
clue.es-castilla-leon-flatland-descripti: Broad, gently undulating agricultural plain dominated by cereal crops and occasional sunflower fields.
clue.es-la-rioja-vineyard-description: Vineyards flanked by mountain ranges to the north and south indicate La Rioja.
clue.es-aragon-ebro-semi-desert-descript: Semi-arid terrain with sandy soil and low scrubby vegetation along the Ebro basin from Navarre through Aragón.
clue.es-aragon-arid-plain-description: Flat, parched terrain in central and southern Aragón with pale rocky or red earth soil.
clue.es-castilla-la-mancha-description: Flat terrain with common vineyards and olive plantations, especially in western provinces.
clue.es-holm-cork-oak-extremadura-descri: Open pastures with widely spaced holm and cork oaks, typical of Extremadura and surroundings.
clue.es-murcia-arid-landscape-descriptio: Sandy soil, medium mountains, and roadside plantations of small fruit and olive trees around Murcia.
clue.es-murcia-hazy-mountain-description: Bare, rugged mountains often seen through hazy mist in Murcia and southern Alicante.
clue.es-sierra-nevada-description: Snow-capped peaks visible from November through May. Sierra Nevada is the only mountain range in southern Spain that carries snow for most of the year.
clue.es-malaga-white-village-description: Settlements composed entirely of white-painted houses cascading down mountain slopes are a quintessential sight along the southern coast near Málaga.
clue.es-olive-tree-description: Olive cultivation is widespread across more than half of Spain.
clue.es-massive-olive-plantation-descrip: Vast olive groves over rolling hills concentrated around Córdoba and Jaén.
clue.es-olive-plantation-south-madrid-de: Olive groves on flat terrain is common south of Madrid.
clue.es-olive-plantation-east-coast-desc: East-coast olive groves enclosed by fences or stone walls with visible mountains nearby.
clue.es-eucalyptus-plantation-north-coas: Eucalyptus plantations line the entire northern coast, especially abundant in Galicia.
clue.es-eucalyptus-dry-environment-descr: Eucalyptus in arid areas likely places you in Huelva province or nearby.
clue.es-orange-plantation-east-coast-des: Orange groves on the Mediterranean coast from Valencia southward, in small valleys with mountains to the west.
clue.es-orange-plantation-guadalquivir-b: Orange orchards on open, flat terrain in the Guadalquivir river basin.
clue.es-corn-field-description: Corn cultivated in major river basins, northern coast, and northwest Castilla y León.
clue.es-stone-pine-description: Pinus pinea has a compact, bulbous crown wider than tall. Flat forests dominated by stone pines are common near Valladolid and Huelva.
clue.es-aleppo-pine-description: Pinus halepensis has a looser, irregular crown. It is the most prevalent pine along the east coast and Balearic Islands.
clue.es-baltic-pine-scots-pine-descripti: Pinus sylvestris grows tall and slender with dark bark that sheds near the top to reveal orange-red wood. The lower trunk is usually branchless. Found mainly in the Pyrenees, Sierra de Guadarrama, and the Iberian System.
clue.es-maritime-pine-atlantic-variant-d: Near the Atlantic coast, Pinus pinaster shows grey bark with red undertones and fluffy upward-pointing branches. Mature trees lose their lower branches.
clue.es-maritime-pine-mediterranean-vari: Away from the Atlantic, Pinus pinaster has grey, deeply fissured bark with red tones. Found in mountain ranges across central and southern Spain.
clue.es-regional-road-line-style-descrip: Small road markings vary by region with solid or dashed edge lines and varied centre lines.
clue.es-kilometre-marker-shape-descripti: Marker posts are rectangular or square, roughly splitting the country. Andalusia's are extra tall, Madrid's show the regional flag, Biscay's have semi-circular tops.
clue.es-kilometre-marker-border-colour-d: Border colours correspond to road size: orange for large, green for medium, yellow for small roads.
clue.es-galician-concello-sign-descripti: Town entry signs in Galicia feature a green or blue strip at the top displaying the municipality name. The word 'Concello' (municipality) is exclusive to this region.
clue.es-asturias-bus-stop-description: Red bus stop posts bearing the CTA logo at the top are specific to Asturias.
clue.es-asturias-cogersa-bin-description: Rubbish and recycling containers marked with the COGERSA logo are recognisable even from a distance and indicate Asturias.
clue.es-asturias-yellow-snow-pole-descri: Yellow roadside poles with one or two reflectors are unique to Asturias, typically found in the mountainous south of the region.
clue.es-aragon-bollard-description: Short, flat rectangular white stick with grey reflectors on both sides common on Aragón regional roads.
clue.es-corrugated-round-signpost-descri: Round corrugated-metal signposts are common in Catalonia, the Basque Country, and the Balearic Islands.
clue.es-catalan-hunting-sign-description: Signs reading 'Àrea privada de Caça' mark private hunting grounds in Catalonia and sometimes the Balearics.
clue.es-lleida-tarragona-bollard-descrip: A bollard with a square orange reflector on the front and a white reflector on the back is almost exclusive to the provinces of Lleida and Tarragona on the mainland.
clue.es-catalan-single-arrow-chevron-des: Large square chevron boards with a single directional arrow are common in Catalonia.
clue.es-murcia-red-arrow-chevron-descrip: Small square chevrons with a red arrow on a white background are exclusive to the region of Murcia.
clue.es-madrid-bus-stop-description: Round-topped red bus stop posts and green inter-urban buses indicate the Community of Madrid. Blue urban buses operate within the city centre.
clue.es-extremadura-green-top-bollard-de: Standard Spanish bollards capped with a green top are exclusive to Extremadura.
clue.es-castilla-la-mancha-stone-marker-: Low stone markers with the regional coat of arms, blue left side and unpainted right side, line field boundaries.
clue.es-rectangular-mesh-pole-descriptio: Steel lattice poles with rectangular cross-sections are concentrated in southern Spain, especially Murcia and southern Alicante.
clue.es-andalusia-green-stripe-sign-desc: Regional government signs have a green stripe along the left edge; smaller green-posted versions appear near nature reserves.
clue.es-andalusia-snow-pole-description: Blue-and-yellow snow marker poles unique to Andalusia.
clue.es-slate-roof-northwest-description: Nearly black slate roofing dominates northwestern Spain, western Galicia, the Pyrenees near Andorra, and mountains northeast of Madrid.
clue.es-galician-concrete-block-house-de: Large concrete blocks, sometimes textured like stone, are common building material in Galicia.
clue.es-galician-granary-horrero-descrip: Elongated raised granaries called 'hórreos gallegos' or 'cabazos' are characteristic of Galician farms.
clue.es-asturian-granary-horrero-descrip: Asturian hórreos are larger, squarer, elevated on four pillars; 'panera' variant sits on six or eight supports. Slate roofs indicate western Asturias.
clue.es-basque-white-house-description: Large white-rendered houses with exposed timber frames are typical of the Basque Country, Basque Navarre, and Cantabria.
clue.es-catalan-masia-description: Traditional stone farmhouses, usually isolated or in small clusters, common in Catalonia, eastern Aragón, and parts of the Valencian Community.
clue.es-white-house-town-south-descripti: Entire towns of whitewashed houses are common in Andalusia and Extremadura.
clue.es-asturias-black-car-description: A black vehicle with no antenna and a visible brake light is associated with Asturias.
clue.es-balearic-island-landscape-descri: Coastal Mediterranean feel with dry Aleppo pine forests on hillsides and small agricultural patches of fruit and olive trees.
clue.es-balearic-rock-wall-description: Low dry-stone walls are extremely prevalent throughout the Balearic Islands.
clue.es-balearic-architecture-descriptio: White-painted houses with gently inclined tile roofs are the norm; some have flat roofs.
clue.es-formentera-description: A small, low-lying island characterised by coastal scrubland. The mountains of neighbouring Ibiza are often visible from the north shore.
clue.es-mallorca-mountain-description: A tall mountain range runs along northwestern Mallorca and is visible from much of the island. No other Balearic island has peaks of comparable size.
clue.es-canary-island-location-descripti: A Spanish archipelago off Africa's west coast, far from mainland Spain.
clue.es-canary-island-landscape-descript: Diverse landscapes: volcanic mountains, pine forests, lava fields, arid zones, and Mediterranean-like countryside.
clue.es-lanzarote-volcanic-soil-descript: Very dark exposed volcanic terrain, almost lunar in places, is more abundant on Lanzarote than on any other Canary Island.
clue.es-fuerteventura-description: An arid island with sparse vegetation. Orange-tinted soil is essentially unique to Fuerteventura within the Canary chain.
clue.es-las-palmas-bollard-description: Bollards with square orange front and white rear reflectors common in Las Palmas province and parts of mainland Spain.
clue.es-lanzarote-wine-plantation-descri: Unique vineyards where each vine is sheltered inside a semicircular stone wall built on dark volcanic soil.
clue.es-la-graciosa-description: A small, barren island north of Lanzarote with consistently overcast skies. Its two south-coast settlements consist of white, flat-roofed houses.
clue.es-ceuta-melilla-location-descripti: Two Spanish autonomous cities on the North African coast, partially surrounded by Morocco.
clue.es-ceuta-architecture-description: North African style, flat-roofed buildings in warm tones from pale yellow to red.
clue.es-ceuta-landscape-description: Hilly Mediterranean terrain with eucalyptus and pine trees outside the urban core.
clue.es-ceuta-black-white-guardrail-desc: Guardrails painted in alternating black and white are unique to Ceuta within Spain.
clue.es-melilla-description: North African architecture similar to Ceuta, with hazy, desaturated, and overcast imagery.
clue.es-camino-santiago-description: Pilgrim routes marked by a yellow scallop shell on a blue background on signs and road surfaces.
clue.es-castilla-la-mancha-spring-covera: Early spring imagery showing dirt farm tracks between bright green fields and bare vineyards on red soil.
clue.es-ap-15-navarra-bollard-descriptio: Flat bollards with square red reflectors, accompanied by guardrails also fitted with red reflectors. Unlike the yellow reflectors seen elsewhere in Spain.
clue.es-barcelona-taxi-description: Black cars with yellow doors, the yellow extends to the boot lid as well.
clue.es-ebro-delta-description: An exceptionally flat landscape of rice paddies and water channels. Significant mountains are visible to the south, west, and north.
clue.es-almeria-greenhouse-description: Dense clusters of white-roofed greenhouses fill the lowland between Almería and Motril, particularly around the town of El Ejido.
clue.es-bilbao-street-sign-description: Street name plaques in Bilbao are set inside an ornate decorative frame not found elsewhere in Spain.
clue.es-donana-national-park-car-meta-de: A unique vehicle type appears on coverage southwest of Seville within the Doñana National Park.
clue.es-country-flag-description: The national flag of Spain is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.lk-language-01-sinhala-writing-desc: The written Sri Lankan language Sinhala have letters that are very round. Some letter makes it look like there are small doodle characters among us.
clue.xx-general-01-43-sri-lanka-poles-de: Sri Lanka commonly uses concrete utility poles with large see through holes in the lower half, often called holey poles
clue.lk-waystone-description: Tall white concrete posts have an indented base section with a yellow road number.
clue.lk-road-line-edge-description: Rural roads often have white edge lines but no centre line.
clue.lk-tropical-landscape-description: Lush green tropical vegetation dominates, with a patchwork of cultivated fields.
clue.lk-tiled-roof-description: Houses frequently have orange or red tile roofs that weather to brownish tones.
clue.lk-buddhism-description: Temples, stupas, Buddha statues, and Buddhist flags are common.
clue.lk-other-religion-description: Hinduism, Islam, and Christianity have distinct regional strongholds.
clue.lk-tuk-tuk-description: Sri Lankan tuk-tuks are bulky with a black roof, typically painted green, yellow, or red.
clue.lk-area-code-description: Sri Lankan landline numbers are 10 digits, starting with a 0 area code. Mobile numbers begin with 07.
clue.lk-religious-distribution-map-descr: Buddhism dominates most of Sri Lanka except the north and east coast. Hinduism is strongest in the north, east, and around Nuwara Eliya. Islam is along the east coast. Christianity clusters in the northwest around Mannar.
clue.lk-tamil-script-distribution-descri: Tamil script appears in Hindu-majority areas: north, east, and central Nuwara Eliya. Tamil-only signs indicate Tamil-majority areas.
clue.lk-topography-description: Hills and mountains are concentrated in central-southern Sri Lanka; the rest is relatively flat.
clue.lk-wet-southwest-climate-descriptio: The southwest receives more rainfall, producing dense, deep-green vegetation.
clue.lk-drier-climate-elsewhere-descript: Outside the wet southwest, the landscape is more open and scrubby with mixed brown and green tones.
clue.lk-tea-plantation-description: Bright-green shrubs planted in neat rows on hillsides, concentrated in central and southwestern highlands, especially west of Nuwara Eliya.
clue.lk-country-flag-description: The national flag of Sri Lanka is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.sj-barren-arctic-landscape-descript: Treeless mountains with moss and grasses; often overcast sky.
clue.sj-russian-language-sign-descriptio: Russian text appears on some signs.
clue.sj-longyearbyen-description: Svalbard's largest settlement, characterised by boxy, minimalistic buildings.
clue.sj-pyramiden-description: An abandoned-feeling settlement with Soviet-style apartment blocks and little human activity. Pyramidal mountains are visible in the distance.
clue.sj-barentsburg-description: The most desolate of Svalbard's three settlements. Multi-coloured apartment blocks sit near the hilltop, and coverage is notably more overcast and gloomy.
clue.sj-nw-spitsbergen-national-park-shi: A large ship circles the Northwest Spitsbergen National Park. Coverage darkens toward the east as the sun sets.
clue.sj-wooden-deck-boat-description: A boat with a wooden deck can be found at specific locations around the archipelago.
clue.sj-country-flag-description: The national flag of Svalbard and Jan Mayen is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.xx-general-01-59-tall-grass-descrip: Eswatini features stretches of tall grass.
clue.sz-dark-brown-wooden-poles-descript: Eswatini's utility poles are dark brown wood with side-mounted insulators.
clue.sz-licence-plate-description: Eswatini plates are long with a green bottom section.
clue.sz-western-highland-grassland-descr: Montane grasslands with golden grass and mountainous backdrop characterise the western highlands.
clue.sz-pine-tree-plantations-descriptio: Commercial pine plantations occur in select western areas.
clue.sz-central-south-dark-green-region-: Area with dark green vegetation and tall wooded mountains.
clue.sz-eastern-flatlands-description: Eswatini's eastern lowlands have flat terrain with distant mountains.
clue.sz-sugarcane-eastern-border-descrip: Sugarcane is cultivated near the eastern boundary with Mozambique.
clue.sz-country-flag-description: The national flag of Eswatini is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.
clue.se-licence-plate-description: Swedish plates are long and white with a blue EU strip; taxi plates have a yellow background.
clue.se-swedish-language-description: Swedish is a North Germanic language with the letters Å, Ä, and Ö.
clue.se-white-road-line-description: All road markings in Sweden are white.
clue.se-utility-pole-description: Swedish wooden utility poles often have a small black metal cap on top.
clue.se-lamp-mounting-wooden-pole-descri: Lamps on Swedish wooden poles are mounted slightly below the top with a double-bolt arrangement.
clue.se-electricity-marker-description: Wooden electricity markers with a blue and white stripe at the top are unique to Sweden.
clue.se-directional-sign-description: Most Swedish directional signs are blue with white text and an arrow, while yellow signs with black text are typically used for smaller local destinations.
clue.se-warning-road-sign-description: Swedish warning and regulatory signs have a red border with a yellow background.
clue.se-chevron-sign-description: Swedish chevrons feature yellow arrows on a blue background.
clue.se-meeting-place-sign-description: Blue signs with a large white M indicate designated meeting places on smaller roads.
clue.se-striped-signpost-marking-descrip: Swedish signposts often have coloured striped markings, commonly blue-and-white or red-and-yellow.
clue.se-red-yellow-road-infrastructure-d: Road infrastructure and work signs in Sweden are often painted red and yellow.
clue.se-street-name-suffix-description: Swedish street names often end in "vägen" or "gatan," abbreviated as "v" and "g" on signs.
clue.se-landscape-overview-description: Sweden has boreal forests, farmlands, lakes, mountainous north and west, and flatter south and east.
clue.se-traditional-wooden-fence-descrip: Traditional fences use thin vertical tree trunks with diagonal trunks stacked on top.
clue.se-volvo-car-description: Volvo is the most popular car brand, nearly 30% of passenger vehicles.
clue.se-swedish-church-flag-description: The church flag has a red cross on yellow with a crown in the centre.
clue.se-broad-leafed-tree-description: Broad-leafed trees grow naturally only in southern Sweden and increase further south.
clue.se-fern-description: Ferns are mostly in southern and central Sweden, occasionally further north along the east coast.
clue.se-treeless-mountain-top-descriptio: Mountains with bare, treeless summits are found exclusively in northwestern Sweden.
clue.se-far-north-boreal-vegetation-desc: Thin, sparse boreal trees growing on sandy soil are characteristic of Sweden's far north.
clue.se-beech-forest-description: Beech forests have barren floors carpeted with brown leaves and are restricted to southern Sweden.
clue.se-rock-wall-description: Stone walls are mainly found in southern Sweden, especially along coasts, Öland, and Gotland.
clue.se-exposed-rock-west-coast-title: Exposed Rocks on the West Coast
clue.se-exposed-rock-west-coast-descript: Rounded, exposed rocky outcrops with low vegetation are common along the Swedish west coast.
clue.se-skane-open-agricultural-landscap: Skåne features open farmland with scattered trees and diverse crops.
clue.se-lake-malaren-landscape-descripti: Around Lake Mälaren, flat terrain has medium fields, forests in the background, and small tree clusters in fields.
clue.se-vastergotland-ostergotland-farml: Flat, open farmland with abundant wind turbines and distant forest lines.
clue.se-halland-west-coast-landscape-des: Flat fields with small, round forested hills and lush vegetation characterize Halland's west coast.
clue.se-northern-coastal-farmland-descri: Flat, small-to-medium agricultural fields near the coast between Umeå and Luleå.
clue.se-jamtland-hillside-farmland-descr: Large farmlands on wide, steep hillsides around Lake Storsjön, usually covered in grass.
clue.se-high-coast-landscape-description: Forested, rocky mountains surround winding agricultural valleys in the High Coast area.
clue.se-sodermanland-valley-field-descri: Medium to small agricultural fields run through small valleys lined with forests.
clue.se-white-sand-gotland-description: White sand is often visible alongside roads on Gotland, especially northern parts and Fårö.
clue.se-red-dirt-road-description: Unpaved roads with red soil appear mainly in Dalarna and parts of Kalmar, Norrbotten, and Västerbotten.
clue.se-grey-dirt-road-northern-jamtland: Grey Dirt Roads in Northern Jämtland
Deep grey dirt roads bordered by low green grass are common in northern Jämtland.
clue.se-oland-island-landscape-descripti: Öland is flat; the south is barren with small bushes, the north lusher with larger bushes and trees.
clue.se-birch-row-north-coast-title: Birch Rows Along the North Coast
clue.se-birch-row-north-coast-descriptio: Long rows of thin birch trees line urban streets in northern coastal towns.
clue.se-grey-metal-roof-description: Grey metal roofing on houses becomes more common further north in Sweden.
clue.se-skane-wooden-gable-triangle-titl: Skåne Houses with Wooden Gable Triangles
clue.se-skane-wooden-gable-triangle-desc: Houses in Skåne often have white stone or red brick walls with coloured wooden triangles on gables.
clue.se-half-timbered-house-description: Half-timbered architecture is mainly found in southern Skåne and parts of Halland.
clue.se-red-brick-house-skane-descriptio: Many older single-family homes in Skåne are built from red brick.
clue.se-corrugated-metal-roof-moss-title: Corrugated Metal Roof Panels with Moss
clue.se-corrugated-metal-roof-moss-descr: Square corrugated metal roofs with moss are typical in southern Sweden, especially Skåne and Blekinge.
